senses.sentence_zh: 玉米是单子叶植物，其种子内只有一片子叶。

etymology_story.zh: 该词源于新拉丁语植物学构词，由表示“一个”的 mono- 与 cotyledon“子叶”组成。cotyledon 最终来自希腊语 kotylēdōn，原指杯状凹处等结构，后来用于植物的胚叶。[韦氏词典：monocotyledon](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/monocotyledon)
etymology_story.en: The word ultimately comes from a New Latin botanical formation combining mono-, meaning 'one', with cotyledon, meaning 'seed leaf'. Cotyledon ultimately derives from Greek kotylēdōn, used for a cup-shaped hollow or structure, and later applied to an embryonic leaf.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：mono-（一个）+ cotyledon（子叶）→ monocotyledon。词形及词族：monocotyledons（复数）、monocotyledonous（单子叶的；单子叶植物的）、monocot（常用缩略名词，也可作形容词）、monocots（缩略词复数）、cotyledon（子叶）、cotyledonary（子叶的）。monocotyledon species 中的 monocotyledon 是名词作定语，无须另立常用形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: mono-, one, + cotyledon, seed leaf → monocotyledon. Forms and family members include monocotyledons, the plural; monocotyledonous, having one cotyledon or relating to monocotyledons; monocot, a common shortened noun also used adjectivally; monocots, its plural; cotyledon, an embryonic leaf; and cotyledonary, relating to cotyledons. In monocotyledon species, monocotyledon functions as a noun modifier and does not require a separate common adjective entry.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: monocot（单子叶植物）是现代生物学中常见的简写；monocotyledonous plant（单子叶植物）是展开的描述性表达，两者在此义上没有实质差别。dicotyledon（双子叶植物）是对比概念，不是近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Monocot is the widely used shortened term in modern biology; monocotyledonous plant is the expanded descriptive expression, with no substantive difference in this meaning. Dicotyledon is a contrasting term, not a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: mono-＝一；cotyledon＝子叶：看种子胚中的“一片叶”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Mono- means one: picture one embryonic seed leaf inside the seed.

senses.pos: n. 名词（植物分类学属名）
senses.meaning_zh: 罂粟属，罂粟科的一个植物属
senses.meaning_en: A genus of flowering plants in the poppy family.
senses.english_definition: Papaver is the scientific name of a genus of poppies that includes the common poppy and the opium poppy. [Collins: papaver](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/papaver)

senses.sentence_zh: 虞美人（Papaver rhoeas）属于罂粟属。

etymology_story.zh: Papaver 沿用拉丁语 papaver“罂粟”，在植物分类学中成为正式属名。它本来就是植物名称，不宜将其更早来源解释成未经证实的词根故事。
etymology_story.en: Papaver preserves Latin papaver, meaning 'poppy', as a formal botanical genus name. It was already a plant name in Latin, so its deeper origin should not be replaced with an unsupported root story.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 Papaver 作为整体借入的属名处理，不作有实际构词作用的前后缀拆分；正式属名首字母大写，排版时通常用斜体。相关词族：papaverous（罂粟的，罕用）、papaveraceous（罂粟科的）、Papaveraceae（罂粟科）、papaverine（罂粟碱）；这些词共享拉丁语词干 papaver-，并非都直接由现代英语属名派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Papaver is a borrowed genus name treated as a whole rather than productively divided into prefixes and suffixes; the formal genus name is capitalized and normally italicized. Related family members include papaverous, relating to poppies, rare; papaveraceous, belonging to the poppy family; Papaveraceae, the poppy family; and papaverine, an alkaloid. These share the Latin stem papaver- rather than all being direct derivatives of the modern English genus name.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: poppy genus（罂粟属）是描述性对应表达；poppy（罂粟类植物）是俗名，既可指该属成员，也用于其他属的植物，范围不完全相同；Papaveraceae（罂粟科）是包含罂粟属的科级名称，不是同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Poppy genus is a descriptive equivalent; poppy is a common name used both for members of Papaver and for plants in other genera, so its scope differs; Papaveraceae names the wider family containing Papaver and is not a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Papaver＝罂粟的拉丁属名；把整词与罂粟花及其蒴果联记。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Papaver is the Latin poppy name: connect the whole word with a poppy flower and its seed capsule.

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆。历史构词 prae-（在前）+ sid-（坐）+ -ium → praesidium；联想坐在前排主持事务的集体。

etymology.text: 政治机构名称经俄语 prezidium 进入英语，俄语形式来自拉丁语 praesidium“卫戍队、保护机构”。praesidium 保留了拉丁语式拼写。

usage_note: 正式组织名称可大写。本课指代表较大组织处理事务的执行机构，不指全体会员大会。presidium 更常见。

senses.meaning_zh: 主席团；政府或大型政治组织的常设领导委员会
senses.meaning_en: A standing executive or presiding committee of a government or political organization.
senses.english_definition: A praesidium is a permanent committee that directs the work of a government or large political organization, especially in a communist political system. [Oxford: presidium](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/presidium)

etymology_story.zh: 其现代政治义经俄语 prezidium 传入英语，最终源于拉丁语 praesidium“保护；卫戍队”。praesidium 是 presidium 的另一种拼写，保留了拉丁语式的 ae，现代所指转为主持或领导事务的集体机构。
etymology_story.en: Its modern political meaning entered English through Russian prezidium, ultimately from Latin praesidium, meaning 'protection' or 'garrison'. Praesidium is an alternative spelling of presidium that preserves Latin-style ae, with the modern meaning referring to a collective directing or presiding body.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常作为整体借词处理；复数为 praesidia，也可用 praesidiums。异体拼写及其复数为 presidium、presidia、presidiums；历史上可联系 prae-（在前）与表示“坐”的拉丁语词根，但这不是现代英语中可自由套用的构词公式。同源相关词包括 preside（主持）、president（主席；总统）、presidency（主席或总统的职位、任期）和 presidential（主席的；总统的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats this as a whole borrowed word; plurals are praesidia and, alternatively, praesidiums. The spelling variant presidium has plurals presidia and presidiums. Historically, it can be connected with Latin prae-, before, and a root meaning 'sit', but this is not a freely productive modern English formation. Related cognates include preside, to chair or direct; president, a chairperson or head of state; presidency, the office or term of a president; and presidential, relating to a president.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: presidium 与 praesidium 意义相同，只是拼写不同；executive committee（执行委员会）是较通用的职能称呼，不限定政治体制；governing council（理事会；管理委员会）强调集体治理，其具体权限依组织而定。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Presidium has the same meaning and differs only in spelling; executive committee is a broader functional term without a particular political association; governing council emphasizes collective governance, with powers determined by the organization.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 借历史意象记：坐在前面主持事务的一群人→主席团。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the historical image of people seated at the front to direct proceedings: a presiding committee.

etymology_story.zh: Saran 原是陶氏化学公司在20世纪采用的商标名称，后来也用作相关合成树脂及薄膜材料的名称。Saran Wrap 则成为美国英语中熟悉的保鲜膜品牌名称；品牌名称本身不能保证不同时期产品的化学成分相同。
etymology_story.en: Saran began as a trademark adopted by Dow in the twentieth century and also became a name for the associated synthetic resin and film materials. Saran Wrap became a familiar American food-wrap brand; the brand name does not imply that its products have always had the same chemical composition.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 saran 是不可再作常用词根、词缀分析的商标来源词，通常作不可数名词。常见组合有 Saran Wrap（莎纶保鲜膜）、saran resin（萨冉树脂）和 saran film（萨冉薄膜）；没有常用的直接派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, saran is a trademark-derived word with no productive root-and-affix breakdown and is normally uncountable. Established combinations include Saran Wrap, saran resin, and saran film; it has no common family of direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cling film（保鲜膜，英国英语常用）与 plastic wrap（塑料保鲜膜，美国英语常用）是包装用途上的近义表达；PVDC（聚偏二氯乙烯）是化学材料名称，与传统萨冉树脂有关，但不能与所有 Saran 品牌产品画等号。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cling film is the usual British term, while plastic wrap is common in American English. PVDC names a chemical polymer associated with traditional saran resins, rather than every product carrying the Saran brand.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 商标变材料名：Saran → 树脂薄膜 → 包住食物的保鲜膜。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the brand-to-material link: Saran → resin film → food wrap.

forms: 复数 stoas 或 stoae。
family: Stoic 斯多葛学派的；与哲人在柱廊授课的历史有关。

morphology.text: stoa 作为独立词素记忆。希腊语词干 sto- + -ikos → stoikos，英语借为 Stoic（斯多葛学派的）。

etymology.text: 借自希腊语 stoa“柱廊”。这种有屋顶、前面立柱的长廊，曾是人们散步和讨论的场所。

usage_note: 指古希腊建筑的一类，不是任意带柱子的房间。本课使用普通名词小写 stoa。

senses.meaning_zh: 古希腊柱廊：一侧或多侧有柱列支撑的有顶长廊。
senses.meaning_en: An ancient Greek covered walkway supported by columns.
senses.english_definition: A stoa is a long covered walkway with columns, especially one built in ancient Greece.
senses.collocation_en: the Stoa of Attalos; a colonnaded stoa
senses.collocation_zh: 阿塔罗斯柱廊；有柱列的长廊
senses.sentence_en: People gathered in the stoa to talk and shelter from the sun.
senses.sentence_zh: 人们聚集在柱廊里交谈、遮阳。

senses.meaning_zh: 斯多葛学派：通常写作 the Stoa，指以雅典彩绘柱廊为名的哲学流派。
senses.meaning_en: The Stoic school of philosophy, usually called the Stoa.
senses.english_definition: The Stoa is the school of philosophy whose followers are known as Stoics.
senses.collocation_en: the early Stoa; the philosophy of the Stoa
senses.collocation_zh: 早期斯多葛学派；斯多葛学派的哲学
senses.sentence_en: The early Stoa taught that virtue was sufficient for happiness.
senses.sentence_zh: 早期斯多葛学派认为，美德足以使人幸福。

etymology_story.zh: stoa 借自古希腊语 stoā，意为“柱廊”。芝诺曾在雅典的彩绘柱廊 Stoa Poikilē 讲学，因此该建筑名称又被用来指他的哲学学派。
etymology_story.en: Stoa comes from ancient Greek stoā, meaning a portico or colonnade. Zeno taught in Athens's Stoa Poikilē, or Painted Porch, so the architectural name also came to designate his philosophical school.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 stoa 是整体借入的单纯词，复数为 stoas 或 stoae。Stoic（斯多葛派的；斯多葛派哲学家）、stoical（坚忍的）、stoically（坚忍地）和 stoicism（斯多葛主义；坚忍）属于历史相关词族，不能简单分析为现代英语 stoa 直接加后缀。
morphology_enriched.en: Stoa is a simple borrowed word in modern English; its plurals are stoas and stoae. Stoic, stoical, stoically, and stoicism form a historically related family, rather than straightforward modern derivatives made by adding suffixes to stoa.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: portico（门廊、柱廊）常指建筑入口处的有顶柱式空间；colonnade（柱列、柱廊）强调成排的柱子；stoa 特指古希腊传统中的有顶长廊，常具有公共活动功能。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A portico often forms a covered entrance to a building; a colonnade emphasizes a row of columns. A stoa is specifically an ancient Greek covered walkway, often used as a public gathering place.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先记柱廊，再记柱廊里的哲学课：stoa → the Stoa → Stoic。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture philosophy taught under a colonnade: stoa → the Stoa → Stoic.

meaning: 维尔盖特（英格兰旧土地面积单位）
aliases: 维尔盖特（英格兰旧土地面积单位）

morphology.text: virgate 作为独立词素记忆；virgate（去词尾 e）+ -er → virgater（持有一维尔盖特土地的人）。

etymology.text: 来自中世纪拉丁语 virgata，关联土地计量词 virga；拉丁语 virga 原指杆、杖。从量地的杆子联想到土地单位。

usage_note: 历史土地单位，常说约30英亩，但地区、时期有差异；不宜当作固定的现代公制单位。

senses.meaning_zh: 维尔盖特：英格兰中世纪的一种土地持有或计量单位，通常约为四分之一海德，实际面积因地而异。
senses.meaning_en: A medieval English land unit, conventionally a quarter of a hide, with a locally variable area.
senses.english_definition: A virgate was a unit of land in medieval England whose actual size varied from place to place.
senses.collocation_en: a virgate of land; half a virgate
senses.collocation_zh: 一维尔盖特土地；半维尔盖特土地
senses.sentence_en: The survey recorded that the tenant held a virgate of land.
senses.sentence_zh: 这份土地调查记录表明，该佃户持有一维尔盖特土地。

senses.meaning_zh: 细长杆状的；枝条状的，尤用于植物形态描述。
senses.meaning_en: Long, slender, and rodlike or twiglike, especially in botanical descriptions.
senses.english_definition: A virgate stem or branch is long and slender like a rod or twig.
senses.collocation_en: virgate stems; virgate branches
senses.collocation_zh: 细长杆状的茎；细长枝条
senses.sentence_en: The shrub has slender, virgate branches.
senses.sentence_zh: 这种灌木长有细长的杆状枝条。

etymology_story.zh: 名词 virgate 经中古英语追溯至中世纪拉丁语 virgāta，与拉丁语 virga“杆、杖”和土地丈量有关。形容词则来自拉丁语 virgātus“有枝条的、杆状的”；两种用法共享“杆、枝条”的历史意象，但借入路径不同。
etymology_story.en: The noun virgate came through Middle English from medieval Latin virgāta, connected with Latin virga, a rod or twig, and with land measurement. The adjective comes from Latin virgātus, meaning furnished with twigs or rodlike; the two uses share a historical image but entered English by different routes.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，名词和形容词 virgate 通常都作为整体借词处理，不宜机械拆作 virg + -ate。名词复数为 virgates，历史用语 virgater 指持有一维尔盖特土地的人；形容词没有常用的进一步派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats both the noun and adjective virgate as whole borrowings, rather than productively formed combinations of virg and -ate. The noun has the plural virgates and the historical derivative virgater, a holder of a virgate; the adjective has no common extended family of derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: yardland（土地单位）是名词 virgate 的对应名称；rodlike（杆状的）强调形似直杆，twiglike（枝条状的）强调细长如小枝，后二者对应其形容词义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Yardland is an alternative name for the noun virgate. For the adjective, rodlike emphasizes the shape of a rod, while twiglike emphasizes resemblance to a slender small branch.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一根杆子，两条联想：用杆量地是名词，长得像杆是形容词。
mnemonic_anchor.en: One rod, two links: land measured with a rod, and a plant shaped like a rod.

usage_note: 主要是英国口语，常用 a wodge of，后面可接食物、纸张等；语气比 piece 更随意。

senses.meaning_zh: 一大块；厚厚一沓；一大团，常用于英国英语非正式语境。
senses.meaning_en: A large, thick piece, lump, or bundle; informal British English.
senses.english_definition: A wodge of something is a large, thick piece or amount of it.
senses.collocation_en: a wodge of cash; a wodge of cheese
senses.collocation_zh: 厚厚一沓现金；一大块奶酪
senses.sentence_en: He pulled a thick wodge of notes from his pocket.
senses.sentence_zh: 他从口袋里掏出厚厚一沓钞票。

etymology_story.zh: wodge 在19世纪的英语中已有记载，来源并不完全确定，通常被认为可能是 wedge“楔形块”的变体。现代意义强调东西厚实、成块或成沓，并不要求它具有楔形。
etymology_story.en: Wodge is recorded in nineteenth-century English and has an uncertain origin, often explained as a possible alteration of wedge. Its modern meaning emphasizes thickness or bulk without requiring a wedge shape.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 wodge 是单纯词，复数为 wodges。较少见的形容词 wodgy 可分析为 wodge 去掉词尾 e 后加 -y，表示“厚实的、块状的”；没有庞大的常用派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Wodge is a simple word in modern English, with the plural wodges. The uncommon adjective wodgy is formed by dropping the final e and adding -y, meaning bulky or lumpy; there is no extensive common family of derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chunk（一大块）突出实物块状；wad（一沓、一团）常指纸张、钞票或柔软材料；lump（一团、一块）强调不规则形状。wodge 带有口语中“厚厚一大份”的感觉。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chunk emphasizes a substantial solid piece; wad often refers to paper, banknotes, or soft material; lump suggests an irregular mass. Wodge informally stresses a thick, substantial quantity.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“厚”：厚厚一块奶酪，厚厚一沓钞票，都是 a wodge。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think thick: a thick piece of cheese or a thick bundle of notes is a wodge.

morphology.text: advowson 作为独立词素记忆；advowson + -er → advowsoner（教职提名权持有人）。

etymology.text: 中古英语 advowson 经盎格鲁法语 avoueson，追溯到拉丁语 advocatio，与召来帮助、担任保护者有关。这里保护人的身份发展出教职提名权。

usage_note: 英国教会史、法律史词汇：指向有权任命者提出教职人选的权利，本身不等于最终任命。

sentence: The college held the advowson of the parish.

senses.meaning_zh: 圣职荐举权：在教区圣职出缺时向教会主管提出任职人选的权利。
senses.meaning_en: The right to present a candidate for appointment to a vacant ecclesiastical benefice.
senses.english_definition: An advowson is the right to put forward a person for appointment to a church position when it becomes vacant.
senses.collocation_en: hold the advowson; the advowson of a parish
senses.collocation_zh: 持有圣职荐举权；某教区的圣职荐举权
senses.sentence_en: The family held the advowson of the parish for several generations.
senses.sentence_zh: 这个家族连续几代持有该教区的圣职荐举权。

etymology_story.zh: advowson 经中古英语和盎格鲁法语 avoueson，追溯至拉丁语 advocātiō，其意义涉及援助、辩护或保护。保护教会的赞助人身份逐渐与荐举圣职人选的权利相联系，形成了这一专门含义。
etymology_story.en: Advowson came through Middle English and Anglo-French avoueson from Latin advocātiō, associated with assistance, advocacy, or protection. A patron's protective relationship with a church became linked to the right to present a candidate for its benefice.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 advowson 是整体继承的历史词，不宜拆成现代英语中仍有构词能力的前后缀。复数为 advowsons；罕见历史派生词 advowsoner 指荐举权持有人。advocate（辩护者；拥护）是词源相关词，并非由 advowson 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Advowson is an inherited historical word without a productive modern English prefix-and-suffix analysis. Its plural is advowsons; the rare historical derivative advowsoner denotes a holder of the right. Advocate is etymologically related, rather than directly derived from advowson.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: right of presentation（圣职荐举权）是最贴切的解释性近义表达；patronage（赞助权、保护权）在教会语境中可指这种权利，但范围更广；presentation（荐举）通常指实际提出人选的行为，而不是持有该权利本身。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Right of presentation is the closest explanatory equivalent. Patronage can denote this right in a church context but has a broader range of meanings. Presentation usually names the act of putting forward a candidate, rather than ownership of the right.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 保护教会的赞助人，有权荐举人选：保护关系 → 圣职荐举权。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the church's patron to the right to present its next candidate: protection → presentation.

etymology_story.zh: anuran 由动物分类名称 Anura 加后缀 -an 构成；Anura 源于希腊语表示“无”的 an- 和表示“尾巴”的 oura。这个名称指成体通常无尾，并不表示蝌蚪没有尾巴。
etymology_story.en: Anuran was formed from the zoological name Anura with the suffix -an; Anura combines Greek an-, meaning 'without,' and oura, meaning 'tail.' The name refers to the normally tailless adults, not to their tadpoles.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：Anura（无尾目，去掉词尾 -a）+ -an（属于……的；该类成员）→ anuran，可作名词和形容词。相关词族：anurans（名词复数）；Anura（分类名称）；anurous（无尾的，专业用语）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: Anura, with its final -a removed, + -an ('relating to' or 'a member of') → anuran, used as both a noun and an adjective. Related forms: anurans, the plural noun; Anura, the taxonomic name; and anurous, a technical adjective meaning 'tailless.'

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: frog（蛙）是常用名称，广义上也包括蟾蜍；toad（蟾蜍）通常指某些体形较粗壮、皮肤较疣状的蛙类，并非独立于蛙类的统一分类群；batrachian（蛙类动物；两栖动物）是较旧的术语，范围随语境而异。anuran 的分类范围最明确，专指无尾目成员。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Frog is the everyday term and can include toads in its broad sense; toad usually names certain stockier, often warty frogs rather than a single separate taxonomic group; batrachian is an older term whose scope varies between frog-like animals and amphibians more broadly. Anuran specifically identifies a member of Anura.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: an-＝无，ur-＝尾：记住“成年没有尾巴的蛙类”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: An- means 'without' and ur- means 'tail': picture an adult frog with no tail.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 apatite 借自德语 Apatit，该名称最终源于希腊语 apatan，意为“欺骗”。命名缘由是磷灰石外观多变，曾被误认为其他矿物。
etymology_story.en: English apatite was borrowed from German Apatit, a name ultimately based on Greek apatan, meaning 'to deceive.' The name reflects the mineral's variable appearance, which led to its being mistaken for other minerals.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 apatite 通常作为完整的矿物名称使用；从历史构词看，可分析为 apat-（源于“欺骗”的希腊语词干）+ -ite（矿物名称后缀）。常见词族及复合形式：apatitic（磷灰石的；含磷灰石的）、fluorapatite（氟磷灰石）、chlorapatite（氯磷灰石）、hydroxyapatite（羟基磷灰石，亦称 hydroxylapatite）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, apatite is normally treated as a complete mineral name; historically, it contains apat-, from a Greek stem associated with deception, + the mineral suffix -ite. Established family members and compounds include apatitic ('relating to or containing apatite'), fluorapatite, chlorapatite, and hydroxyapatite, also called hydroxylapatite.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: phosphate mineral（磷酸盐矿物）是上位名称，范围比 apatite 广；phosphorite（磷块岩）是富含磷酸盐、常含磷灰石的岩石；hydroxyapatite（羟基磷灰石）是磷灰石族中的一种。这些相关术语均不能在所有语境中替代 apatite。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Phosphate mineral is a broader category; phosphorite is phosphate-rich rock that commonly contains apatite; hydroxyapatite is a particular member of the apatite group. These related terms are not interchangeable with apatite in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “欺骗”词源＋矿物后缀 -ite：外观容易让人认错的磷灰石。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect the 'deception' origin with mineral-forming -ite: apatite is the mineral whose appearance fooled observers.

etymology_story.zh: babirusa 借自马来语 babi rusa，字面意思是“猪＋鹿”。这个名称将它的猪类体形与雄性弯曲长獠牙令人联想到的鹿角结合起来。
etymology_story.en: Babirusa comes from Malay babi rusa, literally 'pig-deer.' The name combines the animal's pig-like body with the antler-like impression created by the male's long, curved tusks.

morphology_enriched.zh: 英语中是整体借入词，不宜按英语前后缀拆分；源语结构为 babi（猪）+ rusa（鹿）。相关形式：babirusas（常规复数）、babiroussa（异体拼写）；Babyrousa 是鹿豚属的科学名称，与该借词同源。
morphology_enriched.en: This is a whole-word borrowing in English, not an English prefix-and-suffix formation; its source-language structure is babi ('pig') + rusa ('deer'). Related forms include the regular plural babirusas and the spelling variant babiroussa; Babyrousa is the related scientific genus name.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: babiroussa 是同一名称的异体拼写；deer-pig（鹿猪）是对应其字面含义的别称；wild pig（野生猪类）是更宽泛的上位名称，也包括许多其他动物。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Babiroussa is a spelling variant of the same name; deer-pig is an alternative name reflecting its literal meaning; wild pig is a broader category that includes many other animals.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 猪身＋似鹿角的弯獠牙＝“猪鹿”babirusa。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A pig's body plus antler-like curved tusks gives you the 'pig-deer': babirusa.

etymology_story.zh: forestay 由表示“前方”的 fore- 和表示“支撑索”的航海名词 stay 构成，中古英语已有相关形式。这里的“前”指船首方向，而 stay 表示支撑桅杆的索具。
etymology_story.en: Forestay combines fore-, meaning 'towards the front,' with the nautical noun stay, meaning a supporting rope or cable; related forms existed in Middle English. Here, 'front' means the direction of the bow, and stay names rigging that supports a mast.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：fore-（向前；朝船首）+ stay（支索）→ forestay。复数为 forestays；没有常用的独立派生词。相关复合词包括 backstay（后支索）和 headstay（桅前支索），它们与 forestay 共享 stay 这一构词成分。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: fore- ('forward; towards the bow') + stay ('a supporting rope or cable') → forestay. The plural is forestays, and there are no common independent derivatives. Related compounds include backstay and headstay, which share the element stay.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: headstay（桅前支索）在许多帆船语境中与 forestay 通用，但某些索具配置会区分两者；stay（支索）是上位词，也包括后支索等；backstay（后支索）朝船尾方向支撑桅杆，是方向相对的相关词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Headstay is often interchangeable with forestay in sailing usage, although some rigging arrangements distinguish them; stay is the broader term for this kind of mast-supporting rigging; backstay is a related contrasting term for a stay leading aft.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: fore＝船首方向，stay＝支撑索：向前牵住桅杆的索。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Fore points towards the bow, and a stay supports the mast: a forestay holds the mast from the front.

meaning: 可自由切凿的建筑石料

etymology.text: 英语由 free 和 stone 组合；14世纪已用于这种便于切凿的石料。free 在这里提示加工方向较自由，不是“免费”。

usage_note: 建筑、石工语境中的石材名称。另指离核水果或果核，应靠上下文区分。

senses.meaning_zh: 离核果实，尤指离核桃
senses.meaning_en: a stone fruit, especially a peach, whose stone separates easily from its flesh

etymology_story.zh: freestone 由 free 和 stone 组成，中世纪英语时期已用于可沿不同方向自由切凿的建筑石料。后来这一组合也用于离核果实，此时 free 表示果核不与果肉黏连。
etymology_story.en: Freestone combines free and stone and was used in Middle English for building stone that could be worked freely in different directions. The compound was later also applied to fruit whose stone is free from the surrounding flesh.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：free（不受限制的；不黏连的）+ stone（石料；果核）。常用形式与相关组合：freestones（离核果的复数）、freestone peach（离核桃）、freestone masonry（易切凿石料砌体）；freestone 可作名词和形容词，没有常用的直接动词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: free, meaning unrestricted or unattached, + stone, meaning rock or a fruit stone. Common forms and combinations include freestones, freestone peach, and freestone masonry; freestone functions as a noun and adjective and has no commonly used direct verb or adverb derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: building stone（建筑石料）是用途上的上位词，不保证容易切凿；sandstone（砂岩）是按岩石类型命名，许多砂岩可作 freestone，但两者不等同；stone fruit（核果）包括离核果和黏核果，范围比果实义的 freestone 更广。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Building stone is a broader term based on use and does not guarantee easy cutting; sandstone names a rock type, many examples of which qualify as freestone; stone fruit includes both freestone and clingstone fruit and is therefore broader than the fruit sense of freestone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: free + stone：石料能自由切，果核能轻松离。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Free + stone: the building stone cuts freely; the fruit stone comes free.

morphology.text: homoeo-（相似）+ -path（此处指某种疗法的从业者）→ homoeopath（顺势疗法从业者）。

etymology.text: 英语借自德语 Homöopath，很可能由 Homöopathie（顺势疗法）逆构而成。名称关联这套疗法强调的“相似”概念。

usage_note: 英式常保留 oe，美式多写 homeopath。此词说明从事哪种疗法，不说明从业者必然具有医生资格，也不表示疗效已经成立。

senses.meaning_zh: 顺势疗法从业者
senses.meaning_en: a practitioner of homeopathy
senses.english_definition: A homoeopath is someone who practises homeopathy, a system based on the idea that highly diluted substances can treat symptoms resembling those the substances cause.
senses.collocation_en: a practising homoeopath; consult a homoeopath
senses.collocation_zh: 执业的顺势疗法从业者；咨询顺势疗法从业者

etymology_story.zh: homoeopath 通常被认为借自德语 Homöopath，与 Homöopathie（顺势疗法）有关。其希腊语词源成分分别表示“相似”和“病痛”，对应这种疗法所主张的“以类似症状治类似症状”的观念。
etymology_story.en: Homoeopath is generally traced to German Homöopath, associated with Homöopathie, meaning homeopathy. Its Greek elements mean similar and suffering, reflecting the system's principle of treating symptoms with substances believed to produce similar symptoms.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：homoeo-（相似）+ -path（此处表示某种疗法的从业者）。主要词族：homoeopath／homeopath（从业者）、homoeopathy／homeopathy（顺势疗法）、homoeopathic／homeopathic（顺势疗法的）、homoeopathically／homeopathically（以顺势疗法方式）；homeo- 是不带第二个 o 的拼写变体。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: homoeo-, meaning similar, + -path, here meaning a practitioner of a therapeutic system. The principal family comprises homoeopath/homeopath, homoeopathy/homeopathy, homoeopathic/homeopathic, and homoeopathically/homeopathically; homeo- is the alternative spelling without the second o.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: homeopath（顺势疗法从业者）是同一词的另一种拼写，意义相同；practitioner of homeopathy（顺势疗法执业者）是解释性同义表达；alternative practitioner（替代疗法从业者）范围更广，并不专指顺势疗法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Homeopath is an alternative spelling with the same meaning; practitioner of homeopathy is an explanatory equivalent; alternative practitioner is broader and does not specifically identify someone who practises homeopathy.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: homoeo- 表“相似”，-path 指从业者：记住主张“以似治似”的疗法从业者。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Homoeo- means similar: connect the practitioner with the system's principle of like treating like.

pronunciation.note: 按Merriam-Webster的美式读音记号转写为IPA；ˈ标主重音，ˌ标次重音。

etymology.text: 来自已不常用的动词 imprest“借付”，该动词很可能来自意大利语 imprestare。用“事先拨出一笔钱”的场景来记。

senses.meaning_zh: 预付款；预付备用金
senses.meaning_en: money advanced for specified expenses, especially a replenishable expense fund
senses.english_definition: An imprest is money given to someone in advance to meet particular expenses, often through a fund restored to a fixed amount after spending is recorded.

etymology_story.zh: imprest 与早期表示“借付、预付”的动词 imprest 有关，该动词很可能源自意大利语 imprestare，意为“借出”。词义由预先拨付的钱发展为会计中用于指定开支的预付资金或定额备用金。
etymology_story.en: Imprest is associated with an earlier verb imprest, meaning to lend or advance money, probably from Italian imprestare, meaning to lend. Its meaning developed from money advanced beforehand to funds provided for designated expenses, including fixed petty-cash funds.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常将 imprest 视为不可再作能产拆分的借入词，不宜拆成 im- + prest。常用相关组合：imprest fund（预付备用金）、imprest account（备用金账户）、imprest system（定额备用金制度）、imprest holder（备用金保管人）；没有常用的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, imprest is normally treated as an unanalyzed borrowing rather than a productive combination of im- and prest. Common related expressions include imprest fund, imprest account, imprest system, and imprest holder; there are no commonly used direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: advance（预付款）泛指提前支付的钱；petty cash（小额备用现金）强调支付零星开支，未必采用定额补足制度；revolving fund（周转基金）强调资金经补充后反复使用，用途可以比 imprest 更广。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: An advance is any payment made beforehand; petty cash is money for minor expenses and need not operate under a fixed replenishment system; a revolving fund emphasizes repeated use through replenishment and may serve broader purposes than an imprest.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住“先拨一笔钱，用后凭账补足”的备用金场景。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture money advanced first, then restored after the expenses are accounted for.

meaning: 鼓吹对外强硬的沙文主义者
aliases: 鼓吹对外强硬的沙文主义者

pronunciation.note: 按Merriam-Webster的美式读音记号转写为IPA；ˈ标主重音，ˌ标次重音。

forms: 复数 jingoes；另可作感叹词，本课只学名词。
family: jingoism 侵略性沙文主义；jingoish 好战沙文主义的。

morphology.text: jingo 作为独立词素记忆；jingo + -ism → jingoism（侵略性沙文主义）；jingo + -ish → jingoish（好战沙文主义的）。

etymology.text: 名词义源于1877年英国一首鼓吹对俄强硬的歌，其中用了 by jingo 这一感叹语。后来 jingo 用来指鼓吹好战民族主义的人。

usage_note: 带贬义，指支持侵略性、好战政策的人；不是对任何爱国者的中性称呼。

senses.meaning_zh: 鼓吹对外强硬或战争的极端民族主义者
senses.meaning_en: an aggressively nationalistic person who favors a forceful or warlike foreign policy
senses.english_definition: A jingo is someone who expresses extreme national pride and supports threatening or fighting other countries.
senses.collocation_en: a flag-waving jingo; a warmongering jingo
senses.collocation_zh: 挥旗叫嚣的极端民族主义者；鼓吹战争的沙文主义者

senses.english_definition: People sometimes say by jingo in old-fashioned or humorous speech to express surprise or emphasize what they are saying.

senses.collocation_zh: 哎呀！；天哪！
senses.sentence_en: By jingo, you've done it!
senses.sentence_zh: 哎呀，你竟然办到了！

etymology_story.zh: jingo 起初见于 by jingo 这一委婉的感叹或发誓用语，其更早来源并不确定。19世纪70年代末，英国一首支持对俄强硬的流行歌曲反复使用这一表达，使 jingo 获得了“好战民族主义者”的政治含义。
etymology_story.en: Jingo first appeared in by jingo, a mild exclamation or oath whose earlier origin is uncertain. In the late 1870s, a popular British song supporting a forceful stance against Russia used the expression, giving jingo its political meaning of an aggressive nationalist.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词以 jingo 为词基：jingo + -ism → jingoism（好战沙文主义）；jingo + -ist → jingoist（好战沙文主义者）；jingoistic（好战沙文主义的）→ jingoistically（以好战沙文主义方式）；另有较少见的 jingoish（好战沙文主义的）。名词复数为 jingoes 或 jingos；形容词用法存在，但现代通常更常用 jingoistic。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern base is jingo: adding -ism gives jingoism, adding -ist gives jingoist, and the family also includes jingoistic, jingoistically, and the less common jingoish. The noun plural is jingoes or jingos; adjectival jingo exists, although jingoistic is generally more usual today.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chauvinist（沙文主义者）强调对本国或所属群体的盲目优越感，不一定主张战争；warmonger（战争鼓吹者）强调积极推动战争，不一定出于民族主义；ultranationalist（极端民族主义者）强调民族主义立场极端，jingo 则尤其突出对外强硬或好战。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A chauvinist claims blind superiority for a country or group without necessarily advocating war; a warmonger actively promotes war without necessarily being motivated by nationalism; an ultranationalist holds extreme nationalist views, while jingo especially suggests a belligerent foreign-policy stance.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect the song's cry of by jingo with a flag-waving advocate of confrontation abroad.

etymology_story.zh: joinder 借自盎格鲁法语，与意为“连接、联合”的 joindre 有关，最终可追溯至拉丁语 iungere。它在法律英语中专门用于表示把当事人或请求纳入同一诉讼程序。
etymology_story.en: Joinder comes from Anglo-French and is related to joindre, meaning to join, ultimately from Latin iungere. In legal English, it developed a specialized meaning involving the inclusion of parties or claims in a single proceeding.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常将 joinder 作为整体法律词项处理，意义上与 join（连接；加入）相联，词尾不是表示人物的能产后缀 -er。主要派生与相关词：mis- + joinder → misjoinder（不当合并）、non- + joinder → nonjoinder（遗漏应加入的当事人）、joinders（复数）；join、joint、junction 属于相关同源词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats joinder as an established legal word associated in meaning with join; its ending is not the productive agent suffix -er. Principal derivatives and related forms include misjoinder, nonjoinder, and the plural joinders; join, joint, and junction are related cognates.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: joining（加入；连接）是普通用语，缺少 joinder 的专门法律含义；consolidation（并案审理）通常指把已经分别存在的案件合并处理；impleader（第三方引入程序）指在特定程序下把第三方引入诉讼，范围比 joinder 更具体。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Joining is a general word without joinder's specialized legal meaning; consolidation generally combines cases that already exist separately; impleader is a more specific procedure for bringing a third party into litigation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 联想 join：把相关当事人或请求接入同一诉讼。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think join: bring related parties or claims into one proceeding.

morphology.text: 日语 kan（看）+ ban（板）→ kanban（看板）；借入英语后作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 借自日语 kanban“招牌、标示板”。生产线上用卡片发出补货信号，英语便用这个名称指相应的生产管理方式。

usage_note: 本课学制造业中按需求发出补给信号的管理方式；现代任务看板用法与之有关，但不是任何展示板都叫这种生产系统。

senses.meaning_zh: 看板管理法；用可视化信号控制生产或工作流的拉动式管理方法
senses.meaning_en: A visual, demand-driven system for managing production or workflow.
senses.english_definition: Kanban is a system in which visual signals show what work or supplies are needed and help control how much work is in progress.

senses.meaning_zh: 看板卡；用于触发生产、补货或物料移动的信号
senses.meaning_en: A card or other signal authorizing production, replenishment, or material movement.
senses.english_definition: A kanban is a card or electronic signal that tells people when to produce, replace, or move a particular quantity of goods.
senses.collocation_en: a production kanban; a withdrawal kanban
senses.collocation_zh: 生产看板卡；取货看板卡
senses.sentence_en: When the container is empty, its kanban signals that more parts are needed.
senses.sentence_zh: 容器空了以后，其看板卡便发出需要补充零件的信号。

etymology_story.zh: 借自日语 kanban（看板），本义为“招牌、告示牌”。丰田生产体系用卡片传递生产和补货指令，这个名称随后进入英语，并扩展到软件开发等领域的可视化工作流管理。
etymology_story.en: Kanban was borrowed from Japanese kanban, meaning a signboard or noticeboard. Cards used to communicate production and replenishment instructions in the Toyota Production System gave the word its management meaning, which later extended to visual workflow management in fields such as software development.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整体借词，不宜拆成英语词根和词缀；日语来源可分析为 kan（看）＋ban（板）。相关形式包括复数 kanbans（多张看板卡），以及 kanban card（看板卡）、kanban board（看板工作板）、kanban system（看板管理系统）；没有通行的英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, kanban is an unanalyzed loanword rather than an English root-plus-affix formation; its Japanese components are kan and ban, written 看 and 板. Related forms include the plural kanbans and the compounds kanban card, kanban board, and kanban system; there is no established English derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pull system（拉动式系统）强调由下游需求触发工作，是更宽泛的概念；just-in-time production（准时化生产）强调按需及时生产，看板是其实现工具之一；visual management（可视化管理）强调信息的直观呈现，不一定包含拉动机制。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pull system is the broader term for work triggered by downstream demand; just-in-time production emphasizes producing what is needed when it is needed, with kanban serving as one supporting mechanism; visual management emphasizes visible information and does not necessarily involve a pull mechanism.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 看板发信号：需要多少，才补多少；任务流到哪里，板上就显示到哪里。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A signboard sends the signal: replenish what is needed and make the movement of work visible.

senses.meaning_zh: 偷看；探头看；迅速瞥视，主要用于苏格兰及北英格兰方言

etymology_story.zh: 可追溯到中古英语 kiken，意为“看、窥视”，与荷兰语 kijken 等日耳曼语形式有关，但具体传入路径并不完全确定。该词后来主要保留在苏格兰及部分北英格兰方言中，名词义“一瞥”由动词义发展而来。
etymology_story.en: Keek goes back to Middle English kiken, meaning to look or peep, and is connected with Germanic forms such as Dutch kijken, although the precise route is uncertain. It survived chiefly in Scots and some northern English dialects, with the noun meaning a brief look developing from the verb.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词干为 keek，不含可进一步分析的常用英语词缀。动词变化为 keeks、keeked、keeking；名词复数为 keeks；keek＋-er → keeker，指“偷看的人”，在苏格兰用语中也可指“眼睛”。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern base is keek, with no productive internal English affixes. Verb forms are keeks, keeked, and keeking; the noun plural is keeks; keek + -er forms keeker, meaning someone who peeps and, in Scots usage, an eye.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: peek（偷看、瞥看）是较通行的对应词，常暗示短暂或隐蔽地看；peep（窥看）尤其容易使人联想到从小孔或缝隙看；glance（瞥一眼）强调迅速，不必带有偷偷看的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Peek is a widely used equivalent that often suggests a brief or concealed look; peep particularly suggests looking through a small opening; glance emphasizes speed without necessarily suggesting secrecy.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 keek 和 peek 连在一起记：从门缝里探看一眼；这是联想，不是词源拆解。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link keek with peek: a quick look through a gap. This is a memory association, not an etymological breakdown.

usage_note: 比 neat、tidy 少见，可形容头发、外表或被打理过的事物；常见 well-kempt。

etymology_story.zh: 早期 kempt 是中古英语 kemben“梳理”的过去分词，该动词来自古英语 cemban。肯定形式后来衰落，而 unkempt 保留下来；现代 kempt 的重新使用通常被解释为从 unkempt 去掉 un- 的逆构。
etymology_story.en: Earlier kempt was a past participle of Middle English kemben, meaning to comb, from Old English cemban. The positive form declined while unkempt survived, and the modern revival of kempt is generally explained as a back-formation from unkempt.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中可将 kempt 视为整体形容词；un-（不）＋kempt → unkempt（不整洁的），well＋kempt → well-kempt（整洁的、打理妥当的）。相关派生词包括 kemptness（整洁，罕见）和 unkemptness（凌乱、不整洁）；历史上的分词结构已不属于现代能产构词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, kempt functions as a whole adjective: un- + kempt gives unkempt, and well + kempt gives well-kempt. Related derivatives include the rare kemptness and unkemptness; its historical participial structure is no longer a productive modern formation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: neat（整洁的）强调外观有条理、无凌乱；tidy（整齐的）更强调收拾妥当、摆放有序；well-groomed（仪表整洁的）强调头发、胡须、衣着等经过细心打理，与 kempt 描写人的用法最接近。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Neat emphasizes an orderly appearance; tidy particularly suggests that things have been put in order; well-groomed emphasizes careful attention to hair, facial hair, and clothing and is especially close to kempt when describing a person.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从熟悉的 unkempt 去掉表示否定的 un-：不凌乱，就是梳理整洁。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remove the negative un- from unkempt: the untidy appearance becomes combed and orderly.

etymology_story.zh: 来自新拉丁语属名 Lycopodium，由希腊语 lykos“狼”和 podion“小脚”构成，名称取自植物枝叶与兽足的形态联想。英语随后也用该词指这些植物的细小孢子所制成的粉末。
etymology_story.en: Lycopodium comes from the New Latin genus name Lycopodium, formed from Greek lykos, meaning wolf, and podion, meaning little foot, in reference to the plant's appearance. English also extended the name to the fine powder consisting of spores from these plants.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是学术借词，可按古典构词成分理解为 lyco-（狼）＋pod-（脚）＋-ium（拉丁化名词词尾）；更准确的历史来源是 lykos＋podion。相关词有 lycopod（石松类植物）、Lycopodiaceae（石松科）及 lycopodiaceous（石松科的）；这些词共享古典词干，并非都由现代英语 lycopodium 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: This learned borrowing can be interpreted through the classical elements lyco- meaning wolf, pod- meaning foot, and the Latinized noun ending -ium; historically, its components are more precisely lykos and podion. Related words include lycopod, Lycopodiaceae, and lycopodiaceous; they share a classical stem rather than all being direct modern English derivatives of lycopodium.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: club moss（石松类植物）是较宽泛的通称，不能在所有分类语境中与石松属完全等同；ground pine（地松）是某些石松类植物的俗名，并非真正的松树；lycopodium powder（石松粉）仅对应孢子粉义，不指整株植物。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Club moss is a broader common name and is not always taxonomically identical to the genus Lycopodium; ground pine is a common name for certain club mosses, which are not true pines; lycopodium powder corresponds only to the spore-powder sense, not to the whole plant.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: lyco- 是狼，pod- 是脚：先想“狼的小脚”般的枝叶，再连到植物及其孢子粉。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Lyco- is wolf and pod- is foot: picture little wolf-like feet, then connect the plant with its spore powder.

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语中的相关形式来自地中海罗曼语航海词汇，最终可追溯到拉丁语 medianus“中间的”。这个原本与“中间”有关的名称，在不同船帆布局和航海传统中发生了位置意义的变化，英语现代用法指向后桅及其帆具。
etymology_story.en: The Middle English forms came from Mediterranean Romance nautical vocabulary and ultimately trace back to Latin medianus, meaning middle. As sail arrangements and nautical traditions changed, the positional meaning shifted, and modern English uses the word for the mizzenmast and its sails or equipment.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 mizzen 是不可再作常用词缀拆解的词干；名词复数为 mizzens。主要复合词包括 mizzen＋mast → mizzenmast（后桅）、mizzen＋sail → mizzensail（后桅帆）、mizzen topsail（后桅上帆）及 mizzen staysail（后桅支索帆）；mizen 是拼写变体。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, mizzen is a base without a productive internal affix analysis; its noun plural is mizzens. Principal compounds include mizzen + mast → mizzenmast, mizzen + sail → mizzensail, mizzen topsail, and mizzen staysail; mizen is a spelling variant.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: mizzensail（后桅帆）明确指帆，对应 mizzen 的帆义；mizzenmast（后桅）明确指桅杆，对应其桅杆义；aft sail（后部的帆）只是较宽泛的描述，未必属于后桅。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mizzensail explicitly names the sail and matches the sail sense of mizzen; mizzenmast explicitly names the mast and matches its mast sense; aft sail is only a broader description of a sail toward the stern and need not identify a mizzen sail.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 词源里的“中间”留给历史；现代定位记“主桅后面”：mizzen 可指那里的桅、帆及相关帆具。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep middle as the historical clue; locate the modern word behind the mainmast, where mizzen names the mast, its sail, and related equipment.

etymology_story.zh: 该词于16世纪初进入英语，最早见于苏格兰用法，借自法语 paillasse；其来源与表示“稻草”的法语 paille 和拉丁语 palea 有关。词义直接来自传统做法：把稻草装进布袋，制成床垫。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English in the early sixteenth century, initially in Scots usage, from French paillasse, ultimately connected with Latin palea, meaning straw. Its meaning reflects the practice of stuffing a cloth sack with straw to make a mattress. [Oxford](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/english/palliasse)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中视为整体借词，不宜按英语词根和词缀强行拆分；法语来源可分析为 paille（稻草）+ -asse（名词后缀）。复数为 palliasses；异体拼写为 paillasse，复数 paillasses。没有常用的英语派生词；表示简陋床铺的 pallet 与其有历史词源联系，并非其派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, palliasse is an unanalyzed loanword; its French source can be analyzed as paille, meaning straw, plus the noun-forming suffix -asse. The plural is palliasses; the alternative spelling is paillasse, plural paillasses. There are no common English derivatives; pallet in its bedding sense is historically related rather than derived from palliasse.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: straw mattress（草填床垫）是最直接的释义性近义表达；pallet（简陋床铺）强调床铺简单或临时搭设，不一定填草；mattress（床垫）是上位词，不限定填充材料。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Straw mattress is the closest descriptive equivalent; pallet emphasizes a simple or makeshift bed without necessarily specifying straw; mattress is the broader term and does not specify the filling.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: paille 是“稻草”：草装进布袋，就成了 palliasse。
mnemonic_anchor.en: French paille means straw: put straw inside a sack, and you have a palliasse.

morphology.text: pardon（赦免）+ -er（执行某行为的人）→ pardoner（赎罪券募款传教士）。

etymology.text: 英语在 pardon 后加表示人的 -er，14世纪已有用例。pardon 经中古英语、古法语追溯到晚期拉丁语 perdonare“宽恕”。记住这个人与赦罪活动的联系。

etymology_story.zh: 该词在14世纪的中古英语中已有记载，其历史来源涉及表示相关行为者的盎格鲁法语形式；现代英语中可以清楚地理解为 pardon（赦免）加 -er（行为者）。其历史专义指通过授予大赦为宗教事业募款的人，普通义则是“宽恕者或赦免者”。
etymology_story.en: Recorded in Middle English in the fourteenth century, pardoner has Anglo-French antecedents and is transparently associated in modern English with pardon plus the agent suffix -er. Its historical sense concerns religious fundraising through indulgences, while its general sense means someone who pardons. [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/pardoner); [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/pardoner)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词公式：pardon（宽恕；赦免）+ -er（行为者）→ pardoner；复数 pardoners。词族包括 pardon（名词、动词），pardoned（过去式、过去分词），pardoning（现在分词），pardonable（可宽恕的），pardonably（可以谅解地），pardonability（可宽恕性），unpardonable（不可宽恕的），unpardonably（不可原谅地），unpardonability（不可宽恕性）；pardonee 指获赦者，较少用。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: pardon, meaning forgive or grant a pardon, + agentive -er → pardoner; plural pardoners. The family includes pardon as a noun and verb, pardoned, pardoning, pardonable, pardonably, pardonability, unpardonable, unpardonably, and unpardonability. The less common pardonee denotes the recipient of a pardon.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: indulgence seller（赎罪券售卖者）对应历史专义，突出售卖活动；forgiver（宽恕者）对应普通义，侧重个人谅解；absolver（赦罪者）侧重宣告某人免除罪责，常带宗教意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Indulgence seller matches the historical sense and emphasizes selling; forgiver matches the general sense and emphasizes personal forgiveness; absolver emphasizes releasing someone from guilt, often in a religious context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: pardon 是“赦免”，-er 是“人”：提供赦免的人；放进中世纪背景，就是赎罪券募款者。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pardon means forgiveness, and -er marks a person: someone who pardons; in a medieval setting, connect this with indulgences.

etymology_story.zh: 该词于19世纪经法语 phényle 进入英语；其中 phen- 与苯相关的早期命名及希腊语“发光”有关，背景是苯与照明用煤气的历史联系。后缀 -yl 经法语 -yle 追溯到希腊语 hylē“木材；物质”，后来用于化学基团名称。
etymology_story.en: Phenyl entered English in the nineteenth century through French phényle; phen- belongs to early benzene terminology ultimately associated with Greek words for shining and the historical connection with illuminating gas. The suffix -yl, through French -yle, ultimately comes from Greek hylē, meaning wood or matter, and became a chemical group suffix. [Etymonline](https://www.etymonline.com/word/phenyl); [Académie française](https://www.dictionnaire-academie.fr/article/A9P1963)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代分析：phen-（苯相关的化学词干）+ -yl（基团后缀）→ phenyl（苯基）。直接相关形式有 phenylic（苯基的）、phenylation（苯基化）、phenylate（使苯基化）及其变化形式 phenylated、phenylating；构词组合包括 diphenyl（二苯基；亦用于联苯的旧称）、biphenyl（联苯）、triphenyl-（三苯基）、phenylalanine（苯丙氨酸）和 phenylethyl-（苯乙基）。phenol（苯酚）是相关命名词族成员；化学复合名称可继续生成，不能穷尽。部分词典把名词前的 phenyl 分析为名词定语，另一些词典列为形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: phen-, a benzene-related chemical stem, + -yl, a group suffix → phenyl. Directly related forms include phenylic, phenylation, phenylate, phenylated, and phenylating; combinations include diphenyl, biphenyl, triphenyl-, phenylalanine, and phenylethyl-. Phenol belongs to the related naming family; chemical compounds form an open-ended set. Dictionaries differ in treating prenominal phenyl as an attributive noun or an adjective. [Cambridge](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/phenyl)

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: phenyl group（苯基）是明确的同义表达；phenyl radical 在旧式命名中也可指苯基，但现代自由基语境中的 C₆H₅· 特指带未成对电子的物种；aryl group（芳基）是上位概念，苯基只是其中一种。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Phenyl group is an explicit equivalent. Phenyl radical can denote the group in older terminology, but in modern free-radical contexts C₆H₅· specifically denotes a species with an unpaired electron. Aryl group is broader: phenyl is one kind of aryl group.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 苯环少一个氢，空出一个连接位：C₆H₆ → C₆H₅—，就是 phenyl。
mnemonic_anchor.en: One less hydrogen on benzene leaves an attachment point: C₆H₆ → C₆H₅—, the phenyl group.

etymology_story.zh: pluton 在20世纪进入地质学词汇，很可能由 plutonic“深成的”去掉 -ic 逆构而来。plutonic 源于冥界之神 Pluto 的名字，以地下冥界的形象指代地球内部形成岩石的环境。
etymology_story.en: Pluton entered geological vocabulary in the twentieth century, probably as a back-formation from plutonic by removing -ic. Plutonic derives from the name Pluto, the god of the underworld, connecting underground rock formation with his subterranean realm. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/pluton); [Dictionary.com](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/plutonic)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可用 pluton + -ic → plutonic（深成的）理解词形关系，但历史形成方向很可能相反，即 plutonic − -ic → pluton。复数为 plutons；相关词族有 plutonic、plutonism（深成作用；历史上的火成论）和 plutonist（火成论者）。Pluto 是历史命名来源，不是现代英语中表示岩体的普通词根。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern relationship can be represented as pluton + -ic → plutonic, although the historical direction was probably the reverse: plutonic minus -ic → pluton. The plural is plutons; the related family includes plutonic, plutonism, and plutonist. Pluto is the historical naming source rather than an ordinary modern English root meaning a rock body.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: intrusive body（侵入岩体）是较宽泛的近义表达；batholith（岩基）指规模很大的深成岩体；stock（岩株）通常指规模较小的深成侵入岩体。后两者是具体类型，并非在所有语境下都能替换 pluton。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Intrusive body is a broader near-equivalent; batholith denotes a very large plutonic body; stock generally denotes a smaller plutonic intrusion. The latter two are specific types rather than universally interchangeable synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Pluto 掌管地下冥界：在地下凝固成形的岩体，就是 pluton。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pluto rules the underworld: picture magma solidifying underground into a pluton.

etymology_story.zh: 该词于18世纪初借自法语 rissole，经古法语方言形式追溯到晚期拉丁语 russeolus“微红的”，后者来自拉丁语 russus“红色的”。名称与煎炸后表面变色的形象相联系，而现代各地所指的食物可有裹面包屑、包酥皮或不包外皮等差异。
etymology_story.en: Borrowed from French in the early eighteenth century, rissole ultimately traces through an Old French dialect form to Late Latin russeolus, meaning reddish, from Latin russus, meaning red. The name evokes the color developed during frying, while modern regional versions differ in their coatings and pastry coverings. [Oxford](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/us/definition/english/rissole); [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/rissole)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整体借词，没有可用于普通英语分析的活跃词根与词缀；复数为 rissoles。相关烹饪借词 rissolé 或 rissolé 作形容词，表示“煎炸至棕黄色的”，尤其用于土豆，来自法语动词 rissoler 的过去分词；rissoler 是法语词，不宜列作常用英语动词。rissole 本身没有其他常用英语派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, rissole is an unanalyzed loanword with no productive internal English affixes; its plural is rissoles. The related culinary borrowing rissolé is an adjective meaning browned in fat, especially of potatoes, and comes from the past participle of French rissoler. Rissoler is a French verb rather than a common English verb; rissole itself has no other common English derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Croquette is a close equivalent and usually has a breadcrumb coating; patty emphasizes a flattened shape without specifying coating or cooking method; turnover resembles the pastry-covered version but is defined by folded pastry and may be baked.

etymology_story.zh: 借自现代希伯来语 ṣābār，指仙人掌及其果实。这个称呼以果实外部多刺、内部甜软的特点，比喻土生以色列人外表强硬、内心温厚的传统形象。

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可再作有用拆分的借词：sabra；规则复数为 sabras。没有常用的固定派生词族；sabrahood 是偶见的创造性构词，不能视为常用标准派生词；sabra culture 等属于名词作定语。

It has no established common derivative family: sabrahood is an occasional creative formation rather than a standard common derivative, and phrases such as sabra culture use the noun attributively.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: native-born Israeli（土生以色列人）是最接近的释义，但 sabra 的传统用法尤其关联犹太以色列人；Israeli（以色列人）范围更广，也包括出生在国外的人。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Native-born Israeli is the closest equivalent, although sabra traditionally has a particular association with Jewish Israelis. Israeli is broader and also includes people born abroad.

senses.meaning_zh: 平和；安宁，尤用于印度宗教或文学语境
senses.meaning_en: Peace or tranquility, especially in Indian religious or literary contexts.
senses.english_definition: Shantih is a state of peace or tranquility, especially as expressed in an Indian religious invocation.
senses.collocation_en: the invocation of shantih; the repetition of shantih
senses.collocation_zh: 祈愿安宁；反复诵念“平和”
senses.sentence_en: The repeated word shantih expresses a wish for peace.
senses.sentence_zh: 反复出现的 shantih 一词表达了对安宁的祈愿。

etymology_story.zh: 源自梵语 śānti“平和、安宁”，与表示“平息、安静”的词根 śam 有关；拼写末尾的 h 对应梵语形式 śāntiḥ 的送气音符号。艾略特《荒原》结尾的三次重复，使这一拼写在英语文学中尤为人熟知。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Sanskrit śānti, meaning peace or tranquility, and is related to the root śam, meaning to become calm; the final h represents the visarga in the Sanskrit form śāntiḥ. Eliot's threefold repetition at the end of The Waste Land made this spelling particularly familiar in English literature.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 shantih 作为完整借词记忆，不按英语词根和词缀拆分；shanti 是另一常见转写。梵语来源可联系 śam（平息）和名词构形成分 -ti，但这不是英语中的能产构词公式；该词通常不可数，没有常用英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, shantih is a whole borrowed word rather than a combination of English roots and affixes; shanti is another common transliteration. Its Sanskrit formation connects śam, meaning to become calm, with the noun-forming element -ti, but this is not a productive English formation; the word is normally uncountable and has no common English derivative family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: peace（平和）范围最广；tranquility（宁静）侧重不受扰动的平静状态；serenity（安详）侧重心境平稳。shantih 额外带有梵语祈愿和宗教文学色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Peace is the broadest term; tranquility emphasizes freedom from disturbance; serenity emphasizes a calm, composed state of mind. Shantih additionally carries the associations of Sanskrit invocation and religious literature.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 shantih 想成一声祈愿：愿纷扰平息，愿内心安宁。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hear shantih as a quiet invocation: let disturbance settle and peace remain.

meaning: 德军战俘营（两次世界大战期间）

morphology.text: 德语 Stamm（基础、主干）+ Lager（营地）→ Stammlager；再取 Sta- + -lag → stalag（缩合成的战俘营名称）。

etymology.text: 英语借自德语 Stalag，它是 Stammlager 的缩短形式。由“主营地”的德语名称，记住战争史中的战俘营。

usage_note: 主要用于一战、二战的德国战俘营，尤其关押敌方士兵、士官；不要当作集中营的一般同义词。

senses.meaning_zh: 德国战俘营，尤指第二次世界大战期间关押士兵和士官的营地
senses.meaning_en: A German prisoner-of-war camp, especially one for enlisted personnel in the Second World War.
senses.english_definition: A stalag was a German camp where prisoners of war, especially soldiers below commissioned-officer rank, were held.
senses.collocation_en: escape from a stalag; prisoners in a stalag
senses.collocation_zh: 从德军战俘营逃脱；德军战俘营中的战俘
senses.sentence_en: He spent the final year of the war in a stalag.
senses.sentence_zh: 战争的最后一年，他被关押在一座德军战俘营里。

etymology_story.zh: 借自德语 Stalag，是 Stammlager“主营地、基本营地”的缩略形式，也用于更完整的名称 Mannschaftsstammlager。这个行政名称在英语中成为德国战俘营的历史专称，尤与第二次世界大战有关。
etymology_story.en: The word was borrowed from German Stalag, an abbreviation of Stammlager, meaning main or base camp, also used within the fuller designation Mannschaftsstammlager. In English, the administrative label became a historical term for a German prisoner-of-war camp, especially during the Second World War.

morphology_enriched.zh: 来源构词为德语 Stamm（主干、基础）+ Lager（营地）→ Stammlager，再缩略为 Sta- + -lag → Stalag。现代英语中是完整借词，规则复数为 stalags；没有常用的固定派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Its source formation is German Stamm, meaning stem or base, + Lager, meaning camp, producing Stammlager, then abbreviated as Sta- + -lag → Stalag. Modern English treats it as a whole borrowed noun, with the regular plural stalags and no established common derivative family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: prisoner-of-war camp／POW camp（战俘营）是不限国家的通称；prison camp（囚禁营）范围更广；internment camp（拘禁营）常用于被拘禁的平民，不能与 stalag 完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Prisoner-of-war camp, or POW camp, is the general term without a national restriction; prison camp is broader. Internment camp often refers to the detention of civilians and is not fully interchangeable with stalag.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Sta(m m) + Lag(er)：从“主营地”的德语缩写，联想到德国战俘营。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sta- from Stamm + -lag from Lager: a shortened German camp name becomes a German POW camp.

morphology.text: swan（天鹅）+ -s-（来自所有格的连接成分）+ down（绒羽）→ swansdown（天鹅的细绒）。

etymology.text: 17世纪英语中由 swan 的所有格与 down“绒羽”连写形成。这里 down 不是“向下”，而是柔软的羽绒。

usage_note: 本课指天鹅的细绒，可用于服饰饰边。也有同名织物；若语境说 cotton、cloth，则未必是真羽绒。

etymology_story.zh: 由 swan 的所有格形式与 down“绒羽”结合而成，字面意思是“天鹅的绒羽”。后来因触感相似，也用于指表面柔软蓬松的起绒织物。
etymology_story.en: The word combines the possessive form of swan with down, meaning soft feathers, and literally means a swan's down. It was later applied to fabrics with a similarly soft, fleecy surface.

morphology_enriched.zh: swan（天鹅）+ 所有格 -'s + down（绒羽）→ swansdown，合写后不保留撇号；也可见拼写 swan's-down。down 在此是名词“绒羽”，不是副词“向下”；swansdown 通常不可数，没有常用派生词族，swansdown collar 等属于名词作定语。
morphology_enriched.en: Swan + possessive -'s + down → swansdown, with the apostrophe omitted in the closed compound; the spelling swan's-down also occurs. Down here is the noun meaning soft feathers, not the adverb meaning toward a lower place; swansdown is normally uncountable, has no common derivative family, and functions attributively in phrases such as swansdown collar.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: down（绒羽）是不限鸟类的上位词；eiderdown（绒鸭绒）来自绒鸭，来源不同；flannel（法兰绒）是触感相近的起绒织物，但不能泛指天鹅绒羽，也不一定与 swansdown 织物相同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Down is the broader term for soft feathers from various birds; eiderdown comes specifically from eider ducks. Flannel is a related soft, napped fabric, but it does not mean swan feathers and is not necessarily identical to swansdown fabric.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: swan 的 down：天鹅身上的软绒 → 像这种软绒的织物。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A swan's down: soft feathers first, then fabric with the same soft feel.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 tugrik 经俄语 tugrik 借入，最终源自蒙古语 tögrög，其较早形式常转写为 tögörig，含有“圆、圆形物”的意思。这一名称把圆形钱币与货币单位联系起来。
etymology_story.en: English tugrik came through Russian tugrik from Mongolian tögrög, whose earlier form is often transliterated tögörig and carries the sense of round or a round object. The name connects the shape of a coin with a monetary unit.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是完整借词 tugrik，不宜拆成英语词根与后缀；规则复数为 tugriks。togrog、tögrög 是同一货币名称的其他转写形式；tugrik-denominated（以图格里克计价的）是复合形容词，不是该词的固定派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats tugrik as a whole borrowing rather than an English root-and-affix construction; its regular plural is tugriks. Togrog and tögrög are alternative renderings of the same currency name; tugrik-denominated is a compound adjective rather than an established derivative of tugrik.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: togrog 和 tögrög 是同一蒙古货币名称的不同转写，并非不同币种；Mongolian currency（蒙古货币）是较宽泛的描述，可指整个货币体系或其现金。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Togrog and tögrög are alternative renderings of the same Mongolian currency name, not different currencies. Mongolian currency is a broader description that can refer to the monetary system or its cash.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 蒙古语“圆” → 圆形钱币 → 蒙古货币图格里克。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Mongolian round → a round coin → Mongolia's tugrik.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜整体识记：yellow 部分透明，-hammer 在此不是表示工具的独立构词成分。复数为 yellowhammers；yellowhammer-like 表示“像黄鹀的”，是可临时构成的表达，并非固定派生词；没有常用的其他词性派生形式。考试归属及 CEFR 等级未核定，因此 exam_tags 留空。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat the modern word as a lexical whole: yellow is transparent, but -hammer is not a separate tool-denoting component here. The plural is yellowhammers; yellowhammer-like means resembling a yellowhammer and is a possible occasional formation rather than an established derivative. No other common POS derivatives are established. Exam coverage and a CEFR level are unverified, so exam_tags is empty.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: yellow bunting（黄鹀）是欧亚鸟类义的同义名称；bunting（鹀）是更广的类称；yellow-shafted flicker（黄翅扑动鴷）只对应北美地区义，不能替换欧亚鸟类义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Yellow bunting is an alternative name for the Eurasian species; bunting is a broader category; yellow-shafted flicker matches only the regional North American sense.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先抓 yellow“黄色”：欧洲是黄色鸣禽，北美是翅羽带黄色的啄木鸟。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor both senses in yellow: a yellow songbird in Eurasia, a yellow-winged woodpecker in North America.

morphology_enriched.en: Yeuk is a modern simple base used as both noun and verb; yuke is an alternative spelling. Verb forms are yeuks, yeuked, and yeuking; the noun plural is yeuks. Yeuk + -y produces yeuky, meaning itchy, also spelled yuky; these forms are regional. [Derivative](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/yeuky) Exam coverage and a CEFR level are unverified, so exam_tags is empty.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: itch（痒；发痒）是通用英语中的直接对应词；tickle（痒感；使发痒）常指轻微接触造成的感觉；prickle（刺痒；感到刺痛）强调细小针刺般的刺激。yeuk 的区别主要在苏格兰地域色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Itch is the direct general-English equivalent; tickle often suggests a sensation caused by light contact; prickle emphasizes tiny stabbing sensations. Yeuk is distinguished chiefly by its Scottish regional character.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 yeuk 与 itch 成对记：同一种痒，苏格兰有另一种说法。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pair yeuk with itch: the same urge to scratch, expressed through a Scottish word.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借入意大利语 arioso，原意为“像歌曲的”，由 aria“曲调；咏叹调”的词干加 -oso 构成。这个表示歌唱性风格的词，也成为相应唱段的名称。[词源与三种词性依据](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/arioso)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Italian arioso, meaning songlike, formed from the stem of aria, meaning tune or aria, with -oso. The term for a singing style also became a name for a passage in that style. [Etymology and three parts of speech](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/arioso)

morphology_enriched.zh: 英语中作为完整借词使用，名词、形容词和副词同形；意大利语内部结构为 ari-（aria 的词干）+ -oso“具有……特点的”。名词复数为 ariosos 或 ariosi；相关借词有 aria“咏叹调”和 arietta“小咏叹调”，它们不是由英语 arioso 再派生而来。考试归属及 CEFR 等级未核定，因此 exam_tags 留空。
morphology_enriched.en: English uses the whole borrowed form unchanged as noun, adjective, and adverb; its Italian structure is ari-, the stem of aria, + -oso, meaning characterized by. Noun plurals are ariosos and ariosi. Related loans include aria and arietta, a short aria; neither is an English derivative of arioso. Exam coverage and a CEFR level are unverified, so exam_tags is empty.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: songlike（歌唱般的）是形容词和副词义的通俗释义；cantabile（如歌的／如歌地）同样强调流畅歌唱性，但不专指介于两种声乐形式之间的风格；aria（咏叹调）通常具有更完整、独立的结构，不与 arioso 完全同义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Songlike is a plain-language equivalent for the descriptive uses; cantabile likewise emphasizes smooth singing quality without specifically naming an intermediate vocal style; aria usually has a more fully developed, independent structure and is not an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: aria 是咏叹调，arioso 就是“带着 aria 的歌唱性”：既可指风格，也可指唱段。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with aria: arioso has an aria's singing quality, naming either the manner or the passage.

etymology_story.zh: barbet 与法语 barbe“胡须”有关，最终可追溯至拉丁语表示胡须或有胡须的词形；鸟名呼应喙基部的须状羽毛。犬名同样呼应口鼻部的须毛，英语中常写作 Barbet。[鸟名词源](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/barbet)；[犬种依据](https://www.akc.org/dog-breeds/barbet/)
etymology_story.en: Barbet is connected with French barbe, meaning beard, ultimately from Latin forms referring to a beard or being bearded; the bird name evokes its bill bristles. morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是完整借词，不宜拆成英语 bar + bet；法语构词可联系 barbe“胡须”与后缀 -et。两义复数均为 barbets；没有常用的英语派生词族。coppersmith barbet“赤胸拟啄木鸟”和 crested barbet“冠拟啄木鸟”是鸟名组合，不是词性派生。考试归属及 CEFR 等级未核定，因此 exam_tags 留空。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English this is a whole-word loan, not English bar + bet; its French formation connects barbe, meaning beard, with -et. Both senses have the plural barbets, and there is no common English derivative family. Coppersmith barbet and crested barbet are compound bird names rather than POS derivatives. Exam coverage and a CEFR level are unverified, so exam_tags is empty.

etymology_story.zh: burthen 是 burden 的古旧形式，可追溯至古英语 byrþen“负载”，与 beran“携带、承受”有关。由具体承载的重物，词义扩展到责任、忧虑及船舶载货容量。[古旧形式与词性](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/burthen)；[词源及相关义项](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/burden)
etymology_story.en: Burthen is an archaic form of burden, traceable to Old English byrþen, meaning a load, and related to beran, meaning to carry or bear. The physical load developed into meanings involving responsibility, worry, and a ship's carrying capacity. [Archaic form and parts of speech](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/burthen); [etymology and related senses](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/burden)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代识记以 burthen 为完整词干，不把 -en 当作现行后缀。名词复数及动词第三人称单数为 burthens；过去式及过去分词为 burthened，现在分词为 burthening。burthen + -some → burthensome“繁重的”；un- + burthen → unburthen“卸下重担；倾诉”，均属古旧形式；现代对应词族为 burden、burdened、burdening、burdensome、unburden。考试归属及 CEFR 等级未核定，因此 exam_tags 留空。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat burthen as a complete modern stem rather than analyzing -en as a current suffix. Burthens is the noun plural and third-person singular verb; burthened is the past tense and participle; burthening is the present participle. Burthen + -some gives burthensome, meaning onerous; un- + burthen gives unburthen, meaning relieve of a load or disclose troubles. These are archaic; modern counterparts are burden, burdened, burdening, burdensome, and unburden. Exam coverage and a CEFR level are unverified, so exam_tags is empty.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: burden（负担；使负担）是现代通用对应词；load（负载；装载）更偏具体重量或工作量；encumber（使受累；妨碍）只对应动词义，强调负担限制行动。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Burden is the ordinary modern equivalent as both noun and verb; load more readily emphasizes physical weight or an amount of work; encumber matches the verb sense and stresses restricted movement or action.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 burthen 连到 bear“承受”：肩上承重，心里承忧；现代通常写 burden。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect burthen with bear: weight borne on the shoulders, worry borne in the mind; modern English normally uses burden.

etymology_story.zh: 该词是近代医学利用希腊语构词成分创造的术语：kardia 意为“心脏”，-graph 源于表示“书写、记录”的希腊语词族。它最初用于描记心脏机械活动的仪器，后来也用于指记录心脏电活动的仪器。
etymology_story.en: This modern medical term combines Greek kardia, meaning 'heart', with -graph, from the Greek word family for writing or recording. It was initially used for instruments recording the heart's mechanical activity and was later also applied to instruments recording its electrical activity.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：cardi(o)-（心脏）+ -graph（记录仪器）。主要词族：cardiographs（复数）、cardiography（心动描记法）、cardiographic（心动描记的）、cardiographically（以心动描记方式）、cardiogram（心动描记图）；加 electro- 可形成 electrocardiograph（心电图仪）、electrocardiography（心电描记法）、electrocardiographic（心电描记的）和 electrocardiogram（心电图）。注意 -graph 指仪器，-gram 指记录结果。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: cardi(o)- 'heart' + -graph 'recording instrument'. Principal family members include cardiographs, cardiography, cardiographic, cardiographically, and cardiogram. Adding electro- produces electrocardiograph, electrocardiography, electrocardiographic, and electrocardiogram. The ending -graph identifies the instrument, whereas -gram identifies the resulting record.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: electrocardiograph（心电图仪）专门记录心脏电活动；ECG machine（心电图机）是 electrocardiograph 的常用表达；heart monitor（心脏监护仪）强调持续监测，未必专指描记仪器。cardiograph 的含义较宽，cardiogram 则指记录图，不能与仪器名称混用。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: An electrocardiograph specifically records the heart's electrical activity; ECG machine is its everyday equivalent; a heart monitor emphasizes ongoing observation and does not necessarily identify a particular recording instrument. Cardiograph is broader, while cardiogram names the record rather than the machine.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cardio 是“心”，graph 是“记录”：把心脏活动描记下来的是仪器 cardiograph，留下的图是 cardiogram。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Cardio means 'heart' and graph means 'record': the cardiograph records heart activity, and the cardiogram is the resulting record.

etymology_story.zh: descale 是英语用表示“去除”的 de- 加上 scale 构成的动词；此前缀最终源自拉丁语。scale 在这里指覆盖表面的鳞片或硬质薄层，因此该词既可指除水垢、氧化皮，也可指去鱼鳞。
etymology_story.en: Descale was formed in English by adding the removal prefix de-, ultimately from Latin, to scale. Here scale means a covering of flakes or a hard surface layer, which accounts for its uses involving limescale, metal oxides, and fish scales.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：de-（去除）+ scale（鳞片；垢层）。主要词族：descales（第三人称单数）、descaled（过去式及过去分词）、descaling（现在分词，也可作名词，表示除垢过程）、descaler（除垢剂；除垢工具或设备）。相关基础词有 scale（鳞片；垢层，也可作动词表示去鳞）、scaled（有鳞的；已去鳞的，视语境而定）、scaly（多鳞的；鳞片状的）和 scaliness（鳞片状状态）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: de- 'remove' + scale 'a flake or hard surface layer'. Principal forms are descales, descaled, descaling, and descaler, meaning a substance, tool, or machine used for removing scale. Related base-family words include scale, which can also mean 'remove scales' as a verb, scaled, scaly, and scaliness; scaled can mean either covered with scales or having had scales removed, depending on context.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: decalcify（去钙；除钙垢）专指清除钙质沉积；pickle（酸洗）在金属加工中指用酸处理表面，是除氧化皮的一种方法；scale（给鱼去鳞）在烹饪语境中与 descale 接近。descale 强调去掉表面的鳞片或垢层，不限定清除方法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Decalcify specifically means removing calcium deposits; pickle, in metalworking, means treating a surface with acid and can describe one method of removing oxide scale; scale is a close equivalent when removing fish scales. Descale focuses on removing the covering and does not specify the method.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: de- 表示“去掉”，scale 是“表面那层鳞或垢”：去掉它，就是 descale。
mnemonic_anchor.en: De- means 'remove' and scale is the surface covering: take that covering off to descale.

etymology_story.zh: 表示“二合字母”的 digraph 由希腊语来源的 di-（二）与 -graph（书写符号）构成，强调两个字母共同表示一个音。数学中的 digraph 则是 directed graph（有向图）的缩合形式，并非表示“双重图”。
etymology_story.en: The linguistic term combines Greek-derived di-, meaning 'two', with -graph, referring to a written sign, to describe two letters representing one sound. In mathematics, digraph is instead a shortened combination of directed graph and does not mean 'double graph'.

morphology_enriched.zh: 语言学义的构词公式：di-（二）+ -graph（书写符号）；数学义的构词关系：directed graph → digraph（缩合）。主要词族：digraphs（复数）、digraphic（与二合字母或有向图有关的，具体含义依语境）。相关语言学术语有 monograph（单字母符号，此为专门义）、trigraph（三合字母）和 tetragraph（四合字母），它们与 digraph 平行构成，并非其派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: For the linguistic sense, the structure is di- 'two' + -graph 'written sign'; for the mathematical sense, directed graph is shortened to digraph. Principal family forms are digraphs and digraphic, whose interpretation depends on context. Parallel linguistic formations include monograph in its specialized sense of a single-letter sign, trigraph, and tetragraph; these are related formations rather than derivatives of digraph.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: letter pair（字母对）只说明有两个字母，不保证它们共同表示一个音；two-letter grapheme（双字母字素）在相关拼写分析中与语言学义接近；directed graph（有向图）是数学义的完整同义表达。不要把 digraph 与 diphthong（双元音）混淆：前者描述书写，后者描述语音。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Letter pair merely identifies two letters and does not require them to represent one sound; two-letter grapheme is a close equivalent in relevant spelling analysis; directed graph is the full equivalent of the mathematical sense. A digraph concerns writing, whereas a diphthong concerns pronunciation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 拼写中记“两个字母写一个音”；数学中记“directed graph 缩成 digraph”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: For spelling, remember 'two letters, one sound'; for mathematics, expand digraph back into directed graph.

etymology_story.zh: 古生物学家奥塞内尔·查尔斯·马什于1878年以希腊语 diploos（双的）和 dokos（梁）命名 Diplodocus。名称指其尾部下方某些人字骨的双梁形结构，后来该属名也进入普通英语，用来指梁龙个体。
etymology_story.en: The paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh named Diplodocus in 1878 from Greek diploos, meaning 'double', and dokos, meaning 'beam'. The name refers to the double-beamed structure of certain chevron bones beneath its tail, and the genus name subsequently entered ordinary English as a name for an individual animal.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常将 diplodocus 作为完整借入的恐龙名称使用；历史构词为 diplo-（双）+ 希腊语 dokos（梁）的拉丁化形式。复数可用 diplodocuses 或 diplodoci；正式属名写作 Diplodocus，首字母大写。相关分类学词族包括 diplodocid（梁龙科动物；梁龙科的）、Diplodocidae（梁龙科）、diplodocoid（梁龙超科动物；梁龙超科的）及 Diplodocoidea（梁龙超科）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats diplodocus as a borrowed dinosaur name; historically, it combines diplo- 'double' with a Latinized form of Greek dokos 'beam'. Plurals include diplodocuses and diplodoci; the formal genus name is capitalized as Diplodocus. Related taxonomic formations include diplodocid, Diplodocidae, diplodocoid, and Diplodocoidea.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有常用的严格同义词。sauropod（蜥脚类恐龙）是包含梁龙的更大类别；long-necked dinosaur（长颈恐龙）是通俗描述，也适用于其他恐龙；diplodocid（梁龙科动物）指梁龙所属科的成员，范围也比 diplodocus 更广。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym. Sauropod names the larger dinosaur group containing Diplodocus; long-necked dinosaur is an informal description that also applies to other dinosaurs; diplodocid names any member of its family and is therefore broader than diplodocus.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: diplo- 是“双”，dokos 是“梁”：尾下有“双梁”，所以叫“梁龙”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Diplo- means 'double' and dokos means 'beam': remember the double beams beneath the tail.

etymology_story.zh: durbar 经印度斯坦语 darbār 借入英语，最终源自表示“宫廷、朝廷”的波斯语 darbār。该词从统治者的宫廷及接见活动，扩展为隆重的官方典礼；英国殖民时期的使用也使它传播到非洲部分地区。
etymology_story.en: Durbar entered English through Hindustani darbār, ultimately from Persian darbār, meaning 'royal court'. Its meaning extended from a ruler's court and audiences to grand official ceremonies, and British colonial usage also carried the word into parts of Africa.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 durbar 是整词借词，没有可自由拆分的英语词根与词缀；不应把它按英语拆成 dur- + bar。主要形式是 durbar（单数）和 durbars（复数），没有常用的直接派生动词或形容词。Persian darbār 与 Hindustani darbār 是其来源形式，不是英语派生词；Delhi Durbar 是包含该词的专名。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, durbar is an unanalyzed loanword rather than a productive combination of English roots and affixes; it should not be split into dur- and bar. Its principal forms are durbar and the plural durbars, with no common directly derived verb or adjective. Persian darbār and Hindustani darbār are source forms rather than English derivatives; Delhi Durbar is a proper name containing the word.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: court（宫廷；朝廷）可指统治者及其随从构成的机构，不一定指一次活动；audience（正式觐见）强调受到统治者或显要接见；ceremonial assembly（仪式性集会）强调集会的礼仪性质。durbar 带有特定的南亚历史背景，或其在部分非洲地区延续的传统用法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Court can mean the ruler's household or governing circle rather than a particular event; audience emphasizes being formally received by a ruler or dignitary; ceremonial assembly emphasizes the ritual character of a gathering. Durbar carries a specific South Asian historical background or an established traditional use in parts of Africa.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 联想波斯语来源词中的 dar“门”：走进宫门参加正式朝会，就记住 durbar。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use dar, the Persian word for 'door', as a cue: picture entering a palace doorway for a formal royal gathering, a durbar.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中视为不可再分析的借词词基 eddoe，不宜硬拆前后缀。拼写变体：eddo；复数：eddoes。没有常用的派生动词、形容词或副词；eddoe flour（小芋头粉）、eddoe plant（芋类植株）是名词复合结构，其中 eddoe 作名词修饰语。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, eddoe is an unanalyzable borrowed base rather than a combination of productive affixes. Variant: eddo; plural: eddoes. synonyms_and_nuances.en: Taro is the widely used name and overlaps substantially with eddoe; cocoyam is a regional umbrella term that may include plants from different genera. These names can overlap in culinary usage without being exact equivalents in botanical or cultivar identification.

etymology_story.zh: electret 由 electricity 的片段 electr- 与 magnet 的末尾 -et 融合而成，名称体现了它与永久磁体在电学和磁学上的类比。该术语由奥利弗·亥维赛提出，用于描述能够持久保持电学状态的材料。[词源参考](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/electret)
etymology_story.en: Electret blends electr- from electricity with -et from magnet, expressing an electrical analogy with a permanent magnet. Oliver Heaviside introduced the term for material capable of retaining an electrical state. [Etymological reference](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/electret)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：electr(icity) + (magn)et → electret，属于融合构词，-et 在此不是表示“小”的后缀。复数：electrets；技术复合词包括 thermoelectret（热驻极体）、photoelectret（光驻极体）、piezoelectret（压电驻极体）。electret microphone 中 electret 是名词修饰语，不因此另立常用形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: electr(icity) + (magn)et → electret, a blend; -et is not a diminutive suffix here. Plural: electrets. Technical compounds include thermoelectret, photoelectret, and piezoelectret. In electret microphone, electret is a noun modifier rather than evidence of a separate common adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: polarized dielectric（极化介质）与 charged dielectric（带电介质）是相关描述，而非严格同义词：它们本身不保证极化或电荷能长期保持，electret 则突出这种持久性；permanent magnet（永久磁体）只是磁学类比对象。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Polarized dielectric and charged dielectric are related descriptions rather than exact synonyms: neither expression alone guarantees long retention, whereas electret emphasizes persistence. A permanent magnet is its magnetic analogue.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: electricity + magnet：像永久磁体保持磁性一样，驻极体长期保持电荷或极化。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Electricity + magnet: an electret retains charge or polarization as a permanent magnet retains magnetization.

morphology.text: en-（使进入某状态） + ure（旧词：使用、惯常做法） → enure；与 inure 是拼写变体。

etymology_story.zh: enure 与 inure 是历史上并存的拼写，源于表示“在使用中、在实践中”的短语 en ure 或 in ure；旧词 ure 表示“使用、实践”，经法语追溯至拉丁语 opera。其意义由“通过反复实践而习惯”扩展到“发生作用、生效”，并形成法律上的利益归属用法。[词源与义项参考](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/inure)
etymology_story.en: Enure and inure are historical spelling variants arising from en ure or in ure, meaning 'in use' or 'in practice'; obsolete ure meant use or practice and ultimately derives through French from Latin opera. Meanings developed from becoming accustomed through repeated experience to operating or taking effect, including the legal use concerning benefits. [Etymology and senses](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/inure)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中以完整词基 enure 处理；历史上的 en/in + ure 不应误作完全透明、仍可自由组合的现代构词。屈折形式：enures、enured、enuring；派生名词：enurement（生效；利益归属；习惯化）、enuredness（习惯或不再敏感的状态，罕用）。对应拼写词族包括 inure、inures、inured、inuring、inurement、inuredness。enuresis（遗尿）与本词无构词关系。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat enure as a whole lexical base in modern English; historical en/in + ure is not a fully transparent productive modern formation. Inflections: enures, enured, enuring. Derived nouns: enurement, referring to operation, benefit, or habituation, and rare enuredness, the state of being accustomed or less sensitive. The corresponding spelling family includes inure, inures, inured, inuring, inurement, and inuredness. Enuresis is morphologically unrelated.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: take effect（生效）对应发生效力义；accrue（利益等逐渐产生或归于）与利益归属义接近，但常带累积意味；harden（使变得坚强或麻木）对应习惯义，更突出情感或耐受力的变化。这些表达不能跨义项互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Take effect matches the operative sense; accrue overlaps with benefits arising or passing to someone but often suggests accumulation; harden matches habituation while emphasizing toughness or reduced emotional sensitivity. These alternatives are specific to different senses.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“投入使用”连到两条线：事物开始起作用，人反复经历后变习惯。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with 'put into use': a provision begins to operate, while repeated experience makes a person accustomed.

etymology_story.zh: 该词在中古英语时期经拉丁语借自希腊语 erusipelas，其词源成分与“红”和“皮肤”有关。这个古老的皮肤病名称沿用至现代，但人类丹毒与兽医学中的动物丹毒须区分病原和疾病范围。[词源与义项参考](https://ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=erysipelas)
etymology_story.en: The word entered Middle English through Latin from Greek erusipelas, with elements associated with redness and skin. This ancient disease name survives in modern medicine, but human erysipelas and veterinary erysipelas require distinctions in cause and scope. [Etymology and senses](https://ahdictionary.com/word/search.html?q=erysipelas)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中以整体医学词基 erysipelas 记忆，词尾 -s 不是普通复数标记；通常作不可数名词，搭配单数谓语。派生时可用 erysipelat- 词干：erysipelat- + -ous → erysipelatous（丹毒的、丹毒样的）；erysipelat- + -oid → erysipelatoid（丹毒样的，罕用）。erysipeloid（类丹毒）是相关但不同的疾病名称，不能当作人类丹毒的同义词。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat erysipelas as a whole medical base in modern English; final -s is not an ordinary plural ending. It is normally a mass noun with singular agreement. Derivatives use the stem erysipelat-: erysipelat- + -ous → erysipelatous, relating to or resembling erysipelas; erysipelat- + -oid → rare erysipelatoid, resembling erysipelas. Erysipeloid names a related but distinct infection and is not a synonym for human erysipelas.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Saint Anthony's fire（圣安东尼之火）是丹毒的历史别称，但历史上也用于其他疾病，存在歧义；cellulitis（蜂窝织炎）是临床上密切相关的术语，通常涉及更深的皮肤组织，虽有地区将两词混用，也不宜一概视为完全同义。[临床辨析参考](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/infectious-diseases/bacterial-skin-infections/erysipelas)
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Saint Anthony's fire is a historical name for erysipelas but is ambiguous because it has also named other diseases. Cellulitis is a closely related clinical term, usually involving deeper skin tissues; although regional usage sometimes treats the terms interchangeably, they are not universally exact synonyms. [Clinical distinction](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/infectious-diseases/bacterial-skin-infections/erysipelas)

etymology_story.zh: 现代“工班长”义由 gang（一起工作的工班）加表示人的 -er 构成，见于十九世纪英语。历史上另有表示“步行者、行走者”的 ganger，但不能据此把现代领班义简单解释为从“走动的人”直接演变而来。[现代词源参考](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/ganger)；[历史方言义参考](https://dsl.ac.uk/entry/snd/ganger)
