etymology_story.zh: 英语于16世纪借入拉丁语 caduceus，最终源自多利安希腊语 kārykeion，意为“传令官的杖”，与 kāryx“传令官”同源。它与赫尔墨斯及罗马神墨丘利相联系，后来也被用作医疗标志，但不同于单蛇缠绕的阿斯克勒庇俄斯之杖。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Latin caduceus in the sixteenth century, ultimately from Doric Greek kārykeion, meaning 'a herald's staff,' related to kāryx, 'herald.' Associated with Hermes and his Roman counterpart Mercury, it later also became a medical emblem, although it differs from the single-snake rod of Asclepius.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 caduceus 视为不可再作常用词素切分的借词；复数为 caducei。相关派生词有 caducean“与双蛇杖有关的”，可用词干 caduce- + -an 记忆；这些形式不构成庞大的常用词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, caduceus is a borrowed base without a useful productive internal breakdown; its plural is caducei. The related adjective caducean means 'relating to a caduceus' and can be represented as caduce- + -an; the word has only a small established family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: herald's staff“传令杖”是较宽泛的描述；Hermes' staff“赫尔墨斯之杖”明确指向神话人物。rod of Asclepius“阿斯克勒庇俄斯之杖”是容易混淆的相关标志，只有一条蛇，通常无翼，并非同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Herald's staff is a broader descriptive expression; Hermes' staff identifies the mythological owner. The rod of Asclepius is a related symbol often confused with the caduceus, but it has one snake and normally no wings, so it is not a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 传令官赫尔墨斯的标志：双蛇缠杖，杖顶生翼。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture Hermes the herald: two snakes around a staff, with wings above.

etymology_story.zh: 英语于19世纪借入法语 cassitérite，该名称以希腊语 kassiteros“锡”为基础，加上矿物名称后缀 -ite 构成。名称直接指出这种矿物与锡的关系。

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：cassiter-（源自希腊语“锡”的学术词干）+ -ite（矿物后缀）→ cassiterite“锡石”。相关专业形容词为 cassiteritic“含锡石的；与锡石有关的”；表示多个种类或标本时可用复数 cassiterites。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: cassiter- (a learned stem from the Greek word for tin) + -ite (a mineral suffix) → cassiterite. The related technical adjective is cassiteritic, 'containing or relating to cassiterite'; cassiterites is possible when referring to different types or specimens.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tinstone“锡石”是传统同义名称；tin ore“锡矿石”强调可供提炼锡的矿物材料，范围更广；tin dioxide“二氧化锡”是其化学成分的名称，也可指人工制得的物质，并不专指天然矿物。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tinstone is a traditional synonym. Tin ore is broader and emphasizes material from which tin can be extracted. Tin dioxide names the chemical substance, including manufactured material, rather than specifically the natural mineral.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cassiter- 表示“锡”，-ite 表示“矿物”：含锡的矿物就是锡石。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Cassiter- means tin and -ite marks a mineral: think 'tin mineral.'

meaning: 木麻黄（一类枝条细长、有节的树）

pronunciation.note: 本卡英式读法重音在 /riː/，拉长 /iː/；词尾 /nə/ 轻读。

forms: 可数；复数 casuarinas。
family: Casuarinaceae 木麻黄科；casuarina 常作植物普通名。

morphology.text: casuarin-（casuarina 的科名词干）+ -aceae（植物科名后缀）→ Casuarinaceae（木麻黄科）；casuarina 整词作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 英语借自新拉丁语属名 Casuarina，再追溯到马来语中表示食火鸡的词。细垂枝条像食火鸡的羽毛，是名称的形象线索。

usage_note: casuarina 是木麻黄，细枝虽看着像松针，却不等于 pine（松树）。普通名小写，拉丁属名 Casuarina 大写并通常用斜体。

senses.meaning_zh: 木麻黄；具有细长、有节、针状小枝的常绿乔木或灌木
senses.meaning_en: An evergreen tree or shrub with slender, jointed, needle-like branchlets.
senses.english_definition: A casuarina is an evergreen tree or shrub, native chiefly to Australia and nearby regions, with thin, jointed branchlets that look like pine needles.
senses.collocation_en: casuarina trees; a casuarina windbreak
senses.collocation_zh: 木麻黄树；木麻黄防风林带
senses.sentence_en: A row of casuarina trees sheltered the houses from strong coastal winds.
senses.sentence_zh: 一排木麻黄树为房屋挡住了海岸上的强风。

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自新拉丁语属名 Casuarina，该名称源于表示“食火鸡”的马来语词 kasuari。木麻黄下垂的纤细小枝使人联想到食火鸡蓬松、毛发状的羽毛，因此得名。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the New Latin genus name Casuarina, derived from Malay kasuari, 'cassowary.' The name refers to the resemblance between the tree's fine, drooping branchlets and a cassowary's shaggy, hair-like feathers.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代普通英语中将 casuarina 作为完整借词记忆，复数为 casuarinas。分类学相关形式为 Casuarina“木麻黄属”、casuarin- + -aceae → Casuarinaceae“木麻黄科”，以及 casuarin- + -aceous → casuarinaceous“木麻黄科的”。
morphology_enriched.en: In ordinary modern English, casuarina is a whole borrowed base, with the plural casuarinas. Related taxonomic forms are Casuarina, the genus name; casuarin- + -aceae → Casuarinaceae, the family name; and casuarin- + -aceous → casuarinaceous, 'belonging to the casuarina family.'

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: she-oak“木麻黄类树木”是常见俗称，也可用于近缘属；Australian pine“澳洲松”是某些木麻黄的俗称，但它们并非真正的松树；ironwood“铁木”着重木材坚硬，也用于许多无亲缘关系的树种。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: She-oak is a common name that can also cover related genera. Australian pine is used for some casuarinas, although they are not true pines. Ironwood emphasizes hard timber and is also applied to many unrelated trees.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 食火鸡羽毛般的细垂枝条，就是木麻黄得名的线索。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a cassowary's shaggy feathers hanging like casuarina branchlets.

meaning: 叽喳柳莺（一种欧洲小型鸣禽）

pronunciation.note: 本卡美式读法首段重读；ch 两次都读 /tʃ/，前段元音 /ɪ/，后段 /æ/。

forms: 可数；复数 chiffchaffs。
family: 相关词：warbler 莺类鸣禽；birdsong 鸟鸣。

morphology.text: chiff（模仿鸣声的一段）+ chaff（模仿鸣声的另一段）→ chiffchaff；这是拟声命名，不能按 chaff“谷壳”理解鸟名。

etymology.text: 英语中模仿这种鸟反复鸣叫的声音而造出的鸟名。听起来像交替的 chiff、chaff，两声连起来就是名称。

usage_note: chiffchaff 是具体鸟种，warbler 是更宽泛的莺类名称。

senses.meaning_zh: 叽喳柳莺；鸣声似反复交替的“chiff-chaff”的小型柳莺
senses.meaning_en: A small warbler named after its repeated two-note song.
senses.english_definition: A chiffchaff is a small, mainly European and Asian bird with greenish-brown plumage and a repeated song that sounds like 'chiff-chaff.'
senses.collocation_en: a chiffchaff's song; a singing chiffchaff
senses.collocation_zh: 叽喳柳莺的鸣声；一只正在鸣唱的叽喳柳莺
senses.sentence_en: We heard a chiffchaff singing in the trees beside the path.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们听见一只叽喳柳莺在小路旁的树丛中鸣唱。

etymology_story.zh: 这个英语鸟名通过模仿其反复交替的鸣声而形成。chiff 和 chaff 在这里是拟声成分，与普通名词 chaff“谷壳”的意义无关。
etymology_story.en: This English bird name was formed by imitating the bird's repeated alternating notes. Chiff and chaff function as sound imitations here; the name has no semantic connection with chaff meaning grain husks.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：chiff（拟声）+ chaff（拟声）→ chiffchaff，属于元音交替的拟声构词。复数为 chiffchaffs；没有常用的标准派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: chiff (imitated sound) + chaff (imitated sound) → chiffchaff, an onomatopoeic formation with vowel alternation. The plural is chiffchaffs; there is no commonly used established family of derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: common chiffchaff“叽喳柳莺”是更明确的物种名称；warbler“莺类鸣禽”是范围更广的类别名称；willow warbler“欧柳莺”是外形相似的另一物种，通常可根据鸣声区分，并非同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Common chiffchaff is the more explicit species name. Warbler is a broader category. Willow warbler names a different, similar-looking species that is often distinguished by its song, so it is not a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 听见“chiff、chaff”交替唱，就记住鸟名 chiffchaff。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Its song says its name: chiff, chaff, chiff, chaff.

meaning: 鸡蛇怪（传说中目光能致命的蛇形怪物）

pronunciation.note: 本卡美式读法首音节重读，开头为 /kɑː/；末尾读 /trəs/，不要读成 /traɪs/。

forms: 可数；复数 cockatrices。
family: 相关词：basilisk 蛇怪；legend 传说。

morphology.text: cockatrice + -like → cockatrice-like（像鸡蛇怪的）；cockatrice 本身作为独立词素记忆，不能硬拆成 cock 与普通名词后缀。

etymology.text: 中古英语 cocatrice 来自中古法语 cocatris，再来自中世纪拉丁语 cocatrix。记住古老传说中带有鸡的特征、目光危险的怪物。

usage_note: cockatrice 属于传说生物，并非真实动物学中的蛇种。

senses.meaning_zh: 鸡蛇怪；传说中常具鸡首、蛇身，目光可致命的怪物
senses.meaning_en: A legendary serpent-like monster, often with a rooster's head, said to kill with its gaze.
senses.english_definition: A cockatrice is an imaginary monster, often shown with a rooster's head and a serpent's body, that was believed to kill people by looking at them.
senses.collocation_en: a cockatrice's deadly gaze; a heraldic cockatrice
senses.collocation_zh: 鸡蛇怪致命的目光；纹章中的鸡蛇怪
senses.sentence_en: The medieval illustration shows a cockatrice with a rooster's head and a serpent's tail.
senses.sentence_zh: 这幅中世纪插图描绘了一只长着公鸡头和蛇尾的鸡蛇怪。

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语 cocatrice 经古法语 cocatris 传入，其词源通常追溯至中世纪拉丁语 calcatrix，字面义为“踩踏者”，原先与獴一类动物有关。后来词形受到表示“公鸡”的词的影响，相关传说也将它塑造成兼具鸡与蛇特征的致命怪物。
etymology_story.en: Middle English cocatrice came through Old French cocatris and is usually traced to medieval Latin calcatrix, literally 'treader,' originally associated with a mongoose-like animal. Its form was later influenced by words for a rooster, while folklore developed it into a deadly creature combining rooster and serpent features.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 cockatrice 是不可按常用词根、词缀可靠拆分的完整词，不能直接分析为 cock 加普通后缀。复数为 cockatrices；cockatrice + -like → cockatrice-like“像鸡蛇怪的”是透明、可临时构成的描述形式，并非常用独立派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, cockatrice is a whole base that cannot reliably be divided into ordinary productive roots and affixes; it is not simply cock plus a standard suffix. Its plural is cockatrices; cockatrice + -like → cockatrice-like is a transparent descriptive formation rather than a common independent derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: basilisk“蛇怪”在中世纪传说中常与 cockatrice 混用，但不一定具有公鸡特征；dragon“龙”是更宽泛的神话爬行动物形象；wyvern“双足飞龙”通常有双翼、两足和长尾，属于不同的纹章怪兽。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Basilisk often overlaps with cockatrice in medieval accounts but need not have rooster-like features. Dragon is a broader term for a mythical reptilian creature. Wyvern usually denotes a winged, two-legged creature with a long tail and is a distinct heraldic monster.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用外形辅助记忆：公鸡头、蛇形身、致命眼；这只是记忆画面，并非现代词素拆解。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the picture: rooster's head, serpent's body, deadly eyes; this is a visual hook, not a morphological breakdown.

pronunciation.note: 本卡采用英式 /ˈkʌmfɪt/：首音节重读，o 读 /ʌ/，末音节是短音 /fɪt/。

forms: 可数；复数 comfits。
family: 相关词：confection 糖果甜食；confit 与它有历史联系，但现代常指油封食物。

morphology.text: comfit + box → comfit-box（装糖衣果仁的小盒）；comfit 作为独立词素记忆，不按 com + fit 硬拆。

etymology.text: 经中古英语 confyt 等形式，来自盎格鲁法语 confit“糖渍食品”，再追溯到拉丁语 conficere“制作、完成”。想象给果仁反复裹糖的制作过程。

usage_note: comfit 是裹糖的果仁、种子等小糖果，不是泛指所有 candy，也不同于现代烹饪里的 confit。

senses.meaning_en: a nut, seed, or small piece of fruit coated in sugar
senses.english_definition: A comfit is a small sweet made by covering a nut, seed, or piece of fruit with sugar.
senses.collocation_en: sugar-coated comfits; caraway comfits
senses.collocation_zh: 糖衣小甜食；糖衣葛缕子籽

etymology_story.zh: 经中古英语 confit、confyt 等形式，借自盎格鲁法语，最终源于拉丁语 conficere，意为“制作、完成”。这一表示加工制作的词源，在食品语境中逐渐发展出糖渍或裹糖甜食的意思。
etymology_story.en: Through Middle English forms such as confit and confyt, the word came from Anglo-French and ultimately from Latin conficere, meaning “to prepare or complete.” In food vocabulary, this idea of preparation developed into the meaning of a preserved or sugar-coated sweet.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中视为不可再拆的借入词：comfit，不能按 com- + fit 分析。复数为 comfits；透明复合词有 comfit box（糖果盒）。没有常用的现代派生词族；confit（油封食物）和 confection（甜食）是词源相关词，并非由 comfit 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, comfit is an unanalyzed borrowing, not com- + fit. Its plural is comfits, and a transparent compound is comfit box. It has no common productive modern derivative family; confit and confection are etymological relatives, not derivatives of comfit.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dragée（糖衣小甜食）最接近，但也可指巧克力包衣制品；sugarplum（小糖果）是传统称呼，并不一定含李子；confection（甜食）范围更广，不限定裹糖果仁或种子。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dragée is the closest equivalent, although it can also describe chocolate-coated sweets; sugarplum is a traditional small sweet that need not contain plum; confection is broader and does not specifically imply a coated nut or seed.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住词源中的“制作”：把果仁一层层加工裹糖，就制成 comfit。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the historical idea of preparation: build layers of sugar around a nut to make a comfit.

pronunciation.note: 本卡美式读法重音在 /tiː/；c 在这里读 /tʃ/，词尾是双元音 /oʊ/。

morphology.text: concert-（意大利语 concerto 的词干）+ -ino（小称后缀）→ concertino（小协奏曲）。

etymology.text: 从意大利语借入，是 concerto“协奏曲”的小称形式。可以把本课义项记成篇幅较短的一首协奏曲。

usage_note: 本课 concertino 指短小协奏曲；在讨论 concerto grosso 时，也可能指独奏乐器组，要看上下文。

etymology_story.zh: 借自意大利语 concertino，是 concerto（协奏曲）的小称形式。这个“小”的概念既可指规模较小的协奏曲，也可指大协奏曲中人数较少的独奏小组。
etymology_story.en: Concertino was borrowed from Italian as a diminutive of concerto. The idea of smallness applies both to a smaller concerto and to the small solo group within a concerto grosso.

morphology_enriched.zh: 借入词内部保留意大利语构形：concert-（concerto 去掉词尾 -o）+ -ino（小称后缀）。复数可用英语形式 concertinos 或意大利语形式 concertini；相关音乐词有 concerto（协奏曲）、concertante（协奏性的；协奏曲式作品），它们不是英语中由 concertino 加后缀派生的词。
morphology_enriched.en: The borrowing preserves Italian morphology: concert-, formed by removing the final -o of concerto, + the diminutive suffix -ino. Plurals are concertinos or Italian concertini. Related musical vocabulary includes concerto and concertante; these are not English suffixal derivatives of concertino.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: short concerto（短协奏曲）最接近作品义；concerto（协奏曲）是上位概念，不限定篇幅；solo group（独奏小组）对应演奏群体义，但适用范围比大协奏曲更广。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Short concerto closely paraphrases the composition sense; concerto is the broader category and does not specify length; solo group paraphrases the ensemble sense but is not restricted to the concerto grosso.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: concerto 加上表示“小”的 -ino：小作品，或大乐队中的小独奏组。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Add the diminutive -ino to concerto: a small concerto, or the small solo group within the larger ensemble.

meaning: 喂——！（用于远距离招呼或引起注意的呼声）

pronunciation.note: 本卡英式读法首音节重读，/uː/ 和 /iː/ 分成两个音节，都是长元音。

forms: 作呼喊语时无词形变化；另有动词 cooee、cooeed、cooeeing。
family: cooey 同一呼声的另一拼法；within cooee 在呼喊可及的距离内。

morphology.text: cooee + -ing → cooeeing（发出这种呼声的行为）；cooee 作为独立词素记忆，名词化 -ing 可表示呼喊这一活动。

etymology.text: 英语从澳大利亚原住民语言借入这种呼声，后来成为澳大利亚英语的野外招呼声。把拉长的两段音和远处回应的人联系起来。

usage_note: cooee 用来招呼远处的人，不专门表示欢呼胜利；常见于澳大利亚英语。

senses.meaning_zh: 喂——！有人吗——！（用于远距离招呼或引起注意）

senses.english_definition: You call out “cooee” when you want someone, especially someone some distance away, to notice you.
senses.collocation_en: Cooee! Over here!; call out “cooee”

senses.meaning_zh: 用于远距离招呼的呼声
senses.meaning_en: a long call used to attract someone's attention
senses.english_definition: A cooee is a call that someone makes to attract attention or signal their position.
senses.collocation_en: give a cooee; hear a cooee

senses.meaning_zh: 可听到呼声的距离；接近的范围（主要用于固定短语）
senses.meaning_en: calling distance or a reasonably close range, chiefly in fixed phrases
senses.english_definition: If someone or something is within cooee of a place, amount, or standard, they are reasonably close to it.
senses.collocation_en: within cooee of; not within cooee of

senses.meaning_en: to make a cooee call
senses.english_definition: If you cooee, you make a long call to attract someone's attention or let them know where you are.
senses.collocation_en: cooee to someone; cooee across the valley
senses.collocation_zh: 向某人高声招呼；朝山谷对面呼喊
senses.sentence_en: He cooeed to his friends across the river.
senses.sentence_zh: 他向河对岸的朋友们高声招呼。

etymology_story.zh: 借自澳大利亚悉尼地区的达鲁格语，源语中的相应形式表示“到这里来”，英语通常拼作 cooee。它后来成为澳大利亚英语的远距离招呼声，并由“呼声能传到的范围”发展出“接近”的比喻用法。
etymology_story.en: Cooee was borrowed from Dharug, an Aboriginal language of the Sydney region, from an expression meaning “come here.” It became a distance call in Australian English, and the range over which it could be heard produced figurative expressions meaning “close to.”

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为不可再拆的借入词，不宜分析为 coo + ee。同一词形兼作感叹词、名词和动词；名词复数及动词第三人称单数为 cooees，过去式和过去分词为 cooeed，现在分词为 cooeeing；cooeeing 也可表示呼喊这一活动。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, cooee is an unanalyzed borrowing, not coo + ee. The same form functions as an interjection, noun, and verb. The noun plural and third-person singular verb are cooees; the past tense and past participle are cooeed; the present participle is cooeeing, which can also name the activity.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: yoo-hoo（喂；嗨）通常用于轻松地引起注意；halloo（喂——；高声招呼）也可用于远处呼喊，但较显旧式；call（呼喊；招呼）最宽泛，不指定这种具有澳大利亚地域特色的呼声。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Yoo-hoo is usually a light, informal attention-getter; halloo can also be a distance call but sounds more old-fashioned; call is the general term and does not identify this distinctively Australian cry.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 拉长两段声音“库——伊——”：声音传得到，就是 within cooee；由此联想到“接近”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Imagine a long “koo-ee” carrying across a valley: within cooee means within calling range, and therefore figuratively close.

senses.english_definition: A couchette is a sleeping place on a train, usually in a shared compartment and often made by converting a seat.
senses.collocation_en: book a couchette; a six-berth couchette compartment

etymology_story.zh: 借自法语 couchette，由 couche（床；卧处）加小称后缀 -ette 构成，原意是“小床”。英语主要采用其铁路用法，指列车上的简易卧铺。
etymology_story.en: Couchette comes from French couchette, formed from couche, meaning “bed” or “resting place,” with the diminutive suffix -ette. English chiefly adopted its railway meaning: a basic sleeping berth on a train.

morphology_enriched.zh: 英语中整体借入；其法语内部结构为 couche（床）+ -ette（小称后缀）。复数为 couchettes；常见复合搭配有 couchette car（卧铺车厢）和 couchette compartment（卧铺包厢），没有常用的英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: English borrowed the word whole; its internal French structure is couche, “bed,” + the diminutive suffix -ette. The plural is couchettes. Common compounds include couchette car and couchette compartment; there is no common English derivative family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: berth（交通工具上的铺位）范围更广，也用于船上；bunk（上下铺中的铺位）强调床铺的结构，不限于火车；sleeper（卧铺车厢等）常指整节车厢，不能始终替换表示单个铺位的 couchette。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Berth is broader and also applies to sleeping places on ships; bunk emphasizes a bed arranged above or below another and is not train-specific; sleeper often means an entire sleeping car, so it is not always interchangeable with couchette.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 法语“床”加“小”：夜车包厢里的一张小卧铺。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think “bed + little”: a small sleeping berth inside an overnight train.

meaning: 篝灯；火篮（盛燃料照明的金属容器）

pronunciation.note: 本卡英式读法首音节重读，词尾 -et 读短音 /ɪt/，不要读成 /eɪ/。

forms: 可数；复数 cressets。
family: 相关词：torch 火炬；lantern 灯笼。

morphology.text: cresset + light → cresset-light（篝灯的光）；cresset 整词作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 中古英语从盎格鲁法语借入，关联表示“油脂”的 creisse、gresse。想象把油脂放进金属容器点燃照明，就能连起旧时词义。

usage_note: cresset 指盛着燃料的金属灯器，通常出现在历史叙述中；不是现代电灯。

senses.meaning_zh: 篝灯；用于燃烧油脂、木材等以照明的金属火篮或容器
senses.meaning_en: a metal container in which fuel is burned to provide light
senses.english_definition: A cresset is a metal container that holds burning fuel and is used as a light, especially in descriptions of the past.
senses.collocation_en: a burning cresset; the light of a cresset
senses.collocation_zh: 燃着的篝灯；篝灯的光
senses.sentence_en: A cresset burned above the castle gate.
senses.sentence_zh: 城堡大门上方燃着一盏篝灯。

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语从盎格鲁法语借入 cresset；其更早来源通常与古法语中表示“油脂”的词及小称形式联系起来。这个词所指的旧式灯具通过在容器中燃烧油脂或其他燃料来照明。
etymology_story.en: Middle English borrowed cresset from Anglo-French; its earlier history is generally connected with Old French words for grease and a diminutive formation. The historical lighting device produced light by burning grease or other fuel in a container.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中视为不可再拆的词，不能分析为 cress（独行菜）+ -et。复数为 cressets；描述性复合词可见 cresset light（篝灯光），但没有常用的现代派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, cresset is unanalyzed and should not be divided into cress + -et. Its plural is cressets. A descriptive compound is cresset light, but the word has no common modern derivative family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: brazier（火盆）与其容器形态相近，但通常主要用于取暖；torch（火把）通常是可手持的燃烧照明物；beacon（烽火；信号灯）强调传递信号或指引方向，而 cresset 强调盛放燃料的照明容器。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A brazier resembles a cresset as a fuel-holding container but is usually chiefly for warmth; a torch is typically a portable burning light; a beacon emphasizes signaling or guidance, whereas cresset identifies the container used to hold the lighting fuel.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把词源中的“油脂”放进金属火篮，点燃后就是旧时篝灯。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect the historical grease association with a metal fire basket: fuel inside, light above.

pronunciation.note: 本卡美式读法首音节重读，dh 读 /d/；首段元音 /oʊ/，词尾 /iː/。

forms: 可数；复数 dhobis。
family: dhobie 另一拼法；dhobi ghat 洗衣场。

morphology.text: dhobi + ghat → dhobi ghat（洗衣场）；dhobi 是借入的完整词素，ghat 指河岸台阶等场所。

etymology.text: 从印地语 dhobī 借入英语，和表示“洗”的印度语言词语有联系。记住河岸边洗衣、晾衣的劳动场景。

usage_note: dhobi 多见于南亚生活或历史叙述，指洗衣劳动者；一般职业名称可用 laundry worker。

senses.meaning_zh: 洗衣工；洗衣人（南亚语境）
senses.meaning_en: a person whose occupation is washing clothes, especially in South Asia
senses.english_definition: A dhobi is someone in South Asia whose job is to wash other people's clothes.
senses.collocation_en: a local dhobi; dhobi ghat
senses.collocation_zh: 当地洗衣工；公共洗衣场（常设于河岸）
senses.sentence_en: The local dhobi collects our laundry every Monday.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 dhobi 借自印地语 dhobī，意为“洗衣工”，与印地语表示“洗”的动词 dhonā 有关。借入英语后，这个词保留了南亚职业与生活文化的地域色彩。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed dhobi from Hindi dhobī, meaning a washerman, which is related to dhonā, 'to wash.' In English, it has retained its association with occupations and everyday life in South Asia.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，dhobi 是整体借入的名词，不能拆成能产的英语词根与词缀；复数为 dhobis。常见复合词有 dhobi ghat（公共洗衣场）和 dhobi wallah（洗衣工）；它没有常用的英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, dhobi is a borrowed noun with no productive English root-and-affix breakdown; its plural is dhobis. Common compounds include dhobi ghat, a communal washing place, and dhobi wallah, a laundry worker; it has no established family of common English derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: washerman（男洗衣工）强调男性身份；laundry worker（洗衣工作人员）是性别中立、适用范围更广的职业名称；launderer（洗衣者或洗衣业者）较正式。dhobi 特别带有南亚地域和文化色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Washerman specifically denotes a male worker; laundry worker is gender-neutral and applies to a wider range of workplaces; launderer is more formal and can denote a person or business. Dhobi specifically carries South Asian regional and cultural associations.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 dhobi 与河岸洗衣场联系起来：洗衣的人是 dhobi，洗衣的地方是 dhobi ghat。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a riverside laundry: the person washing is the dhobi, and the washing place is the dhobi ghat.

meaning: 针鼹（一类有刺的卵生哺乳动物）

pronunciation.note: 本卡美式读法重音在 /kɪd/；ch 读 /k/，词尾 /nə/ 轻读。

forms: 可数；复数 echidnas。
family: 相关词：monotreme 单孔类哺乳动物；spiny anteater 针鼹的俗名。

morphology.text: echidna + -like → echidna-like（像针鼹的）；echidna 整词作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 经新拉丁语动物属名借入英语，再可追溯到拉丁语和希腊语中表示“蛇、蝰蛇”的词。如今它却是满身刺、会产卵的哺乳动物名称。

usage_note: echidna 是针鼹，不是 hedgehog（刺猬）；外形都有刺，动物类别不同。

senses.meaning_en: a spiny, egg-laying mammal native to Australia and New Guinea

senses.collocation_en: short-beaked echidna; long-beaked echidna
senses.collocation_zh: 短吻针鼹；长吻针鼹

etymology_story.zh: echidna 经科学拉丁语属名 Echidna 进入英语，最终源自希腊语 ekh idna 所对应的词 ἔχιδνα，意为“蝰蛇”。这个原本与蛇有关的名称被用于动物分类，后来成为这种有刺卵生哺乳动物的普通名称。
etymology_story.en: Echidna entered English through the scientific Latin genus name Echidna, ultimately from Greek ἔχιδνα, meaning 'viper.' A name originally associated with snakes was applied in zoological classification and became the everyday name of this spiny, egg-laying mammal.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，echidna 作为完整词基使用，通常不拆成英语词根与词缀；常用复数为 echidnas。相关构词包括 echidna-like（像针鼹的）、short-beaked echidna（短吻针鼹）和 long-beaked echidna（长吻针鼹）；它没有常用的能产派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, echidna functions as a complete base rather than a combination of English roots and affixes; its usual plural is echidnas. Related formations include echidna-like, short-beaked echidna, and long-beaked echidna; it has no common productive family of derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: spiny anteater（有刺食蚁兽）是针鼹的另一通俗名称，但针鼹并非真正的食蚁兽；monotreme（单孔类动物）和 egg-laying mammal（卵生哺乳动物）都是范围更广的类别名称，也包括鸭嘴兽。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Spiny anteater is an alternative common name, although an echidna is not a true anteater. Monotreme and egg-laying mammal are broader category terms that also include the platypus.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住“有刺、产卵、喝奶”这组三重特征，就能锁定针鼹。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor the animal with three features: spines, eggs, and milk.

meaning: 铁氰化物（含铁氰根的化合物）

pronunciation.note: 本卡美式读法主重音在 /saɪ/；cy 读 /saɪ/，末段 -nide 读 /naɪd/。

forms: 通常作物质名不可数；指多种盐时可用 ferricyanides。
family: ferricyanic 铁氰酸的；相关词 ferrocyanide 亚铁氰化物。

morphology.text: ferri-（三价铁）+ cyanide（氰化物）→ ferricyanide（铁氰化物）。

etymology.text: 属于国际科学词汇，以表示三价铁的 ferri- 和 cyanide 组合命名。ferri- 可追溯到拉丁语 ferrum“铁”，名称提示了铁的化学状态。

usage_note: ferricyanide 与 ferrocyanide 名称相近，但铁的氧化态不同；本课指化合物，不把它泛称为任何氰化物。

senses.meaning_zh: 铁氰化物；含六氰合铁(III)酸根的盐；亦指该配离子
senses.meaning_en: a salt containing the hexacyanidoferrate(III) ion, or the ion itself
senses.english_definition: A ferricyanide is a salt containing a complex ion in which an iron atom in the +3 oxidation state is bonded to six cyanide groups.
senses.collocation_en: potassium ferricyanide; ferricyanide ion
senses.collocation_zh: 铁氰化钾；铁氰根离子
senses.sentence_en: The reaction reduces ferricyanide to ferrocyanide.
senses.sentence_zh: 该反应将铁氰根还原为亚铁氰根。

etymology_story.zh: ferricyanide 是由 ferri- 与 cyanide 组成的科学术语；ferri- 源自拉丁语 ferrum“铁”，在这套命名中表示铁处于 +3 氧化态。cyanide 的词源最终与希腊语表示“深蓝色”的词有关，反映了氰化物化学与普鲁士蓝的历史联系。
etymology_story.en: Ferricyanide is a scientific formation combining ferri- with cyanide; ferri- comes from Latin ferrum, 'iron,' and here identifies iron in the +3 oxidation state. Cyanide ultimately derives from a Greek word for dark blue, reflecting the historical connection between cyanide chemistry and Prussian blue.

morphology_enriched.zh: ferri-（铁处于 +3 氧化态）+ cyanide（氰化物）→ ferricyanide。相关构词包括 ferricyanide ion（铁氰根离子，[Fe(CN)6]³⁻）、potassium ferricyanide（铁氰化钾）和 sodium ferricyanide（铁氰化钠）；对照词 ferrocyanide（亚铁氰化物）中的 ferro- 表示铁处于 +2 氧化态。
morphology_enriched.en: Ferri- (iron in the +3 oxidation state) + cyanide → ferricyanide. Related formations include ferricyanide ion, [Fe(CN)6]³⁻, potassium ferricyanide, and sodium ferricyanide; the contrasting term ferrocyanide uses ferro- to identify iron in the +2 oxidation state.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hexacyanidoferrate(III)（六氰合铁(III)酸根或其盐）是系统命名形式，hexacyanoferrate(III) 是仍常见的传统命名形式；两者都应根据上下文区分配离子与盐。potassium ferricyanide（铁氰化钾）仅指一种具体钾盐，不能代替所有 ferricyanides。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hexacyanidoferrate(III) is the systematic naming form, while hexacyanoferrate(III) is a widely used older form; context distinguishes the complex ion from its salts. Potassium ferricyanide denotes one particular potassium salt and cannot replace ferricyanide in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“铁 + 六个氰配体”：ferri- 对应铁(III)，与 ferro- 对应的铁(II) 成对记忆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture iron surrounded by six cyanide ligands: pair ferri- with iron(III) and ferro- with iron(II).

pronunciation.note: 主重音在 op 段；fibre 读 /faɪbər/，op 的元音为 /ɒ/，末段 /tɪk/ 不重读。

forms: 形容词；不用复数或时态变化。美式拼法 fiberoptic，也常写作 fibre-optic / fiber-optic。
family: fibre optics 光纤技术；optical fibre 光纤。

morphology.text: fibre（纤维）+ optic（光学的）→ fibreoptic（光纤的）。

etymology.text: 现代英语由 fibre 和 optic 组成，源于 fibre optics 这一技术名称。把细纤维里传送的光和这个词连起来。

usage_note: fibreoptic 说明设备使用光纤，不等于 wireless（无线的）；英式 fibre 对应美式 fiber。

senses.english_definition: Fibreoptic equipment uses thin glass or plastic fibres to carry light, images, or information.

senses.sentence_zh: 这家诊所使用光纤仪器检查患者的气道。

etymology_story.zh: fibreoptic 由 fibre“纤维”和 optic“光学的”组合而成，与现代技术名称 fibre optics“光纤光学；光纤技术”相联系。其含义从利用细纤维导光延伸到传输图像和通信信号。
etymology_story.en: Fibreoptic combines fibre with optic and is associated with the modern technical term fibre optics. Its meaning covers the use of thin fibres to guide light and, through that light, transmit images and communication signals.

morphology_enriched.zh: fibre（纤维）+ optic（光学的）→ fibreoptic；常见拼写为 fibre-optic，美式拼写为 fiberoptic 或 fiber-optic。相关词族与术语包括 fibre optics（光纤技术）、fibreoptics（同义合写形式）、optical fibre（光导纤维）和 fibre-optically（通过光纤，以光纤方式）；名词学科名称通常用 fibre optics。
morphology_enriched.en: Fibre + optic → fibreoptic; a common spelling is fibre-optic, with American forms fiberoptic and fiber-optic. Related forms and terms include fibre optics, the closed form fibreoptics, optical fibre, and fibre-optically, meaning by means of optical fibres; the field is normally named with the noun phrase fibre optics.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fibre-optic（光纤的）与 fibreoptic 意义相同，只是拼写形式不同；fiber-optic 是相应的美式拼写；optical（光学的）范围更广，不一定涉及光纤。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fibre-optic has the same meaning as fibreoptic and differs only in spelling; fiber-optic is the corresponding American spelling. Optical is broader and does not necessarily involve fibres.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: fibre 是细丝，optic 关乎光：让光沿细丝走，就是光纤技术。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Fibre supplies the thin strand; optic supplies the light: light travelling along a strand gives the core idea.

pronunciation.note: 本卡美式读法首音节重读；开头 /fjuː/ 保留 /j/，末尾 /koʊs/ 的 s 不浊化。

morphology.text: fuc-（取自拉丁语 fucus，海藻）+ -ose（糖类后缀）→ fucose（岩藻糖）。

etymology.text: 国际科学词汇，以拉丁语 fucus“海藻”配上糖类名称常见的 -ose 构成。海藻是记住名称的线索，但这种糖不只存在于海藻中。

usage_note: fucose 是一种特定的糖，不是葡萄糖 glucose，也不是泛指所有糖类。

senses.meaning_zh: 岩藻糖；一种六碳脱氧糖，天然形式主要为 L-岩藻糖
senses.meaning_en: a six-carbon deoxy sugar occurring naturally mainly as L-fucose
senses.english_definition: Fucose is a sugar found in seaweeds and in many complex carbohydrates attached to proteins and lipids in living organisms.

etymology_story.zh: fucose 由海藻属名 Fucus 的词干与糖类名称后缀 -ose 构成，反映了早期从海藻材料中分离这种糖的历史。它后来也被发现广泛存在于动物等生物的糖蛋白和糖脂中。
etymology_story.en: Fucose was formed from the stem of the seaweed genus name Fucus and the sugar suffix -ose, reflecting its early isolation from seaweed material. It was subsequently recognized as a widespread component of glycoproteins and glycolipids in animals and other organisms.

morphology_enriched.zh: fuc-（取自海藻属名 Fucus）+ -ose（糖类后缀）→ fucose。主要相关构词包括 fucosyl（岩藻糖基）、fucoside（岩藻糖苷）、fucosidase（岩藻糖苷酶）、fucosylate（使岩藻糖基化）、fucosylation（岩藻糖基化）、fucosylated（经岩藻糖基化的）、fucosyltransferase（岩藻糖基转移酶）、defucosylation（去岩藻糖基化）和 afucosylated（无岩藻糖基的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Fuc- (from the seaweed genus Fucus) + -ose (the sugar suffix) → fucose. Principal related formations include fucosyl, a fucose-derived group; fucoside, a fucose glycoside; fucosidase, an enzyme that cleaves fucosidic bonds; fucosylate, fucosylation, and fucosylated, referring to the addition of fucose groups; fucosyltransferase, an enzyme that transfers them; defucosylation, their removal; and afucosylated, lacking such groups.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 6-deoxygalactose（6-脱氧半乳糖）是 fucose 的结构名称，但未指定立体构型；L-fucose（L-岩藻糖）与 6-deoxy-L-galactose（6-脱氧-L-半乳糖）指同一种特定立体异构体，也是自然界最常见的形式。D-fucose（D-岩藻糖）则是另一种对映异构体。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: 6-Deoxygalactose is a structural name for fucose without specifying its stereochemical configuration. L-fucose and 6-deoxy-L-galactose name the same particular stereoisomer, the predominant natural form; D-fucose is the other enantiomer.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: fuc- 连海藻，-ose 连糖：名字从海藻来，分布却远超海藻。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link fuc- to seaweed and -ose to sugar: the name points to seaweed, while the sugar occurs much more widely.

pronunciation.note: 本卡英式读法首音节重读；ng 后保留 /ɡ/，-oid 读双元音 /ɔɪd/。

forms: 形容词；一般不分比较级，必要时说 more fungoid。
family: fungus 真菌；fungal 真菌的。

morphology.text: fung-（fungus 的词干，真菌）+ -oid（像……的）→ fungoid（似真菌的）。

etymology.text: 英语在 fungus 的词干后接上 -oid 构成；fungus 来自拉丁语，-oid 可追溯到希腊语中“形状”的表达。外形像真菌，是本课的记忆重点。

usage_note: fungoid 强调像真菌的形状或性质；fungal 更直接表示与真菌有关。

senses.meaning_zh: 似真菌的；真菌状的
senses.meaning_en: Resembling a fungus in appearance or growth.
senses.english_definition: Something that is fungoid looks or grows like a fungus.

senses.collocation_zh: 真菌状增生物；真菌状外观

senses.sentence_zh: 潮湿的木头上覆盖着一层颜色浅淡的真菌状生长物。

etymology_story.zh: fungoid 由拉丁语 fungus（蘑菇、真菌）来源的词干 fung- 加上后缀 -oid 构成。-oid 最终源自希腊语中表示“形状、样貌”的成分，因此全词强调“形似真菌”。
etymology_story.en: Fungoid combines fung-, from Latin fungus meaning 'mushroom' or 'fungus', with the suffix -oid. This suffix ultimately comes from Greek elements expressing form or appearance, so the word emphasizes resemblance to a fungus.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：fung-（真菌）+ -oid（似……的）→ fungoid。主要同族词：fungus（真菌；复数 fungi 或 funguses）、fungal（真菌的）、fungous（真菌的或似真菌的）、fungicide（杀真菌剂）、fungicidal（杀真菌的）；这些词共享真菌词根，并非都由 fungoid 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: fung- 'fungus' + -oid 'resembling' → fungoid. Principal word-family members include fungus, plural fungi or funguses; fungal; fungous; fungicide; and fungicidal. These share the fungus root rather than all being derivatives of fungoid.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fungus-like（似真菌的）最直白，与 fungoid 接近；fungous（真菌的、似真菌的）较少见，意义有重叠；fungal（真菌的）通常表示与真菌有关或由真菌引起，不单指外形相似。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fungus-like is the clearest close equivalent; fungous is less common and overlaps in meaning; fungal normally means relating to or caused by fungi, without necessarily suggesting a fungus-like appearance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: fung-＝真菌，-oid＝像：像真菌一样。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Fung- means fungus; -oid means resembling: fungus-shaped or fungus-like.

meaning: 引信（使弹药在规定条件下起爆的装置）

pronunciation.note: 本卡美式读法只有一个音节 /fjuːz/，保留 /j/，末尾读浊音 /z/。

forms: 可数；复数 fuzes。fuse 是本义的另一拼法。
family: fuzed 装有引信的；fuzing 引信配置或装引信。

morphology.text: fuze + -ing → fuzing（装配引信这一活动，去掉末尾 e）；fuze 整词作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: fuze 是表示爆炸物引信的 fuse 的变体拼写；fuse 的这一名词义一般被认为缩自 fusee。助记时把 z 与装置名称的特殊拼写联系起来，不与电路保险丝混淆。

relations.meaning: 引信这一义项的另一拼法

usage_note: 本课 fuze 指弹药引信；电路里的保险丝通常写 fuse。

senses.meaning_zh: 引信；使弹药在规定条件下起爆的装置
senses.meaning_en: A device that initiates the explosion of ammunition under specified conditions.
senses.english_definition: A fuze is a device fitted to a bomb, shell, or other explosive weapon that makes it explode at a particular time or under particular conditions.
senses.collocation_en: proximity fuze; impact fuze
senses.collocation_zh: 近炸引信；触发引信
senses.sentence_en: The shell was fitted with a proximity fuze.
senses.sentence_zh: 这枚炮弹装有近炸引信。

senses.meaning_zh: 给弹药装引信
senses.meaning_en: To fit ammunition with a fuze.
senses.english_definition: If someone fuzes a bomb or shell, they fit it with a device that controls when or how it explodes.
senses.collocation_en: fuze a shell; fuzed ammunition
senses.collocation_zh: 给炮弹装引信；装有引信的弹药
senses.sentence_en: The report states that the shells had been fuzed before delivery.
senses.sentence_zh: 报告称，这些炮弹在交付前已经装好了引信。

etymology_story.zh: fuze 是爆炸物义 fuse 的变体拼写，常用于技术语境，以区别于电路中的保险丝。这个 fuse 通常被认为缩自 fusee，后者经法语 fusée 追溯至拉丁语 fusus（纺锤），与原先纺锤状物体及火药筒的形状有关。
etymology_story.en: Fuze is a variant spelling of the explosive-device sense of fuse, often used technically to distinguish it from an electrical fuse. This fuse is generally traced to fusee, through French fusée to Latin fusus 'spindle', reflecting the shape of objects and powder-filled tubes.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：fuze 是独立词基，不宜拆成更小的现代词素；名词转作动词表示“装引信”。屈折形式：fuzes（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、fuzed（过去式、过去分词）、fuzing（现在分词或动名词，去掉末尾 e）；相关拼写为 fuse、fused、fusing。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: fuze is an independent base with no productive internal division; conversion gives the verb meaning 'fit with a fuze'. Inflections are fuzes, fuzed, and fuzing, with final e dropped before -ing. Related alternative spellings include fuse, fused, and fusing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fuse 在爆炸物义上可与 fuze 对应，但也可指导火索或电路保险丝；detonator（雷管、起爆器）强调直接引发爆轰的部件；igniter（点火器）强调引燃，未必引起爆轰。动词 fuze 专指装引信，与泛指使弹药进入待发状态的 prime 并不完全相同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fuse can be an alternative spelling in the explosive sense, but also denotes a burning cord or an electrical safety component; detonator emphasizes the component that initiates detonation; igniter emphasizes starting combustion. As a verb, fuze specifically means fitting a fuze, whereas prime has the broader meaning of preparing something to function.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 fuze 记成弹药的“起爆条件控制器”；名词是引信，动词是装引信。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of a fuze as ammunition's explosion-condition controller: the noun names the device, and the verb means fitting it.

meaning: 地占术（借地面纹样或地形占卜）

pronunciation.note: 本卡美式读法首音节重读；开头 geo 分作 /dʒiːə/，-mancy 读 /mænsi/。

forms: 通常不可数。
family: geomancer 地占师；geomantic 地占术的。

morphology.text: geo-（地）+ -mancy（占卜）→ geomancy（地占术）。

etymology.text: 经中古英语、盎格鲁法语和中世纪拉丁语，追溯到晚期希腊语 geōmanteia。名称把“土地”和“占卜”连在一起。

usage_note: geomancy 是一种占卜传统，geology 是研究地球的科学，不能把二者当成同义词。

senses.meaning_zh: 地占术；通过土、沙或点画形成的图形进行占卜
senses.meaning_en: Divination by interpreting patterns formed in earth, sand, or arrangements of dots.
senses.english_definition: Geomancy is a way of trying to discover hidden information or predict events by interpreting patterns made in earth or sand, or patterns of dots.
senses.collocation_en: practise geomancy; a treatise on geomancy
senses.collocation_zh: 施行地占术；一部关于地占术的论著
senses.sentence_en: The manuscript explains how patterns of dots were interpreted in geomancy.
senses.sentence_zh: 这份手稿解释了地占术如何解读点画图形。

senses.meaning_zh: 堪舆；风水术，尤指根据地形等判断地点吉凶的传统方法
senses.meaning_en: Traditional assessment of the auspiciousness of places, especially in descriptions of feng shui.
senses.english_definition: Geomancy can also mean a traditional practice of examining land and its features to decide whether a place is suitable or auspicious for a building or burial.
senses.collocation_en: Chinese geomancy; principles of geomancy
senses.collocation_zh: 中国堪舆术；风水原理
senses.sentence_en: The historian studied the influence of Chinese geomancy on the location of tombs.
senses.sentence_zh: 这位历史学家研究了中国堪舆术对墓地选址的影响。

etymology_story.zh: geomancy 经法语和中世纪拉丁语传入英语，最终源自希腊语 geōmanteia，由“土地”和“占卜”两部分组成。它原指利用土沙或相关图形占卜，后来也被用于描述中国风水等与土地及选址有关的传统。
etymology_story.en: Geomancy entered English through French and medieval Latin, ultimately from Greek geōmanteia, combining 'earth' and 'divination'. It referred to divination using earth or associated patterns and was later also applied to land-based traditions such as Chinese feng shui.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：geo-（地、土地）+ -mancy（占卜）→ geomancy。主要派生词：geomancer（地占师、堪舆师）、geomantic（地占术的、堪舆的）、geomantical（较少见的形容词变体）、geomantically（以地占或堪舆方式）；派生时常出现 geomant- 这一词干形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: geo- 'earth' + -mancy 'divination' → geomancy. Principal derivatives are geomancer, geomantic, the less common adjective geomantical, and the adverb geomantically. The stem form geomant- appears in several derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: divination（占卜）是上位词，涵盖各种占卜方法；earth divination（土地占卜）是解释性的近义表达；feng shui（风水）只对应 geomancy 的部分用法，不能替代通过点画图形占卜的意义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Divination is the broader category covering many methods; earth divination is a close explanatory equivalent; feng shui corresponds to only some uses of geomancy and does not replace its meaning involving divinatory dot patterns.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: geo-＝地，-mancy＝占卜：从土地或地上的图形“读吉凶”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Geo- means earth and -mancy means divination: 'reading' fortunes from the ground or its patterns.

meaning: 正模标本（命名新物种时指定的单一模式标本）

pronunciation.note: 本卡读法重音在首段 /hoʊ/，o 读双元音；末段 type 读 /taɪp/。

forms: 可数；复数 holotypes。
family: holotypic 正模标本的；type specimen 模式标本。

morphology.text: holo-（完整的）+ type（模式、典型）→ holotype（正模标本）。

etymology.text: 现代生物分类术语，由希腊语来源的 holo- 和 type 组合而成；type 在这里承载“模式标本”的含义。记住描述新物种时指定的那一件标本。

usage_note: holotype 是正模标本，不是随便一件同种标本；paratype 指副模标本。

senses.meaning_zh: 正模；在原始命名时确立、作为物种或种下分类群名称依据的单一标本，某些植物命名情形下可为图示
senses.meaning_en: The single original name-bearing type of a species or infraspecific taxon, usually a specimen.
senses.english_definition: A holotype is the single specimen, or in certain botanical cases an illustration, established when a species or lower-ranking taxon is first named as the reference to which that name is attached.
senses.collocation_en: holotype specimen; designate a holotype
senses.collocation_zh: 正模标本；指定正模
senses.sentence_en: The holotype is preserved in the museum's collection.
senses.sentence_zh: 该正模标本保存在这家博物馆的馆藏中。

etymology_story.zh: holotype 是现代分类学术语，由希腊语来源的 holo-（完整、全部）与 type（模式）组合而成。type 最终源自希腊语 typos（印记、模型），在分类学中发展为固定名称适用范围的模式。
etymology_story.en: Holotype is a modern taxonomic formation combining Greek-derived holo- 'whole' with type. Type ultimately comes from Greek typos 'impression' or 'model' and acquired the taxonomic meaning of a reference that fixes the application of a name.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：holo-（完整、全部）+ type（模式）→ holotype；复数 holotypes，主要派生形容词为 holotypic（正模的）。相关术语包括 type specimen（模式标本）、isotype（等模式标本，主要用于植物学）和 paratype（副模标本），它们不是由 holotype 直接加词缀形成的。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: holo- 'whole' + type 'nomenclatural type' → holotype; the plural is holotypes, and a principal adjectival derivative is holotypic. Related terms include type specimen, isotype, chiefly in botany, and paratype; these are related formations rather than direct derivatives of holotype.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: type specimen（模式标本）是较宽泛的名称，正模只是模式标本的一种；name-bearing type（载名模式）强调固定名称的功能，但并非所有载名模式都是正模；paratype（副模标本）是原始描述所依据的其他标本之一，不能与正模互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Type specimen is broader, with a holotype being one kind of type specimen; name-bearing type emphasizes the function of fixing a name but also includes other categories; paratype refers to another specimen included in the original description and is not interchangeable with holotype.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把“整个名称的依据”锚定在一件原始模式上：holotype＝正模；它不一定是外形最典型的个体。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor the whole name to one original type: holotype. It need not be the most typical-looking individual.

pronunciation.note: 本卡美式读法主重音在 carbon 的 /kɑːr/；hydro 开头读 /haɪ/，ch 读 /k/。

forms: 可数；复数 hydrochlorofluorocarbons；常缩写为 HCFC。
family: HCFC 氢氯氟烃的缩写；chlorofluorocarbon 氯氟烃。

morphology.text: hydro-（氢）+ chloro-（氯）+ fluoro-（氟）+ carbon（碳）→ hydrochlorofluorocarbon（氢氯氟烃）。

usage_note: hydrochlorofluorocarbon 含氢；chlorofluorocarbon 不含名称开头的 hydro-。本课只辨认化合物类别。

etymology_story.zh: hydrochlorofluorocarbon 是现代化学复合名称，用氢、氯、氟和碳的名称成分表示其元素组成。这里的 hydro- 表示氢，而不是日常构词中常见的“水”。
etymology_story.en: Hydrochlorofluorocarbon is a modern chemical compound name that identifies its hydrogen, chlorine, fluorine, and carbon components. Here hydro- refers to hydrogen rather than its familiar general meaning of water.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：hydro-（氢）+ chloro-（氯）+ fluoro-（氟）+ carbon（碳）→ hydrochlorofluorocarbon。复数为 hydrochlorofluorocarbons；缩写为 HCFC，缩写复数为 HCFCs；没有常用的专属形容词或动词派生形式，作名词定语时词性仍是名词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: hydro- 'hydrogen' + chloro- 'chlorine' + fluoro- 'fluorine' + carbon → hydrochlorofluorocarbon. The plural is hydrochlorofluorocarbons; the abbreviation is HCFC, plural HCFCs. There are no common dedicated adjective or verb derivatives; attributive use remains nominal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: HCFC 是同一名称的标准缩写。相关但并非同义的 CFC（氯氟烃）不含氢，HFC（氢氟烃）不含氯；这三个类别不能互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: HCFC is the standard abbreviation for the same term. The related terms CFC, chlorofluorocarbon, and HFC, hydrofluorocarbon, are not synonyms: CFCs lack hydrogen, while HFCs lack chlorine.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 顺着名称数元素：氢—氯—氟—碳；HCFC 的四个字母也依次对应这四种元素名称。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Read the elements in order: hydrogen—chlorine—fluorine—carbon; HCFC follows the same sequence.

senses.meaning_zh: 肠梗阻；现代临床用语中通常指肠蠕动停滞造成的功能性肠梗阻
senses.meaning_en: Intestinal obstruction, especially failure of intestinal contents to move because bowel activity has stopped.
senses.english_definition: Ileus is a condition in which material cannot move normally through the intestine, usually because the intestinal muscles have stopped working properly.
senses.collocation_en: postoperative ileus; paralytic ileus
senses.collocation_zh: 术后肠麻痹；麻痹性肠梗阻
senses.sentence_en: The patient developed ileus after abdominal surgery.
senses.sentence_zh: 患者在腹部手术后出现了肠麻痹。

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自拉丁语 ileus，后者源于希腊语 eileos，表示一种肠道病症，传统上与表示“卷绕、扭转”的希腊语动词相联系。这个名称最初用于肠道阻塞性病症，现代临床用法通常侧重肠动力停止所致的梗阻。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed ileus from Latin, which took it from Greek eileos, a name for an intestinal disorder traditionally connected with a Greek verb meaning 'to roll or twist.' Originally associated with obstructive bowel conditions, the term now commonly emphasizes obstruction caused by loss of intestinal movement.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，ileus 是整体借入的医学名词，不能按 ile + -us 拆解来推导词义。它通常作不可数名词，没有常用的直接派生词；ileus-like（类似肠梗阻的）是临时构成的复合形容词。ileal（回肠的）来自 ileum（回肠），不是 ileus 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, ileus is a borrowed medical noun treated as a whole, rather than a meaningful combination of ile + -us. It is usually uncountable and has no common direct derivatives; ileus-like is a freely formed compound adjective. Ileal derives from ileum, not from ileus.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: intestinal obstruction（肠梗阻）是较宽泛的名称，可包括机械性和功能性梗阻；paralytic ileus（麻痹性肠梗阻）明确强调肠蠕动丧失；intestinal pseudo-obstruction（肠假性梗阻）指无机械性堵塞却出现梗阻表现的相关病症，并非在所有语境中都与 ileus 等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Intestinal obstruction is a broader term covering mechanical and functional causes; paralytic ileus specifically emphasizes loss of bowel movement; intestinal pseudo-obstruction describes a related condition with obstructive symptoms but no mechanical blockage and is not interchangeable with ileus in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“肠道停止输送”的画面：通道可能没有堵住，内容物却不再前进。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the bowel's conveyor belt stopping: the passage may be open, but its contents no longer move forward.

pronunciation.note: 本卡美式读法主重音在 chem 的 /kem/；ch 读 /k/，前面的 /noʊ/ 不作主重音。

forms: 学科名，通常不可数。

morphology.text: immuno-（免疫）+ chemistry（化学）→ immunochemistry（免疫化学）。

etymology.text: 现代英语科学术语，由免疫组合形式 immuno- 与 chemistry 构成，表示从化学角度研究免疫现象。把它记成免疫学与化学的交会处。

usage_note: immunochemistry 聚焦免疫现象的化学方面，immunology 是范围更广的免疫学。

senses.meaning_zh: 免疫化学；研究免疫系统成分及免疫反应的化学性质的学科
senses.meaning_en: The study of the chemical properties of immune-system components and reactions.
senses.english_definition: Immunochemistry is the scientific study of the chemical nature of substances involved in immunity and the reactions between them.
senses.collocation_en: immunochemistry techniques; research in immunochemistry
senses.collocation_zh: 免疫化学技术；免疫化学研究
senses.sentence_en: Her research in immunochemistry focuses on how antibodies bind to antigens.
senses.sentence_zh: 她的免疫化学研究主要关注抗体如何与抗原结合。

etymology_story.zh: 这是由 immuno-（免疫）与 chemistry（化学）组成的现代科学术语，反映了用化学方法研究抗体、抗原及其反应的发展。immuno- 最终源自拉丁语 immunis，原义为“免除义务或负担的”，后来发展出不受疾病侵害的含义。
etymology_story.en: This modern scientific term combines immuno- with chemistry, reflecting the development of chemical approaches to antibodies, antigens, and their reactions. Immuno- ultimately comes from Latin immunis, meaning 'exempt from duties or burdens,' which later acquired the medical idea of protection from disease.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：immuno-（免疫组合形式）+ chemistry（化学）→ immunochemistry（免疫化学）。直接词族包括 immunochemical（免疫化学的）、immunochemically（以免疫化学方式）和 immunochemist（免疫化学研究者）；相关基础词族包括 immune（免疫的）、immunity（免疫力）、immunology（免疫学）以及 chemist（化学家）、chemical（化学的；化学物质）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: immuno- (the combining form for immunity) + chemistry → immunochemistry. Direct family members include immunochemical, immunochemically, and immunochemist; related base families include immune, immunity, and immunology, together with chemist and chemical.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chemical immunology（化学免疫学）是接近的描述性表达；immunology（免疫学）范围更广，涵盖整个免疫系统；immunobiochemistry（免疫生物化学）侧重免疫过程的生物化学机制，与 immunochemistry 有较大重叠，但并非处处可互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chemical immunology is a close descriptive equivalent; immunology covers the immune system more broadly; immunobiochemistry emphasizes the biochemical mechanisms of immune processes and overlaps substantially with immunochemistry without always being interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: immuno- 管免疫，chemistry 管化学：用化学解释免疫。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Immuno- means immunity and chemistry means chemistry: explain immunity through chemistry.

pronunciation.note: 本卡美式读法重音在 /fæn/，元音为 /æ/；末尾 /tə/ 轻读。

forms: 可数；复数 infantas。

morphology.text: infant-（西班牙语 infante 的称号词干）+ -a（阴性词尾）→ infanta（王室女性称号）。

etymology.text: 从西班牙语、葡萄牙语借入，是王室称号 infante 的女性形式。记住它是特定王室传统里的女儿称号，不是英语 infant“婴儿”。

usage_note: infanta 指西班牙或葡萄牙王室的女性称号；泛指公主用 princess。称号放在人名前常大写，如 Infanta Elena。

senses.meaning_en: A title for a female member of the Spanish or former Portuguese royal family, especially a monarch's daughter who is not the heiress apparent.
senses.english_definition: An infanta is a princess of the Spanish or former Portuguese royal family, especially a daughter of the monarch who does not hold the title of heiress apparent.

etymology_story.zh: 英语从西班牙语和葡萄牙语借入 infanta，它是王室称号 infante 的阴性形式。这个词最终源于拉丁语 infans（不会说话的；幼儿），后来在伊比利亚王室传统中专门用于君主的子女，因此与英语 infant 同源，但并不表示“女婴”。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed infanta from Spanish and Portuguese as the feminine counterpart of the royal title infante. It ultimately comes from Latin infans, meaning 'unable to speak' and hence 'young child,' which developed a specialized royal use in Iberia; it is therefore related to English infant but does not mean 'female baby.'

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 infanta 作为完整的借入名词使用，复数为 infantas。源语言中的形式关系可表示为 infant-（称号词干）+ -a（阴性词尾），但 -a 在这里不是英语中可自由套用的派生后缀；对应男性称号为 infante，复数为 infantes。英语中没有常用的直接形容词或动词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats infanta as a complete borrowed noun, with the plural infantas. Its source-language structure can be represented as infant- (the title stem) + -a (a feminine ending), but -a is not a freely productive English suffix here; the corresponding male title is infante, plural infantes. There are no common direct adjective or verb derivatives in English.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: princess（公主；王妃）是范围更广的王室称号，可来自血统或婚姻；royal daughter（君主之女）只描述亲属关系，不一定是正式称号；infanta 则带有特定的西班牙及历史上葡萄牙王室制度背景。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Princess is a broader royal title acquired through birth or marriage; royal daughter describes a family relationship without necessarily naming a formal title; infanta identifies a title within Spanish and historical Portuguese royal traditions.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“王家的孩子”记到“王家的女儿”：infanta 是王室称号，同源于 infant，却不受婴儿年龄限制。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Move from 'royal child' to 'royal daughter': infanta shares its ancestry with infant, but the title is not limited to babies.

senses.meaning_zh: 富豪名流圈的；具有频繁国际旅行和奢华社交生活特点的，通常拼作 jet-set
senses.meaning_en: Relating to wealthy international travellers and their fashionable, luxurious way of life, usually spelled jet-set.
senses.english_definition: A jet-set lifestyle or social world involves wealthy people travelling frequently to fashionable places around the world.
senses.collocation_en: a jet-set lifestyle; the jet-set crowd
senses.collocation_zh: 频繁飞往各地享乐的奢华生活方式；国际富豪名流群体
senses.sentence_en: The magazine offers a glimpse of her jet-set lifestyle.

senses.meaning_zh: 作为富豪名流频繁乘飞机到各地游乐，也拼作 jet-set
senses.meaning_en: To travel frequently by air for pleasure as part of a wealthy, fashionable lifestyle, also spelled jet-set.
senses.english_definition: If someone jetsets, they travel frequently by plane to fashionable places for holidays and social events.
senses.collocation_en: jetset around the world; jetset between London and New York
senses.collocation_zh: 乘飞机到世界各地游乐；频繁乘飞机往返伦敦和纽约参加社交或休闲活动
senses.sentence_en: She spent her twenties jetsetting around the world.
senses.sentence_zh: 她二十多岁时经常乘飞机到世界各地游乐。

etymology_story.zh: jet set 在二十世纪中叶随着喷气式航空旅行的发展而流行，由 jet（喷气式飞机）和 set（社交圈）组成，指能够经常飞往各国享乐的富裕群体。这个名词表达随后也产生了形容词用法和表示这种旅行生活方式的动词用法。
etymology_story.en: Jet set became popular in the mid-twentieth century as jet travel developed, combining jet with set in the sense of a social circle to describe wealthy international pleasure travellers. The noun expression subsequently developed adjectival and verbal uses.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：jet（喷气式飞机）+ set（社交圈）→ jet set／jet-set／jetset。名词通常写作 jet set，形容词通常写作 jet-set，动词可写作 jet-set 或 jetset；相关形式包括 jet-setter／jetsetter（经常乘飞机四处游乐的名流）和 jet-setting／jetsetting（这种旅行活动；过这种生活的）。动词常见屈折形式为 jetsets、jetsetting、jetsetted，带连字符的拼法相应为 jet-sets、jet-setting、jet-setted。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: jet (a jet aircraft) + set (a social circle) → jet set / jet-set / jetset. The noun is usually jet set, the adjective usually jet-set, and the verb may be jet-set or jetset; related forms include jet-setter / jetsetter and jet-setting / jetsetting. Common verb inflections are jetsets, jetsetting, and jetsetted, or the corresponding hyphenated forms jet-sets, jet-setting, and jet-setted.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: high society（上流社会）强调社会地位与社交圈，不要求经常旅行；glitterati（名流显贵）强调引人注目的名气与魅力；globetrotters（环球旅行者）强调周游世界，本身不表示富有或属于上流社会。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: High society emphasizes social rank and elite connections without requiring frequent travel; glitterati emphasizes glamorous, conspicuous celebrities; globetrotters travel widely but need not be wealthy or socially prominent.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: jet 是飞机，set 是圈子：一个靠飞机串起全球聚会的富豪圈。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Jet means aircraft and set means social circle: a wealthy circle whose parties are connected by flights.

senses.meaning_zh: 脏兮兮的；破旧难看的；令人嫌弃的，主要用于英国非正式口语
senses.meaning_en: Dirty, shabby, or unpleasant, chiefly in informal British English.
senses.english_definition: If something is manky, it is dirty, in poor condition, or unpleasant to look at or touch.
senses.collocation_en: a manky old towel; manky trainers
senses.collocation_zh: 一条脏兮兮的旧毛巾；脏旧的运动鞋
senses.sentence_en: He left a pair of manky trainers by the front door.
senses.sentence_zh: 他把一双脏兮兮的旧运动鞋放在了前门旁。

etymology_story.zh: manky 在二十世纪中叶的英国非正式英语中出现，其确切来源尚不确定。有的词源解释将它经由 Polari 俚语追溯到意大利语 mancare（缺少、不足），也有解释将它与法语 manqué（未成功的、有欠缺的）联系起来；现代词义集中于脏、破旧或令人不快。
etymology_story.en: Manky appeared in informal British English in the mid-twentieth century, but its precise origin is uncertain. Some accounts trace it through Polari slang to Italian mancare, 'to lack,' while others connect it with French manqué, 'unsuccessful or deficient'; its modern meanings centre on dirtiness, shabbiness, and unpleasantness.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 manky 作为整体形容词记忆，没有可可靠独立释义的现代词根 mank-。常见比较级为 mankier，最高级为 mankiest；名词 mankiness 表示“脏旧或令人嫌弃的状态”。manky-looking（看起来脏旧的）是可以临时构成的复合形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, manky is best treated as a whole adjective, without assigning an independent meaning to a supposed root mank-. Its comparative and superlative are mankier and mankiest; the noun mankiness names the quality of being dirty, shabby, or unpleasant. Manky-looking is a freely formed compound adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: grubby（脏兮兮的）主要强调表面有污垢；filthy（极脏的）强调污秽程度很重；shabby（破旧的）强调磨损和外观失修，而 manky 常把脏旧与令人嫌弃的感觉合在一起。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Grubby mainly suggests surface dirt; filthy indicates a much greater degree of dirtiness; shabby emphasizes wear and a neglected appearance, whereas manky often combines poor condition with a feeling of disgust.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想象一条又脏又旧、让你不想碰的毛巾：manky 把“脏旧”和“嫌弃感”连在一起。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a dirty old towel you do not want to touch: manky links poor condition with disgust.

usage_note: menorrhagia 侧重月经出血过多；amenorrhea 指闭经，两者不是同一病症。

senses.meaning_zh: 月经过多；经血量异常多或经期异常延长
senses.meaning_en: Abnormally heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding.
senses.english_definition: Menorrhagia is a condition in which menstrual bleeding is unusually heavy or lasts unusually long.
senses.collocation_en: heavy menstrual bleeding; treatment of menorrhagia
senses.collocation_zh: 月经过多；月经过多的治疗
senses.sentence_en: She consulted her doctor about persistent menorrhagia.
senses.sentence_zh: 她因持续月经过多而向医生求诊。

etymology_story.zh: 该词通过新拉丁语医学词汇进入英语，由源自希腊语的 meno-（月经，与“月份”有关）和 -rrhagia（大量流出）组成。后一个成分最终与希腊语表示“破裂、迸出”的动词有关，整个词用于描述异常多或异常持久的月经出血。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through medical New Latin, combining Greek-derived meno-, referring to menstruation and ultimately to a month, with -rrhagia, meaning an excessive discharge. The latter element ultimately relates to a Greek verb meaning 'to burst,' and the compound denotes unusually heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代医学构词：meno-（月经）+ -rrhagia（大量流出、出血）→ menorrhagia。直接派生词：menorrhagic（形容词，月经过多的）；相关构词成分见于 menorrhea（月经来潮）和 hemorrhage（出血），后二者属于构词相关词，并非本词的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern medical formation: meno- 'menstruation' + -rrhagia 'excessive discharge or bleeding' → menorrhagia. Its direct adjective is menorrhagic. Related combining forms occur in menorrhea 'menstrual flow' and hemorrhage 'bleeding'; these are structurally related words rather than direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: heavy menstrual bleeding 是直白、常用的临床表达，强调经血过多；hypermenorrhea 是较传统的医学近义词，也主要强调出血量多。menorrhagia 的传统用法还可包含经期异常延长。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Heavy menstrual bleeding is a plain, commonly used clinical expression emphasizing excessive menstrual blood loss. Hypermenorrhea is a more traditional medical near-synonym with a similar emphasis. Traditional uses of menorrhagia can also include unusually prolonged menstruation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: meno- 锁定“月经”，-rrhagia 提示“迸出、过量流出”：月经出血过多。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Meno- identifies menstruation; -rrhagia suggests bursting or excessive discharge: excessive menstrual bleeding.

usage_note: mucopolysaccharide 是一类复杂糖链的旧称，现代也称 glycosaminoglycan；不是单糖。

senses.meaning_zh: 黏多糖；尤指现通常称为糖胺聚糖的一类长链糖分子
senses.meaning_en: A complex carbohydrate of a group now generally called glycosaminoglycans.
senses.english_definition: A mucopolysaccharide is a long-chain carbohydrate found especially in connective tissues and mucus, belonging to a group now generally called glycosaminoglycans.
senses.collocation_en: acid mucopolysaccharides; mucopolysaccharide accumulation
senses.collocation_zh: 酸性黏多糖；黏多糖蓄积
senses.sentence_en: The older textbook describes hyaluronic acid as a mucopolysaccharide.
senses.sentence_zh: 这本较早的教科书将透明质酸描述为一种黏多糖。

etymology_story.zh: 该词是二十世纪的科学构词，由 muco-（源自拉丁语 mucus，意为“黏液”）与 polysaccharide（多糖）组合而成，反映这类物质最初与黏液样材料的联系。后来，对其中主要分子类别的命名逐渐转用更能体现化学结构的 glycosaminoglycan（糖胺聚糖）。
etymology_story.en: This twentieth-century scientific formation combines muco-, from Latin mucus 'slime or mucus,' with polysaccharide, reflecting the substances' association with mucus-like materials. Glycosaminoglycan later became the preferred name for the principal molecular class, describing its chemical structure more specifically.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：muco-（黏液）+ polysaccharide（多糖）；后者可分析为 poly-（多）+ saccharide（糖类）。复数：mucopolysaccharides；相关疾病名：mucopolysaccharidosis（黏多糖贮积症），复数 mucopolysaccharidoses；基础词族包括 saccharide、polysaccharide 和 polysaccharidic（多糖的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: muco- 'mucus' + polysaccharide, itself poly- 'many' + saccharide 'sugar compound.' The plural is mucopolysaccharides. A related disease term is mucopolysaccharidosis, plural mucopolysaccharidoses. The underlying family includes saccharide, polysaccharide, and polysaccharidic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: glycosaminoglycan（糖胺聚糖）是现代通常采用的对应名称；acid mucopolysaccharide（酸性黏多糖）是强调酸性特征的传统名称；polysaccharide（多糖）是上位词，范围更广，并不限于黏多糖。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Glycosaminoglycan is the usual modern corresponding term. Acid mucopolysaccharide is a traditional expression emphasizing acidic properties. Polysaccharide is a broader category that includes many carbohydrates outside this group.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: muco- 想到黏液，poly- 想到很多，saccharide 想到糖：许多糖单元连成具有黏液样特性的长链。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Muco- suggests mucus, poly- means many, and saccharide means sugar: many sugar units forming a mucus-associated chain.

senses.meaning_zh: 脑袋；头脑，思考能力（诙谐、略显旧式，尤见于英式英语）
senses.meaning_en: A person's head or ability to think, used humorously, especially in dated British English.
senses.english_definition: Your noddle is your head, especially when someone is talking humorously about your ability to think.
senses.collocation_en: use your noddle; an old noddle
senses.collocation_zh: 动动脑筋；老脑袋
senses.sentence_en: Use your noddle and work it out for yourself.
senses.sentence_zh: 动动脑筋，自己把它想明白。

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自中古英语 nodel，早期指后脑或颈背部，更早的来源并不确定。其意义后来扩展为整个脑袋，并产生了诙谐地指称思考能力的用法。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Middle English nodel, which referred to the back of the head or the nape; its earlier origin is uncertain. Its meaning later broadened to the whole head and, humorously, to a person's thinking ability.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 noddle 视为不可再作有效词缀分析的单纯词，不宜拆成 nod + -dle。复数为 noddles；没有常用的直接派生词；noddle-like（像脑袋的）属于可以临时组成的表达，并非核心词族成员。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, noddle is a simple lexical base without a productive internal affix analysis; it is not usefully divided into nod + -dle. Its plural is noddles. It has no common direct derivatives; noddle-like is a possible occasional formation rather than a core family member.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: head 是中性、通用的“头”；noggin 是较随意、诙谐的“脑袋”；brain 更直接指大脑或智力。noddle 兼有“脑袋”和“动脑能力”的意味，语气尤其俏皮、略显旧式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Head is neutral and general. Noggin is informal and humorous. Brain refers more directly to the organ or intellectual ability. Noddle combines the ideas of head and thinking with a particularly playful, somewhat old-fashioned tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“后脑”到“整个脑袋”，再到“动脑筋”：use your noddle。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the meaning from the back of the head to the whole head, then to thinking: use your noddle.

meaning: 诺奈日（古罗马历中的一个固定日期）

pronunciation.note: 本卡美式读法只有一个音节 /noʊnz/；o 读 /oʊ/，末尾 s 读浊音 /z/。

forms: 形式以 -s 结尾，作日期名称可用单数结构；不再另加复数 -s。
family: 相关日期名：calends 月首日；ides 伊德斯日。

morphology.text: non-（拉丁语 nonus“第九”的词干）+ -ae（阴性复数词尾）→ nonae（经法语成为 nones）；现代英语把 nones 作为完整日期名记忆。

etymology.text: 经中古英语 nonys 和盎格鲁法语 nones，来自拉丁语 nonae，关联 nonus“第九”。古罗马按包含首尾的方式计数，把它定位为 ides 前的第九天。

usage_note: 这里 nones 是古罗马历日期，不是 none“没有一个”的普通复数；它也另有宗教时辰义，本课不考。

senses.meaning_zh: 诺奈日；古罗马历三、五、七、十月的第七日，其他月份的第五日
senses.meaning_en: The seventh day of March, May, July, and October, and the fifth day of other months in the ancient Roman calendar.

senses.meaning_zh: 第九时辰经；传统上约在下午三时举行的基督教日课祈祷
senses.meaning_en: A Christian canonical prayer office traditionally associated with the ninth hour of daylight.
senses.english_definition: Nones is a Christian prayer service traditionally said at the ninth hour of daylight, approximately three in the afternoon.
senses.collocation_en: say nones; the office of nones
senses.collocation_zh: 诵念第九时辰经；第九时辰日课
senses.sentence_en: The monks gathered in the chapel to say nones.
senses.sentence_zh: 修士们聚集在小圣堂里诵念第九时辰经。

senses.meaning_zh: 无宗教归属者；在调查中选择“无宗教”的人（复数）
senses.meaning_en: People who report having no religious affiliation.
senses.english_definition: Nones are people who identify with no religion, especially when answering a survey about religious affiliation.
senses.collocation_en: religious nones; the rise of the nones
senses.collocation_zh: 无宗教归属者；无宗教归属人群的增加
senses.sentence_en: The survey grouped atheists, agnostics, and other unaffiliated respondents together as nones.
senses.sentence_zh: 该调查将无神论者、不可知论者和其他无宗教归属的受访者统称为无宗教归属者。

etymology_story.zh: 历法义经法语来自拉丁语 nonae，与 nonus（第九）有关，因为罗马人连首尾一起计算，将该日算作 ides（望日）之前的第九天；日课义则来自拉丁语 nona hora（第九时辰）。现代“无宗教归属者”义独立产生于英语 none，源于宗教调查中的“无”这一回答。
etymology_story.en: The calendar sense came through French from Latin nonae, related to nonus 'ninth,' because inclusive Roman counting placed it nine days before the ides; the prayer sense comes from Latin nona hora 'ninth hour.' The modern religious-affiliation sense arose independently from English none, reflecting a survey answer.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历法义和日课义在现代英语中均宜整体记忆；这里的 non- 不是表示否定的前缀。无宗教归属义则为 none（无；无宗教归属的人）+ 复数词尾 -s → nones，单数通常表达为 a religious none；三个义项没有共同的常用派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: The calendar and prayer senses are best learned as whole lexical forms; their non- is not the negative prefix. The religious-affiliation sense is none 'no affiliation; an unaffiliated person' + plural -s → nones, with a singular commonly phrased as a religious none. The three senses have no shared productive derivative family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 日课义的对应表达是 None 或 the ninth-hour office（第九时辰日课）；无宗教归属义可用 the religiously unaffiliated，强调没有宗教归属，而 nonbelievers 强调不信教，范围并不完全相同。历法义没有常用的精确英语同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the prayer sense, None and the ninth-hour office are corresponding expressions. For the affiliation sense, the religiously unaffiliated emphasizes lack of affiliation, whereas nonbelievers emphasizes lack of belief and is not fully equivalent. The calendar sense has no common exact English synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 读 /noʊnz/ 时联想“第九”：望日前的第九天或第九时辰；读 /nʌnz/ 时联想调查选项 none：“没有宗教归属”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: For /noʊnz/, think 'ninth': nine days before the ides or the ninth prayer hour. For /nʌnz/, think of the survey answer none: no religious affiliation.

meaning: 操纵子（一组共同受调控、转录的基因及调控元件）

pronunciation.note: 本卡美式读法首音节重读，开头读 /ɑː/；中间 /pə/ 轻读，末段 /rɑːn/ 次重读。

forms: 可数；复数 operons。
family: operonic 操纵子的；operator 操纵序列。

morphology.text: oper-（法语 opérer 的词干，运作）+ -on（科学名词后缀）→ operon（操纵子）。

etymology.text: 借自法语 opéron，由 opérer“使运作、产生作用”和 -on 构成；opérer 又可追溯到拉丁语表示“工作”的词。把协同运作的一组基因当作记忆画面。

usage_note: operon 是一组基因和调控元件组成的单位；operator 是其中的一种调控序列，不等于整个操纵子。

senses.meaning_zh: 操纵子；由共同受调控并作为一个转录单位表达的基因及相关调控序列构成的遗传单位
senses.meaning_en: A genetic unit containing genes transcribed together under shared regulatory control.
senses.english_definition: An operon is a group of genes and associated regulatory DNA sequences that allow the genes to be controlled together and transcribed into a single RNA molecule.
senses.collocation_en: the lac operon; operon expression
senses.collocation_zh: 乳糖操纵子；操纵子的表达
senses.sentence_en: The lac operon contains genes involved in lactose metabolism.
senses.sentence_zh: 乳糖操纵子包含参与乳糖代谢的基因。

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自法语 opéron，是二十世纪中叶分子遗传学发展过程中形成的术语，与雅各布和莫诺提出的基因调控模型密切相关。其命名与 operator（操纵区）这一术语及科学名词中表示单位的 -on 相联系，用来表示共同受控的遗传功能单位。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from French opéron, a term established during the development of molecular genetics in the mid-twentieth century and closely associated with Jacob and Monod's model of gene regulation. Its formation connects with operator and the scientific unit-forming ending -on, naming a jointly controlled genetic unit.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 operon 通常作为完整的专业词基使用；其术语构词可联系 oper-（与 operator 有关）+ -on（科学单位名词成分）。复数为 operons；直接派生形容词为 operonic（操纵子的）；常见复合表达有 lac operon（乳糖操纵子）和 trp operon（色氨酸操纵子）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, operon normally functions as a complete technical base; its terminological formation can be related to oper- from operator + the scientific unit-forming element -on. Its plural is operons, and its direct adjective is operonic. Common compounds include lac operon and trp operon.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: transcription unit（转录单位）强调由一次转录产生 RNA 的 DNA 区段，范围不完全等同于操纵子；gene cluster（基因簇）只要求基因在位置上聚集，不一定共同转录；regulon（调控子）指受同一调控机制控制的一组基因或操纵子，可以分布在不同位置。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Transcription unit emphasizes the DNA region copied into an RNA transcript and does not have exactly the same scope as operon. Gene cluster describes neighboring genes without necessarily implying shared transcription. Regulon denotes genes or operons controlled by the same regulatory system, potentially at separate locations.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 operon 想成“统一操控的一组基因”：共用调控开关，合成一条共同的 RNA 转录本。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture an operon as a jointly operated gene group: shared regulatory switches produce one common RNA transcript.

pronunciation.note: 本卡美式读法重音在 /deɪ/；中间 a 读双元音 /eɪ/，末尾 /nəs/ 轻读。

forms: 可数；复数 pandani；也有指叶纤维的物质名用法。
family: 相关词：screw pine 露兜树的俗名；pandan 与其名称同源。

morphology.text: pandan-（马来语 pandan，露兜树）+ -us（拉丁化名词词尾）→ pandanus（露兜树）。

etymology.text: 英语借自新拉丁语植物属名，属名取自马来语 pandan“露兜树”。想象热带海岸上长着长叶片的树，就能把借词和场景连起来。

usage_note: 本课 pandanus 指植物；在材料语境中也可指用其叶制成的纤维。普通名小写，植物学属名 Pandanus 大写。

senses.meaning_en: a tropical tree or shrub of the genus Pandanus
senses.english_definition: A pandanus is a tropical tree or shrub that has long, narrow leaves, often arranged in spirals, and often develops supporting roots above the ground.
senses.collocation_en: pandanus leaves; pandanus palms
senses.collocation_zh: 露兜树叶；露兜树（外形似棕榈，但并非棕榈）
senses.sentence_en: The villagers wove pandanus leaves into mats and baskets.
senses.sentence_zh: 村民们用露兜树叶编织席子和篮子。

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自新拉丁语植物属名 Pandanus，该名称以马来语 pandan 为基础，加上拉丁化词尾。它后来也作为普通名词，指这一属中的树木或灌木。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the botanical New Latin genus name Pandanus, formed from Malay pandan with a Latinized ending. The name also became a common noun for trees and shrubs belonging to that genus.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常将 pandanus 视为整体借词；历史结构为 pandan（马来语植物名）+ -us（拉丁化词尾）。相关形式：pandan（相关植物及其芳香叶片的名称）、pandanuses（规则复数）；Pandanus 是属名，Pandanaceae 是露兜树科的学名，并非普通英语派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats pandanus as an undivided loanword; its historical structure is pandan, a Malay plant name, + the Latinized ending -us. Related forms include pandan, used for related plants and their aromatic leaves, and the regular plural pandanuses. Pandanus is the genus name, and Pandanaceae is the botanical family name rather than an ordinary English derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: screw pine（露兜树）是常见俗名，突出螺旋排列的叶片，但这种植物并非松树；pandan（香露兜等植物及其叶片）在烹饪语境中通常特指提供芳香叶片的种类，范围比 pandanus 窄。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Screw pine is a common name referring to the spiral arrangement of the leaves, although the plant is not a pine. Pandan, especially in cooking, usually refers more narrowly to plants grown for their aromatic leaves.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: pandan 是植物本名，-us 是拉丁化外衣：想象热带海岸上长着螺旋长叶和支柱根的露兜树。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pandan is the plant name, and -us gives it a Latinized form: picture a tropical coastal tree with spiralling leaves and supporting roots.

meaning: 迷情药（传说中能激起爱意的药剂）

pronunciation.note: 本卡美式读法首音节重读；ph 读 /f/，元音是短音 /ɪ/，词尾读 /tər/。

forms: 可数；复数 philtres；美式常写 philter。
family: philter 美式拼法；love potion 迷情药。

morphology.text: phil-（爱，源自希腊语）+ -tron（表示工具的词尾）→ philtron（经拉丁语、法语演变为 philtre）；现代拼写整体记忆。

etymology.text: 经中古法语 philtre、拉丁语 philtrum，追溯到希腊语 philtron，与表示“亲爱的、喜爱的”的 philos 有联系。记成传说中让人坠入爱河的药剂。

usage_note: philtre 常见于传说、文学或歌剧，不是对真实药效的说明；一般的药水或魔药可用 potion。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语 philtre、拉丁语 philtrum，最终源于希腊语 philtron，意为使人产生爱意的药剂或魅惑物。它与希腊语表示爱或亲爱的词根有关，因此在英语中主要保留了传说中“爱情魔药”的含义。
etymology_story.en: The word came through French philtre and Latin philtrum from Greek philtron, a love-inducing potion or charm. Its Greek base is associated with love or affection, and English chiefly preserves the legendary meaning of a love potion.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 philtre 视为整体借词，不能按现有拼写机械拆分；历史上可联系希腊语 phil-（爱）和 -tron（表示工具或手段的成分）。常用相关形式：philter（美式拼写）、philtres／philters（复数）；没有常用的现代派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats philtre as an undivided loanword rather than a transparently constructed word. Historically, it is associated with Greek phil-, relating to love, and -tron, an element indicating an instrument or means. Common related forms are the American spelling philter and the plurals philtres and philters; there is no common modern derivative family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: love potion（迷情药）最直接明确，通常可替换 philtre；potion（药水、魔药）范围更广，不一定与爱情有关；charm（魔咒、护符）可以指产生魔力的咒语或物件，不一定是饮剂。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Love potion is the clearest direct equivalent. Potion is broader and need not involve love. Charm can mean a magical spell or object and does not necessarily refer to a drink.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: phil- 联系“爱”：philtre 就是故事里让人产生爱意的那杯魔药。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect phil- with love: a philtre is the storybook drink that creates affection.

pronunciation.note: 本卡读法主重音在首段 /piː/，随后 /ə/ 轻读；-nism 读 /nɪzəm/，s 发 /z/。

forms: 抽象名词，通常不可数。
family: pianistic 钢琴演奏的；pianist 钢琴家；piano 钢琴。

morphology.text: pian-（piano 的词干）+ -ism（表示技艺或实践的名词后缀）→ pianism（钢琴演奏技艺）。

etymology.text: 十九世纪英语以 piano 的词干接 -ism 构成，表示弹钢琴的艺术或技术。记住评论家评价的是演奏功力，而不是乐器本身。

usage_note: pianism 指钢琴演奏的艺术或技术；piano 是乐器，pianist 是演奏者。常见于乐评。

senses.english_definition: Pianism is the art or technique of playing the piano, especially the skill and style shown by a particular performer.

etymology_story.zh: pianism 于十九世纪进入英语，由 piano 的词干形式与 -ism 构成，用来指钢琴演奏的艺术或技法。piano 本身是意大利语 pianoforte 的缩略形式，原名体现了这种乐器能奏出轻重不同的音量。
etymology_story.en: Pianism entered English in the nineteenth century, formed from a stem of piano with -ism to name the art or technique of piano playing. Piano itself shortens Italian pianoforte, whose name reflects the instrument's ability to produce both soft and loud sounds.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词可记为 pian(o) + -ism → pianism，其中 piano 在这一形式中去掉末尾的 o。主要词族：piano（钢琴）、pianos（复数）、pianist（钢琴演奏者）、pianists（复数）、pianistic（钢琴演奏的；适合钢琴演奏的）、pianistically（从钢琴演奏角度；以钢琴演奏方式）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern formation can be represented as pian(o) + -ism → pianism, with the final o of piano omitted in this form. The main family includes piano, plural pianos; pianist, plural pianists; pianistic, relating or suited to piano playing; and pianistically, meaning in terms of piano playing or in a pianistic manner.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: piano playing（弹钢琴、钢琴演奏）最中性，可指一般活动；piano technique（钢琴演奏技术）侧重触键、指法等技术控制；keyboard artistry（键盘演奏艺术）强调艺术表现，但也可用于其他键盘乐器。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Piano playing is neutral and can describe the activity in general. Piano technique emphasizes technical control, such as touch and fingering. Keyboard artistry stresses expressive achievement but can also refer to instruments other than the piano.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: piano 是乐器，pianism 是驾驭这件乐器的艺术与功力。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Piano names the instrument; pianism names the art and skill of mastering it.

pronunciation.note: 本卡美式读法首音节重读；pro 读 /proʊ/，末段 -caine 读 /keɪn/。

forms: 药物名，通常不可数。

morphology.text: pro- + -caine（局部麻醉药名称常见成分）→ procaine（普鲁卡因）；这是药物命名结构，不能从 pro- 猜测药效。

etymology.text: 二十世纪国际科学词汇，由 pro- 和药物名成分 -caine 组合命名。记忆时注意结尾 -caine 常见于局部麻醉药名称。

usage_note: procaine 是具体的局部麻醉药名称，不是所有麻醉药的统称，也不是镇痛药的通用名称。

senses.meaning_zh: 普鲁卡因，一种局部麻醉药
senses.meaning_en: a drug used as a local anaesthetic
senses.english_definition: Procaine is a drug that is used to prevent pain in a particular part of the body by temporarily blocking nerve signals.
senses.collocation_en: procaine hydrochloride; a procaine injection
senses.collocation_zh: 盐酸普鲁卡因；一次普鲁卡因注射
senses.sentence_en: The textbook lists procaine as an ester local anaesthetic.
senses.sentence_zh: 这本教科书将普鲁卡因列为酯类局部麻醉药。

etymology_story.zh: procaine 是二十世纪初形成的科学药名，由 pro- 与从 cocaine 等名称中发展出的 -caine 组合而成。它指一种合成局部麻醉药；Novocain 则是与这种药物相关的历史商品名。
etymology_story.en: Procaine is an early twentieth-century scientific drug name formed from pro- and -caine, an element developed from names such as cocaine. It denotes a synthetic local anaesthetic; Novocain is a historical trade name associated with the drug.

morphology_enriched.zh: 命名结构为 pro- + -caine → procaine；这里的 pro- 不宜自行赋予能解释药效的含义，-caine 是多种局部麻醉药名称中的惯用成分。该词通常作不可数名词，没有常用的普通英语派生词；procaine hydrochloride（盐酸普鲁卡因）是相关化学名称。
morphology_enriched.en: The naming structure is pro- + -caine → procaine. Here pro- should not be assigned an invented meaning explaining the drug's effects, while -caine is a conventional element in the names of several local anaesthetics. The word is normally an uncountable noun and has no common ordinary English derivatives; procaine hydrochloride is a related chemical name.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Novocain（常亦写作 Novocaine）是与普鲁卡因相关的商品名，口语中有时被泛用于牙科局部麻醉药；local anaesthetic（局部麻醉药）是上位词，包含普鲁卡因及许多其他药物，不能在需要精确药名时直接替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Novocain, also commonly written Novocaine, is a trade name associated with procaine and is sometimes used loosely for dental local anaesthetics. Local anaesthetic is the broader category containing procaine and many other drugs, so it cannot replace the specific name when precision matters.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 看到 -caine，联想到局部麻醉药名称；procaine 对应普鲁卡因。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Let -caine cue the naming pattern of local anaesthetics, then connect procaine with this particular drug.

morphology.text: quant-（quantity 的截短词干）+ -ile（仿 percentile 的名词词尾）→ quantile（分位数）。

etymology.text: 二十世纪英语根据 quantity 的开头部分，仿照 percentile 的形式造词。记住按相等比例划分数据所用的界值。

usage_note: quantile 是分位数的总称；quartile、percentile 分别涉及四等分和一百等分，不是平均值 mean。

senses.english_definition: A quantile is a value that marks a specified proportion of the way through a distribution when its values are arranged from lowest to highest.

etymology_story.zh: quantile 是二十世纪形成的统计学术语，以 quantity 的开头部分为基础，仿照 percentile 等既有分位术语构成。它将百分位数、四分位数等具体名称推广为一般概念，指与指定累积比例对应的界值。
etymology_story.en: Quantile arose as a statistical term in the twentieth century, using the opening of quantity and following the pattern of existing terms such as percentile. It generalizes specific terms such as percentile and quartile to a value corresponding to a specified cumulative proportion.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词可表示为 quant-（取自 quantity，数量）+ -ile（仿 percentile 等词的结尾）→ quantile。常用形式为 quantiles（复数）；quantile-based（基于分位数的）是复合修饰语。quantity（数量）、quantify（量化）、quantification（量化）、quantitative（定量的）是相关词汇，但并非由 quantile 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern formation can be represented as quant-, taken from quantity, + -ile, patterned on endings in terms such as percentile, → quantile. The usual inflected form is quantiles; quantile-based is a compound modifier. Quantity, quantify, quantification, and quantitative are related vocabulary, rather than direct derivatives of quantile.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: percentile（百分位数）是按百分比标示的分位数；quartile（四分位数）通常指将分布分为四个等比例部分的三个内部分界值之一；median（中位数）是 0.5 分位数。三者都是更具体的概念，不能在任意语境中替换 quantile。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A percentile is a quantile expressed on a percentage scale. A quartile usually means one of the three internal cut points dividing a distribution into four equal-proportion parts. The median is the 0.5 quantile. These are more specific concepts and cannot replace quantile in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先排序，再按比例找界值：quantile 记的是“比例对应的数值位置”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Order the values, then locate a proportion: a quantile is the value at that proportional position.

senses.meaning_zh: 齿舌：许多软体动物口内用于刮取或切碎食物的带齿带状器官

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 radula，意为“刮具”，与 radere“刮、削”有关；英语早期曾用它指外科刮具，19世纪又将其用于软体动物类似刮具的取食器官。[词源资料](https://www.etymonline.com/word/radula)
etymology_story.en: Radula comes from Latin radula, meaning a scraping tool, related to radere, meaning to scrape. English first used it for a surgical scraper and later applied it to the scraping feeding organ of mollusks. [Etymology source](https://www.etymonline.com/word/radula)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为完整借词学习，不宜强拆为有独立现代意义的前后缀。专业构词词干为 radul-：radul- + -ar → radular（齿舌的）；相关专业词有 radulate（有齿舌的）、raduliform（齿舌状的）及 subradular（齿舌下的）；名词复数为 radulae，也可用 radulas。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, radula is best learned as a whole borrowed base rather than divided into productive English affixes. Its technical stem is radul-: radul- + -ar forms radular, meaning relating to a radula; related technical formations include radulate, having a radula; raduliform, shaped like a radula; and subradular, beneath the radula. The plural is radulae or radulas.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: rasping tongue（锉状舌）与 toothed ribbon（带齿带状结构）是解释性近义表达，分别突出刮磨功能和带状形态；odontophore（齿舌支持器）是相关的支撑结构，不能与 radula 等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Rasping tongue emphasizes the scraping function, while toothed ribbon describes the structure's shape; both are explanatory equivalents rather than equally precise technical names. An odontophore supports the radula and is not the radula itself.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “刮具”长进口中：一条带着细齿的小刮带。

usage_note: rebarbative 偏正式、书面，表示令人反感或恼火，不表示有吸引力。

senses.meaning_zh: 令人反感的；粗厉难亲近的；艰涩乏味而使人却步的
senses.meaning_en: Unpleasant, off-putting, or forbiddingly unattractive
senses.english_definition: If you describe someone or something as rebarbative, you mean that their unpleasant manner, appearance, or difficulty makes you want to avoid them.
senses.collocation_en: a rebarbative personality; rebarbative prose
senses.collocation_zh: 令人反感的个性；艰涩难亲近的文风
