etymology_story.zh: 19世纪末借自法语 rébarbatif，追溯至古法语 se rebarber，指“胡须相对地对峙”，其中 barbe“胡须”源自拉丁语 barba。面对面对抗的形象逐渐发展出“粗厉、令人反感”的意思。[词源资料](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/us/definition/english/rebarbative)
etymology_story.en: Borrowed from French in the late nineteenth century, rebarbative goes back to Old French se rebarber, meaning to confront someone aggressively, literally beard to beard. Its reference to confrontation developed into the meaning unpleasant or off-putting. [Etymology source](https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/us/definition/english/rebarbative)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 rebarbative 是完整借入的形容词，不能把 re- 机械理解为“再次”。词族：rebarbative + -ly → rebarbatively（令人反感地）；rebarbative + -ness → rebarbativeness（令人反感的特质）；另有罕见名词 rebarbativity（令人反感的性质）。
morphology_enriched.en: Rebarbative is a borrowed adjective in modern English; its initial re- should not be interpreted mechanically as again. Its family includes rebarbative + -ly → rebarbatively, in an off-putting manner; rebarbative + -ness → rebarbativeness, the quality of being off-putting; and the rare alternative noun rebarbativity.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: repellent（令人厌恶的）强调强烈排斥感；off-putting（令人却步的）较日常，强调降低接近或参与的意愿；abrasive（生硬伤人的）主要形容言行态度，而 rebarbative 还可形容外观、文风或内容。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Repellent suggests strong disgust; off-putting is more everyday and emphasizes discouraging interest or involvement; abrasive usually describes a harsh manner, whereas rebarbative can also describe appearance, prose, or subject matter.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “胡须对胡须”地顶撞：态度扎人，让人退避。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Beard-to-beard confrontation: imagine a bristly manner that pushes people away.

pronunciation.note: 本卡美式读法首音节重读，oe 在此读 /e/；保留 /tɡ/ 的衔接，末尾 /ən/ 轻读。

forms: 可数；复数 roentgens。单位名通常小写，符号常写 R。
family: roentgenology 放射学；roentgenogram X光片。

morphology.text: roentgen + -ology → roentgenology（放射学）；roentgen 作为人名转成的独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 国际科学词汇，以德国物理学家 Wilhelm Röntgen 的姓氏命名。把发现X射线的科学家与这一照射量单位联系起来。

usage_note: roentgen 是照射量单位，不是长度单位，也不等同于描述其他辐射量的所有单位。人名 Röntgen 大写，单位名 roentgen 小写。

senses.meaning_en: Relating to the roentgen unit or to X-rays, chiefly in technical or traditional attributive use
senses.english_definition: Roentgen is used before a noun to show that something concerns X-rays or the unit named after their discoverer.

etymology_story.zh: 来自德国物理学家 Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen 的姓氏，他于1895年发现X射线；英语中的 oe 对应德语字母 ö。他的姓氏先用于射线名称，后来又用于照射量单位。[词源资料](https://www.etymonline.com/word/roentgen) [单位释义](https://www.nrc.gov/education-regulatory-research/glossary/roentgen-r)
etymology_story.en: The word comes from the surname of Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen, who discovered X-rays in 1895; oe represents German ö. His name was used for the rays and subsequently for a unit of radiation exposure. [Etymology source](https://www.etymonline.com/word/roentgen) [Unit definition](https://www.nrc.gov/education-regulatory-research/glossary/roentgen-r)

morphology_enriched.zh: roentgen 是由人名转成的完整词基，复数为 roentgens，另有拼写 röntgen。相关医学构词以 roentgen/o- 表示“X射线”：roentgenology（X射线学）、roentgenologist（X射线学专家）、roentgenological（X射线学的）、roentgenography（X射线摄影术）、roentgenographic（X射线摄影的）、roentgenogram（X射线照片）及 roentgenotherapy（X射线治疗）；这些词多属传统专业术语。[词性资料](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/roentgen)
morphology_enriched.en: Roentgen is an indivisible surname-derived base, with plural roentgens and alternative spelling röntgen. The related medical combining form roentgen/o- means X-ray: roentgenology, the study or medical use of X-rays; roentgenologist, a specialist in that field; roentgenological, relating to it; roentgenography, X-ray imaging; roentgenographic, relating to that imaging; roentgenogram, an X-ray image; and roentgenotherapy, X-ray treatment. These are largely traditional technical terms. [Part-of-speech source](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/roentgen)

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 单位义没有可随意替换的普通近义词：röntgen 是同词异拼；gray（戈瑞）计量吸收剂量，sievert（希沃特）计量当量剂量或有效剂量，二者都不等于计量照射量的 roentgen。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: The unit has no interchangeable everyday synonym: röntgen is simply an alternative spelling. Gray measures absorbed dose, while sievert measures equivalent or effective dose; neither is synonymous with roentgen, which measures exposure.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 伦琴发现X射线，他的姓氏也成了照射量单位。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Röntgen discovered X-rays; his name also became an exposure unit.

etymology_story.zh: 来自拉丁语 rubus“黑莓、悬钩子类灌木”，后被用作新拉丁语植物属名 Rubus。英语既用它指这一植物属，也用小写形式指该属的一株植物。[词源与释义资料](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/rubus)
etymology_story.en: Rubus comes from the Latin name for a blackberry or bramble and was adopted as the botanical genus name Rubus. English also uses the lowercase word for an individual plant belonging to that genus. [Etymology and definition source](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/rubus)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是完整借词，没有常用的可分解前后缀，也没有广泛通行的日常派生词族。作普通植物名时可用 rubus 作单复数；作分类学属名时写作 Rubus，规范排版用斜体；Rubus species 是“属名＋名词”的组合，并非派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Rubus is a whole borrowed word without a productive modern English prefix–suffix analysis or an extensive everyday derivative family. As a common plant name, rubus can serve as both singular and plural; as a taxonomic genus name, Rubus is capitalized and conventionally italicized. Rubus species is a name-plus-noun combination, not a derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bramble（悬钩子类刺灌木）是较接近的普通名称，但常让人想到黑莓；blackberry（黑莓）和 raspberry（覆盆子）分别指该属中的特定植物类群，不能代替整个属名。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bramble is a close everyday term, often suggesting a blackberry bush. Blackberry and raspberry refer to particular groups within Rubus, so neither can replace the name of the entire genus.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 Rubus 看成黑莓与覆盆子共同的“属姓”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of Rubus as the shared genus surname of blackberries and raspberries.

senses.sentence_zh: 她加入了一个读书小组，可以在那里结识同样认同 sapphic 身份的人。

etymology_story.zh: 经法语和拉丁语追溯至希腊语 Sapphikos“萨福的”，最初主要指萨福及其诗歌形式。由于她的诗歌描写女性之间的爱慕，该词后来也发展出与女性之间的情爱及相关身份有关的意义。[词源资料](https://www.etymonline.com/word/Sapphic)
etymology_story.en: Through French and Latin, Sapphic traces back to Greek Sapphikos, meaning of Sappho, originally referring chiefly to the poet and her verse forms. Her portrayal of love between women later gave the word meanings connected with attraction between women and related identities. [Etymology source](https://www.etymonline.com/word/Sapphic)

morphology_enriched.zh: 可按专名词干 Sapph- + -ic（与……有关的）理解，但历史上是借入的形式。相关词族：Sappho（萨福）、Sapphic/sapphic（萨福的；萨福体的；女性之间情爱的）、Sapphics/sapphics（萨福体诗歌，或 sapphic 身份者的复数）、Sapphism/sapphism（女性之间的同性情爱，较旧用语）、Sapphist/sapphist（女性同性恋者，较旧用语）及罕见副词 sapphically（以萨福诗体；以女性之间情爱的方式）。诗人和诗体义通常大写，现代性向及身份义常小写。[词性资料](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/sapphic)
morphology_enriched.en: The word can be understood as the proper-name stem Sapph- + -ic, meaning relating to, although the form was historically borrowed. Its family includes Sappho; Sapphic/sapphic; Sapphics/sapphics, referring to verse or the plural of the identity noun; Sapphism/sapphism, a dated term for love between women; Sapphist/sapphist, a dated term for a lesbian; and rare sapphically, in a Sapphic poetic manner or in relation to love between women. Literary senses generally take a capital S; modern attraction and identity senses often use lowercase. [Part-of-speech source](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/sapphic)

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 诗体义没有完全等同的普通近义词，lyric（抒情诗的）范围更广；情爱义中 lesbian（女同性恋的）通常指更特定的性向，而 women-loving-women（女性爱女性的）是较接近的解释性表达，sapphic 还可涵盖双性恋女性及部分非二元性别者。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the verse sense, lyric is broader and does not specify Sappho's meters. For attraction, lesbian usually denotes a more specific orientation, while women-loving-women is a close explanatory equivalent; sapphic can also include bisexual women and some nonbinary people.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住萨福：她的诗歌形式，以及她笔下女性之间的爱。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember Sappho: her verse forms and her poetry of love between women.

etymology_story.zh: 英语将 scandal（丑闻、恶意闲话）与 monger（商贩）组合，把传播丑闻比作兜售商品；该词在18世纪初已有使用。Scandal 最终来自希腊语 skandalon（绊脚物、诱人犯错之物），monger 则承自古英语 mangere（商贩）。
etymology_story.en: English combined scandal with monger, meaning a dealer, to portray someone as a seller of damaging stories; the compound was already in use in the early eighteenth century. Scandal ultimately comes from Greek skandalon, a stumbling block or temptation, while monger descends from Old English mangere, a trader. [Compound history](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/scandalmonger), [scandal history](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/scandal), [monger history](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/monger).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：scandal（丑闻、恶意闲话）+ monger（兜售者、传播者）→ scandalmonger。直接相关形式：scandalmongers（复数）、scandalmongering（名词：散布丑闻；形容词：散布丑闻的）；scandal 词族另有 scandalous（丑恶的、令人震惊的）、scandalously（令人震惊地）、scandalize/scandalise（使震惊）、scandalized/scandalised（感到震惊的）及 scandalization/scandalisation（使人震惊）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: scandal + monger, a dealer or spreader → scandalmonger. Directly related forms include scandalmongers, the plural, and scandalmongering, a noun for spreading scandal and an adjective describing that activity; the scandal family also includes scandalous, scandalously, scandalize/scandalise, scandalized/scandalised, and scandalization/scandalisation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gossip（爱说闲话的人）范围更广，不一定带强烈恶意；rumormonger（散布谣言者）强调传播未经证实的消息；slanderer（诽谤者）强调以虚假陈述损害名誉。Scandalmonger 特别突出热衷传播他人丑事，所传内容不一定全是捏造的。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A gossip talks about other people's private affairs, sometimes without strong malice; a rumormonger spreads unverified reports; a slanderer damages reputations through false statements. A scandalmonger particularly relishes circulating disgraceful or embarrassing stories, which need not all be invented.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把丑闻当货物兜售的人：scandal + monger。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A dealer whose merchandise is scandal: scandal + monger.

etymology_story.zh: 英语从德语 Septett 借入该词，其词根最终来自拉丁语 septem（七），英语用例可追溯至1799年。它既可指为七个声部写的乐曲，也可指七位表演者组成的组合，并可泛指任何七个一组的人或事物。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word from German Septett, ultimately based on Latin septem, meaning seven; English use is recorded from 1799. It denotes both music for seven parts and an ensemble of seven performers, and it can also describe other groups of seven. [Merriam-Webster: septet](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/septet).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可作表层分析：sept-（七）+ -et（见于音乐组合名称的词尾），但整个词是借入词，不能把 -et 一概解释为“乐团”。词形包括 septets（复数）和 septette（异体拼写）；同数词根的相关词有 septuple（七倍的；使增至七倍）及 septuplet（七胞胎之一；音乐中的七连音），它们不是 septet 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: A useful surface analysis is sept-, seven, + -et, an ending found in musical ensemble names, although the whole word was borrowed and -et does not universally mean ensemble. Forms include the plural septets and the spelling variant septette; related numerical formations include septuple, meaning sevenfold or to multiply by seven, and septuplet, one of seven offspring or a musical seven-note grouping, rather than direct derivatives of septet.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: seven-piece ensemble（七人乐队或合奏组）是组合义的明确近义表达；group of seven（七人或七物组成的一组）适用于一般分组；ensemble（合奏或合唱组合）不限定人数。Septet 还可表示乐曲本身，前两个表示组合的表达不能直接替代这一义项。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Seven-piece ensemble is a close equivalent for the performing group; group of seven covers the general grouping sense; ensemble leaves the number unspecified. Septet can additionally name the composition itself, a meaning not automatically conveyed by the group expressions.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sept- 抓住“七”：七位演奏者，或给七个声部写的曲子。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Let sept- signal seven: seven performers, or music for seven parts.

etymology_story.zh: Sone 是20世纪根据拉丁语 sonus（声音）创造的科学单位名称，英语记录可追溯至1936年。它把声音这一概念具体化为人耳所感受到的响度，用于主观听觉量的测量。
etymology_story.en: Sone is a twentieth-century scientific coinage based on Latin sonus, meaning sound, with English use recorded from 1936. It applies the idea of sound specifically to perceived loudness, giving a unit to a listener's auditory experience. [Merriam-Webster: sone](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/sone).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 sone 作为完整单位名称处理，不宜机械拆成能自由构词的词根和后缀。词形与常用组合包括 sones（复数）、sone scale（宋响度标度）、sone value（以宋计的响度值）和 sone-based（基于宋响度标度的）；sonic（声音的）及 sonorous（声音洪亮悦耳的）与它有词源联系，但不是由 sone 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, sone functions as a complete unit name rather than a freely productive root-and-suffix combination. Forms and useful compounds include sones, sone scale, sone value, and sone-based; sonic, relating to sound, and sonorous, having a rich resonant sound, are etymologically related but are not direct derivatives of sone.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 该单位没有可任意互换的普通近义词。Unit of perceived loudness（主观响度单位）是解释性表达；phon（方）是响度级单位；decibel（分贝）用于表达对数量值比，在声学中常见于声压级等量，三者不能作为同一单位互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: This unit has no freely interchangeable everyday synonym. Unit of perceived loudness is an explanatory paraphrase; phon measures loudness level; decibel expresses a logarithmic ratio and commonly appears in acoustic quantities such as sound pressure level. These units are not interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sonus 是“声音”：sone 量的是“听起来有多响”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sonus means sound: a sone measures how loud that sound feels.

etymology_story.zh: 医学用法经中古英语 tercian、盎格鲁法语追溯至拉丁语 tertianus（第三的），与 febris tertiana（按首尾都计算为第三天再发作的热病）有关。把首次发作当天算第一天，再次发作便在第三天，因此实际约相隔48小时；其他专业用法也保留了“第三”或“三度”的联系。
etymology_story.en: The medical use passed through Middle English tercian and Anglo-French from Latin tertianus, meaning of the third, associated with febris tertiana. Counting the first attack as day one makes the next attack fall on day three, approximately forty-eight hours later; other specialist uses likewise retain an association with thirds or a third stage. [Merriam-Webster: tertian](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/tertian), [Collins: tertian](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/tertian).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可作表层分析：terti-（第三）+ -an（……的；与……有关的人），但该词的医学用法历史上是借入的。名词复数为 tertians；tertian + -ship → tertianship（耶稣会第三试习期）；tertiary（第三的、第三级的）是同源相关词，不是由 tertian 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: A modern surface analysis is terti-, third, + -an, relating to something or a person associated with it, although the medical word was historically borrowed. The noun plural is tertians; tertian + -ship gives tertianship, the Jesuit formation period; tertiary, meaning third or third-level, is a related formation rather than a derivative of tertian.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 医学义中，alternate-day（隔日的）是直接解释，intermittent（间歇性的）范围更广，并不指定48小时周期。音乐义中，third-based（以三度为基础的）是解释性近义表达；triadic（三和弦的）只涉及三音和弦，而 tertian 也可涵盖按三度构成的七和弦等。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: In medicine, alternate-day directly paraphrases the timing, while intermittent is broader and specifies no forty-eight-hour cycle. In music, third-based is an explanatory equivalent; triadic concerns three-note chords, whereas tertian also covers seventh chords and other structures built in thirds.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“第三”：医学上第一天发作、第三天再发；音乐上按三度叠置；会士进入第三试习期。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor everything to third: attacks on days one and three, musical thirds, and a Jesuit's third probation.

etymology_story.zh: Trioxide 是19世纪化学命名中的组合词，由表示“三”的 tri- 与 oxide（氧化物）构成，英语用例可追溯至1863年。Tri- 最终承接希腊语表示“三”的构词形式，名称直接标示化学式中的氧原子数。
etymology_story.en: Trioxide arose in nineteenth-century chemical naming from tri-, meaning three, and oxide, with English use recorded from 1863. The prefix ultimately reflects the Greek combining form for three, and the name directly indicates the oxygen count in the formula. [Merriam-Webster: trioxide](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/trioxide), [Collins: trioxide](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/trioxide).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：tri-（三）+ oxide（氧化物）→ trioxide；复数为 trioxides。相关命名有 monoxide（一氧化物）、dioxide（二氧化物）和 tetroxide（四氧化物）；oxide 的相关词族包括 oxidize/oxidise（氧化）、oxidation（氧化）、oxidative（氧化的）及 oxidant（氧化剂），这些不是 trioxide 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: tri-, three, + oxide → trioxide; the plural is trioxides. Related names include monoxide, dioxide, and tetroxide; the broader oxide family includes oxidize/oxidise, oxidation, oxidative, and oxidant, which are not direct derivatives of trioxide.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 该词没有可普遍替换的严格近义词。Oxide（氧化物）是上位词；dioxide（二氧化物）表示两个氧原子，不能替换 trioxide；sesquioxide（倍半氧化物）表示元素与氧的原子数比为2∶3，因此 As2O3 可同时属于两类，而 SO3 不属于倍半氧化物。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no universally interchangeable exact synonym. Oxide is the broader category; dioxide specifies two oxygen atoms and cannot replace trioxide; sesquioxide specifies a 2:3 ratio of the other element to oxygen, so As2O3 belongs to both categories, whereas SO3 is not a sesquioxide.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: tri- 就是“三”：盯住化学式中 O 后面的 3。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Tri- means three: look for the 3 after O in the formula.

etymology_story.zh: Uridine 是根据 uracil（尿嘧啶）的名称改造而成的化学名称，使用了核苷命名中可见的 -idine 形式。它指尿嘧啶与核糖结合形成的核苷，不宜机械拆成 uro-、-ide 和 -ine。
etymology_story.en: Uridine is a chemical name adapted from uracil, using the ending -idine found in nucleoside names. It names the nucleoside formed from uracil and ribose and should not be mechanically divided into uro-, -ide, and -ine.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜将 uridine 视为完整的化学词基；其命名关系为 uracil → uridine，而不是普通的词根加词缀构词。主要相关形式有 uridyl（尿苷基）、uridylic（尿苷酸的）、uridylate（尿苷酸或其盐）、uridylation／uridylylation（尿苷酸化）；相关化合物包括 deoxyuridine（脱氧尿苷）、pseudouridine（假尿苷）以及 uridine monophosphate／diphosphate／triphosphate（尿苷一／二／三磷酸，UMP／UDP／UTP）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, uridine is best treated as a complete chemical base; its naming relationship is uracil → uridine rather than an ordinary root-plus-affix construction. Principal related forms include uridyl, uridylic, uridylate, and uridylation or uridylylation; related compounds include deoxyuridine, pseudouridine, and uridine monophosphate, diphosphate, and triphosphate, abbreviated UMP, UDP, and UTP.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有通用的精确近义词。相关术语中，uracil（尿嘧啶）仅指碱基，uridine（尿苷）是该碱基加核糖，uridylate（尿苷酸或其盐）通常涉及进一步连接的磷酸基团；三者不可互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no ordinary exact synonym. Among related terms, uracil names the base alone, uridine names that base attached to ribose, and uridylate generally refers to a phosphorylated form or its salt; these terms are not interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把命名关系连起来记：uracil 是碱基，接上核糖就成为 uridine。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the names to the structures: uracil is the base; adding ribose gives uridine.

etymology_story.zh: Uxoriousness 由形容词 uxorious 加 -ness 构成；uxorious 来自拉丁语 uxorius（妻子的；与妻子有关的），其基础是 uxor（妻子）。英语中的 uxorious 发展出“过分宠爱或顺从妻子”的评价意味，名词保留了这一含义。
etymology_story.en: Uxoriousness was formed by adding -ness to uxorious, which comes from Latin uxorius, meaning 'of or relating to a wife,' from uxor, 'wife.' In English, uxorious developed the evaluative meaning of excessive devotion or submission to a wife, which the noun preserves.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：uxorious（过分宠爱或顺从妻子的）+ -ness（性质或状态）→ uxoriousness。直接词族包括 uxorious、uxoriously（过分宠妻地）和 uxoriousness；同源词 uxorial 意为“妻子的；与妻子有关的”，本身不含“过度”的意思。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: uxorious, meaning excessively devoted or submissive to one's wife, + -ness, marking a quality or state, → uxoriousness. The direct family includes uxorious, uxoriously, and uxoriousness; the related word uxorial means 'of or relating to a wife' without itself implying excess.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Wife-worship（对妻子的崇拜）突出理想化和仰慕；dotage（溺爱）突出近乎失去理性的宠爱，对象不限于妻子；submissiveness（顺从）突出服从他人意愿，并不必然包含爱意。Uxoriousness 特指对妻子的过度宠爱或顺从。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Wife-worship emphasizes idealization and admiration; dotage emphasizes foolishly excessive affection and need not concern a wife; submissiveness emphasizes yielding to another person's wishes without necessarily involving affection. Uxoriousness specifically concerns excessive devotion or submission to one's wife.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Uxor 是“妻子”：uxoriousness 就是围着妻子转到了“过度”的程度。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Uxor means 'wife': uxoriousness is devotion to one's wife carried to excess.

senses.collocation_en: dance a valse; valse-musette
senses.collocation_zh: 跳一支华尔兹舞；法式缪塞特华尔兹舞
senses.sentence_en: The dancers performed a graceful valse.
senses.sentence_zh: 舞者们跳了一支优雅的华尔兹舞。

etymology_story.zh: Valse 借自法语，法语词又来自德语 Walzer（华尔兹），与表示“滚动、旋转”的 walzen 有关。英语保留了这一法语形式，尤其用于圆舞曲的作品名称和音乐描述。
etymology_story.en: Valse was borrowed from French, whose word comes from German Walzer, related to walzen, meaning 'to roll or turn.' English retained the French form especially in musical titles and descriptions of waltz compositions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 valse 是不可再作常规拆分的借词，复数为 valses。相关复合形式包括 valse-musette（法式缪塞特华尔兹）；valse brillante（辉煌圆舞曲）和 valse lente（慢圆舞曲）是保留法语形式的音乐短语。Waltz 是同源的英语词形，其词族包括 waltzes、waltzed、waltzing 和 waltzer，并非 valse 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, valse is an unanalyzed loanword with the plural valses. Related compounds include valse-musette; valse brillante and valse lente are musical phrases retaining French forms. Waltz is the related English form, with the family waltzes, waltzed, waltzing, and waltzer, rather than a direct derivative of valse.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Waltz（华尔兹舞或舞曲）是通常使用的英语对应词，适用范围最广；Viennese waltz（维也纳华尔兹）特指通常速度较快的舞种；valse-musette（缪塞特华尔兹）特指法国缪塞特舞厅传统中的风格。后两者都是更具体的类别。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Waltz is the ordinary English equivalent and has the broadest application; Viennese waltz names a particular, generally faster dance style; valse-musette names a style associated with the French musette dance-hall tradition. The latter two are narrower categories.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 valse 与 waltz 配对：两者都围绕“旋转起舞”，valse 保留法语外形。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pair valse with waltz: both evoke turning in a dance, while valse keeps the French form.

etymology_story.zh: Vibrio 来自新拉丁语微生物名称 Vibrio，最终源于拉丁语 vibrare（摇动、振动）。这一名称最初着眼于微生物的运动，后来成为弧菌属名称及相关细菌的普通名称。
etymology_story.en: Vibrio comes from the New Latin microorganism name Vibrio, ultimately from Latin vibrare, meaning 'to shake or vibrate.' The name originally emphasized movement and later became both a bacterial genus name and a common name for associated bacteria.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 vibrio 是完整词基，常见复数有 vibrios 和拉丁式 vibriones；学名属名写作 Vibrio。相关形式包括 vibrioid（弧菌状的）、vibriosis（弧菌病，复数 vibrioses）、vibriocidal（杀弧菌的）和 vibriophage（弧菌噬菌体）；vibration（振动）与其历史同源，但不是由 vibrio 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, vibrio is a complete base, with the plurals vibrios and the Latin-style vibriones; the scientific genus name is capitalized Vibrio. Related formations include vibrioid, vibriosis with plural vibrioses, vibriocidal, and vibriophage; vibration shares its historical root but is not derived from vibrio.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有适用于所有语境的精确近义词。Curved bacterium（弯曲的细菌）是描述性近似表达，不必然属于弧菌属；bacterium（细菌）范围更广；cholera vibrio（霍乱弧菌）仅指其中与霍乱相关的特定细菌。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact synonym for every context. Curved bacterium is a descriptive approximation and does not necessarily identify the genus Vibrio; bacterium is broader; cholera vibrio refers specifically to the bacterium associated with cholera.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 词源记运动，词义记形状：vibr- 联想振动，vibrio 联想弯曲的小细菌。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use motion for the root and shape for the meaning: vibr- suggests vibration, while a vibrio is a small curved bacterium.

etymology_story.zh: Autocrine 是现代生物医学术语，由 auto-（自身）与 -crine（分泌）组合，构词模式与 endocrine、paracrine 相呼应。Auto- 源于希腊语 autos（自身），-crine 最终与希腊语 krinein（分离）有关，在此发展为“分泌”的含义。
etymology_story.en: Autocrine is a modern biomedical term combining auto-, meaning 'self,' with -crine, meaning 'secretion,' following the pattern of endocrine and paracrine. Auto- comes from Greek autos, 'self,' while -crine ultimately relates to Greek krinein, 'to separate,' developing the sense of secretion.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：auto-（自身）+ -crine（分泌）→ autocrine（自分泌的）；相关名词 autocriny 指自分泌作用，使用较少，通常用 autocrine signaling 或 autocrine secretion 表达。共享 -crine 的术语有 endocrine（内分泌的）、paracrine（旁分泌的）、intracrine（胞内分泌的）和 juxtacrine（接触依赖性信号传导的），这些是并列构词，不是 autocrine 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: auto-, meaning 'self,' + -crine, meaning 'secretion,' → autocrine. The less common related noun autocriny denotes autocrine activity, usually expressed as autocrine signaling or autocrine secretion. Other formations sharing -crine include endocrine, paracrine, intracrine, and juxtacrine; these are parallel formations rather than direct derivatives of autocrine.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全等同且同样常用的单词近义词，self-signaling（向自身发送信号）可作解释性近似表达。相关术语中，paracrine（旁分泌的）强调作用于附近其他细胞，endocrine（内分泌的）强调信号经循环系统到达远处靶细胞；autocrine 则强调作用于释放信号的细胞自身。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no equally common exact single-word synonym; self-signaling is an explanatory approximation. Among related terms, paracrine emphasizes action on nearby other cells, while endocrine emphasizes signals traveling through the circulation to distant target cells; autocrine emphasizes action on the releasing cell itself.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Auto- 是“自己”，-crine 是“分泌”：细胞发出的信号，回到自己身上起作用。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Auto- means 'self' and -crine means 'secretion': the cell releases a signal that acts back on itself.

etymology_story.zh: basophil 是19世纪后期形成的科学术语，由表示“碱、碱性的”的 baso- 与表示“喜爱、亲和”的 -phil 构成，后者源于希腊语 philos。它最初描述细胞对碱性染料的亲和性，后来也成为一种粒细胞的名称。
etymology_story.en: Basophil arose in late nineteenth-century scientific vocabulary from baso-, referring to a base or basic substance, and -phil, ultimately from Greek philos, meaning loving. It described an affinity for basic dyes and also became the name of a particular type of granulocyte.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：baso-（碱、碱性的）+ -phil（对……有亲和性者；亲和……的）。主要词族：basophils（复数）、basophilic（嗜碱性的，较常用的形容词）、basophilous（嗜碱性的，较少用）、basophilia（嗜碱性；临床语境中也指嗜碱性粒细胞增多）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: baso- (base or basic substance) + -phil (having an affinity for something). Principal family members are basophils, the plural; basophilic, the more usual adjective; basophilous, a less common adjective; and basophilia, meaning affinity for basic dyes or, clinically, an increased basophil count.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: basophilic granulocyte 是名词义的明确同义表达，突出其粒细胞身份；basophilic 是表达“嗜碱性的”时更常用的形容词；basophilous 具有相近的染色学含义，但使用较少。形容词所描述的嗜碱性结构不一定属于嗜碱性粒细胞。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Basophilic granulocyte is an explicit synonym for the cell, emphasizing its classification as a granulocyte. Basophilic is the more usual adjective for affinity for basic dyes, while basophilous is a less common equivalent. A structure described by these adjectives need not belong to a basophil.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Baso- means basic and -phil means affinity: remember a cell that attracts basic dyes, rather than a cell that is itself alkaline.

etymology_story.zh: batterie 借自法语，源于 battre“击打”，其更早来源是拉丁语 battuere。法语中“击打”的一般含义在芭蕾术语中专指舞者腾空时双腿快速相击的动作。
etymology_story.en: Batterie was borrowed from French, where it derives from battre, meaning to beat, ultimately from Latin battuere. In ballet terminology, the general idea of beating became specialized to rapid beats of the legs during jumps.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 batterie 作为完整的法语借词处理，不按英语词缀强拆。法语来源可分析为 batt-（击打）+ -erie（构成动作或集合名词）；英语中没有常用的直接派生词，相关历史同源词包括 batter（连续击打）、battery（原有连续击打之义）和 battement（芭蕾踢腿或摆腿动作），不应视为 batterie 的英语派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, batterie is normally treated as a whole French loanword. Its French formation contains batt- (beat) and -erie, a suffix forming action or collective nouns. It has no common direct English derivatives; historically related words include batter, battery, and the ballet term battement, but these are not English derivatives of batterie.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: beaten steps 是接近的描述性表达，指包含击腿的舞步；entrechat 指腾空时双腿快速交叉相击的一种具体动作；battu 表示某个跳跃“带击腿”，通常修饰动作名称。后两者与 batterie 密切相关，但不是可自由替换的同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Beaten steps is a close descriptive expression for steps incorporating leg beats. An entrechat is a particular jump involving crossing beats of the legs, while battu describes a jump performed with a beat. The latter two are related technical terms rather than interchangeable synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 batt- 与“击打”相连：舞者跃起，双腿在空中快速“打拍子”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect batt- with beating: picture a dancer jumping and making the legs beat rapidly in the air.

senses.meaning_en: A blessing, especially in literary language.
senses.english_definition: A benison is a blessing or an expression of the wish that someone will receive goodness, protection, or happiness.
senses.collocation_en: bestow a benison; a father's benison
senses.collocation_zh: 赐予祝福；父亲的祝福
senses.sentence_en: She left home with her father's benison.
senses.sentence_zh: 她带着父亲的祝福离开了家。

etymology_story.zh: benison 经中古英语、古法语 beneison 等形式传入英语，最终源于拉丁语 benedictio“祝福”。其深层结构包含 bene“好”与 dicere“说”，体现了从“说好话”到“祈福、祝福”的意义发展。
etymology_story.en: Benison entered English through Middle English and Old French forms such as beneison, ultimately from Latin benedictio, meaning blessing. Its deeper elements are bene, meaning well, and dicere, meaning to say, connecting speaking well with offering a blessing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：benison 为不可再作常规分析的整体名词，不能把它误拆为 ben- + -ison。直接词形有复数 benisons；历史同源词有 benediction（祝福、祝祷）和 benedictory（祝福的、祝祷的），后两者不是在现代英语中由 benison 加词缀构成的。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: benison is a morphologically opaque noun, not a productive combination of ben- and -ison. Its direct inflected form is the plural benisons. Historical relatives include benediction and benedictory; neither is formed by adding a modern English affix to benison.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: blessing 是最通用的“祝福”，也可指福分或好事；benediction 更常指正式、尤其宗教仪式中的祝祷；benison 意义相近，但带有明显的文学或古雅色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Blessing is the ordinary general term and can also mean a benefit or fortunate circumstance. Benediction often denotes a formal, especially religious, blessing. Benison conveys a similar idea in a distinctly literary or old-fashioned register.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 联系同源词 benediction：bene“好”+ dicere“说”——把美好的话送给别人，就是祝福。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use its relative benediction as the anchor: bene means well and dicere means say—good words offered to someone become a blessing.

etymology_story.zh: beringed 是英语内部构成的词，以表示“使带有、饰以”的 be- 与 ring“戒指、环”结合，并以 -ed 形成形容词。ring 可追溯到古英语 hring；全词描绘的是手或手指被戒指装点的状态。
etymology_story.en: Beringed was formed within English using be-, which can indicate furnishing or covering something, ring, and adjectival -ed. Ring goes back to Old English hring, and the resulting adjective describes a hand or finger adorned with rings.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：be-（使带有、饰以）+ ring（戒指）+ -ed（表示具有某种装饰或处于某种状态）。重音在 ring，-ed 读 /d/，不另成音节；常用基础词族包括 ring、rings、ringed、ringless 和 ringlet（小环；卷发）。表示“打电话、鸣响”的 ring 有 rang、rung 等形式，属于另一个历史词源的词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: be- (furnish or adorn with) + ring + -ed (having an ornament or being in a resulting state). Stress falls on ring, and -ed is pronounced /d/ without an extra syllable. Common members of the underlying family include ring, rings, ringed, ringless, and ringlet. Ring meaning telephone or make a ringing sound, with rang and rung, has a separate historical origin.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ringed 可表示戴着戒指，但也常指有环纹、被环绕或被套环；ring-adorned 明确强调以戒指装饰，是描述性近义表达；bejewelled 指佩有珠宝，范围比戒指更广。beringed 通常带有较强的描写或文学色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ringed can mean wearing rings but also describes bands, encirclement, or fitted rings. Ring-adorned is an explicit descriptive equivalent emphasizing decoration. Bejewelled refers more broadly to being decorated with jewels. Beringed typically has a descriptive or literary flavor.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: be- 表“饰以”，ring 是“戒指”：一只被戒指装点的手。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Read be- as adorned with and ring as a finger ornament: picture a hand decorated with rings.

etymology_story.zh: bilabial 是由拉丁语来源的 bi-“二、双”和 labial“唇的”构成的语音学术语，labial 最终源于拉丁语 labium“嘴唇”。它先描述双唇参与的发音方式，随后也用作名词，指这种部位发出的辅音。
etymology_story.en: Bilabial is a phonetic term formed from Latin-derived bi-, meaning two, and labial, ultimately from Latin labium, meaning lip. It describes articulation involving both lips and also functions as a noun for a consonant produced at that place of articulation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：bi-（双）+ labial（唇的）；进一步分析为 bi- + labi-（唇）+ -al（……的）。直接词族包括 bilabials（名词复数）、bilabially（以双唇方式）和较少用的 bilabiality（双唇发音性质）；相关基础词族包括 labial、labially、labialize/labialise 和 labialization/labialisation。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: bi- (two) + labial (relating to the lips), further analyzable as bi- + labi- (lip) + -al. Direct family members include the plural noun bilabials, the adverb bilabially, and the less common noun bilabiality. The broader base family includes labial, labially, labialize/labialise, and labialization/labialisation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: two-lipped 是“双唇的”的直译性表达，但在语音学中不如 bilabial 精确、常用；labial 范围较广，可指任何涉及嘴唇的发音；labiodental 指下唇与上齿共同参与的“唇齿音”，是相邻类别而非同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Two-lipped is a literal descriptive equivalent but is less precise and conventional in phonetics. Labial is broader, covering articulation involving the lips generally. Labiodental describes articulation using the lower lip and upper teeth, so it names a neighboring category rather than a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: bi- 是“双”，labi- 是“唇”：发 /p/ 时感受上下唇先合拢再分开。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bi- means two and labi- means lip: say /p/ and feel both lips come together and then separate.

etymology_story.zh: 由 bill（旧时指刀剑或砍削工具）与 hook（钩）复合而成，以刀刃的钩状外形命名。这里的 bill 源于古英语 bil，表示剑或类似的利刃武器。

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：bill（砍削工具）+ hook（钩）→ billhook（钩形砍刀），属于复合名词。复数：billhooks；没有常用的独立派生词。

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pruning knife（修枝刀）通常较小，适合精细修剪；machete（砍刀）通常刀身较长，适合清理植被；sickle（镰刀）主要用于割草或收割。billhook 的特点是适合砍削木质枝条的钩形刀刃。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A pruning knife is usually smaller and suited to precise trimming; a machete generally has a longer blade for clearing vegetation; a sickle is mainly used for cutting grass or harvesting crops. A billhook is distinguished by its hooked blade for cutting woody growth.

etymology_story.zh: 19世纪以法国科学家 Jean-Baptiste Biot（让-巴蒂斯特·比奥）的姓氏命名，以纪念他对云母光学性质的研究。姓氏 Biot 加上矿物名称后缀 -ite，形成 biotite。
etymology_story.en: Biotite was named in the nineteenth century after the French scientist Jean-Baptiste Biot, honoring his work on the optical properties of mica. His surname was combined with the mineral suffix -ite.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：Biot（比奥的姓氏）+ -ite（矿物名称后缀）→ biotite；不能拆成表示“生命”的 bio-。词族包括 biotitic（含黑云母的；黑云母质的）、biotitization／biotitisation（黑云母化）；biotites 可表示不同种类或样品的黑云母。
morphology_enriched.en: Structure: Biot (the scientist's surname) + -ite (a mineral suffix) → biotite; the opening letters do not represent bio-, meaning life. Family members include biotitic (containing or consisting of biotite) and biotitization/biotitisation (formation of or alteration to biotite); biotites can refer to different varieties or samples.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: black mica（黑云母）是通俗近义名称；mica（云母）是范围更广的矿物类别；muscovite（白云母）是通常颜色较浅的另一类云母，并非黑云母的同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Black mica is a common descriptive equivalent; mica names the broader mineral category; muscovite is another, usually lighter-colored mica and is not a synonym for biotite.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Biot 的名字 + 矿物尾巴 -ite：比奥名下的深色云母，不是“生命石”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Biot's name plus the mineral ending -ite: remember dark mica named after Biot.

etymology.text: 快马义经古法语 coursier（奔跑的马）进入英语，来自 cours（奔跑、行程）。可以想象骑士胯下飞奔的马。

etymology_story.zh: 快马义经古法语 coursier 进入英语，最终与拉丁语 currere（奔跑）有关，名称突出马的奔跑能力。鸟名则由 course（奔跑、追逐）加 -er 构成，同样突出在地面疾跑的习性。
etymology_story.en: The horse sense entered English through Old French coursier and ultimately belongs to the family of Latin currere, meaning to run. The bird name was formed from course, meaning to run or pursue, plus -er, referring to the bird's swift movement on the ground.

morphology_enriched.zh: 快马义是历史借词，现代宜整体识记；鸟名可分析为 course（奔跑，去词尾 e）+ -er → courser（善跑的鸟）。复数：coursers；相关词族有 course（奔跑、追逐）、coursed（过去式及过去分词）、coursing（奔跑；用猎犬追猎）。
morphology_enriched.en: The horse sense is an inherited loanword best learned as a whole; the bird name can be analyzed as course (run, dropping final e) + -er → courser. Plural: coursers; related forms include course (run or pursue), coursed (past tense and past participle), and coursing (running or hunting with pursuing hounds).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 快马义中，steed（坐骑）同样偏文学，但不特别强调速度；charger（战马）突出作战用途；racehorse（赛马）专指用于竞赛的马。鸟类义没有通用的单词同义词，不能用这些马匹名称替代。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the horse sense, steed is similarly literary but does not specifically emphasize speed; charger emphasizes military use; racehorse specifically denotes a horse used for racing. The bird sense has no general one-word synonym and cannot be replaced by these horse terms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“奔跑”这一条线：文学里是飞奔的马，鸟类里是贴地快跑的走鸻。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep running at the center: a galloping horse in literature, or a swift ground-running bird.

etymology_story.zh: 英语用表示“去除、使失去”的前缀 dis- 与 mast（桅杆）构成此词，字面意思就是“使失去桅杆”。mast 来自古英语 mæst，该词因而一直与帆船航海紧密相关。
etymology_story.en: English formed dismast by attaching the removal prefix dis- to mast, literally meaning to deprive something of its mast. Mast comes from Old English mæst, and the verb has remained closely associated with sailing vessels.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：dis-（除去、使失去）+ mast（桅杆）→ dismast。词形与词族：dismasts（第三人称单数）、dismasted（过去式、过去分词；也可作分词形容词，表示失去桅杆的）、dismasting（现在分词；也可作名词，表示断桅事件）、dismastment（断桅；拆除桅杆）。
morphology_enriched.en: Structure: dis- (remove or deprive of) + mast → dismast. Forms and family: dismasts (third-person singular), dismasted (past tense and past participle, also used adjectivally), dismasting (present participle, also a noun for the event), and dismastment (loss or removal of a mast).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: unmast（卸下桅杆）通常突出主动拆卸；demast（拆桅、使失去桅杆）意义接近但较少见；disable（使失去正常运作能力）范围更广，不一定涉及桅杆。dismast 尤其常用于风暴或事故造成的断桅。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Unmast usually emphasizes deliberate removal; demast has a closely related meaning but is less common; disable is broader and need not involve a mast. Dismast is especially associated with mast loss caused by storms or accidents.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: dis- 表示“去掉”，mast 是“桅杆”：桅杆一去，船就 dismasted。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Dis- takes away the mast: picture a sailing vessel suddenly left without its mast.

etymology_story.zh: 英语从西班牙语借入 duro，它是 peso duro 的简称，字面意思为“硬比索”，原指足值银币。西班牙语 duro 源自拉丁语 durus（硬的）；这个货币名称后来也用于西班牙的五比塞塔硬币及相应金额。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed duro from Spanish, where it shortens peso duro, literally hard peso, originally referring to a full-value silver coin. Spanish duro comes from Latin durus, meaning hard; the currency name was later also applied to Spain's five-peseta coin and the corresponding amount.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整体借入的名词，不再拆分；复数为 duros，没有常用的英语派生词。在来源语言西班牙语中可分析为 dur-（硬）+ -o（阳性单数词尾）；英语 durable（耐用的）、durability（耐用性）、endure（忍受；持久）与其有共同的拉丁语词源，但不是 duro 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, duro is an unanalyzed borrowed noun; its plural is duros, and it has no common English derivatives. In Spanish, its source form can be analyzed as dur- (hard) + -o (the masculine singular ending); English durable, durability, and endure share its Latin ancestry but are not derivatives of duro.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: silver peso（银比索）强调币种及银质；Spanish dollar（西班牙银元）通常指国际贸易中流通的八里亚尔银币；five-peseta coin（五比塞塔硬币）对应 duro 在西班牙后来的用法。这些名称分别对应不同历史货币背景，不能一概互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Silver peso emphasizes the denomination and silver content; Spanish dollar usually refers to the eight-real silver coin used in international trade; five-peseta coin matches the later Spanish use of duro. These expressions belong to different historical currency contexts and are not universally interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: duro 原意“硬的”：先记硬邦邦的银比索，再记后来西班牙的“五比塞塔”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Duro means hard: picture a solid silver peso, then connect the later Spanish use with five pesetas.

etymology_story.zh: eld 经中古英语传自古英语 ieldo，表示“年老”，与 old 同源；它还发展出“古时、往昔”的意义，如今主要见于古雅或诗歌语体。参见[《韦氏词典》eld 词条](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/eld)。
etymology_story.en: Eld descends through Middle English from Old English ieldo, meaning old age, and is historically related to old; it also acquired the meaning of ancient times and now survives chiefly in archaic or poetic language. See [Merriam-Webster's eld entry](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/eld).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 eld 视为不可再分析的独立词根，不拆成前缀或后缀，两个义项通常均不可数。历史相关词包括 old（老的）、older／oldest（更老／最老）、elder／eldest（年长的／最年长的）、elderly（年老的）、olden（往昔的）；elden（变老；使变老）是罕见古体动词，不是 eld 的现代常用派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, eld is an unanalyzed simple root, with no productive prefix or suffix; both senses are normally uncountable. Historical relatives include old, older/oldest, elder/eldest, elderly, and olden; elden, meaning to grow or make old, is a rare archaic verb rather than a current productive derivative of eld.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: old age（老年）是中性、日常的说法；senescence（衰老）强调生物性的老化过程，语体正式；antiquity（古代）对应 eld 的“往昔”义，不指某个人的老年。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Old age is the neutral everyday expression; senescence is formal and emphasizes biological aging; antiquity corresponds to the historical-time sense of eld rather than an individual's later life.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 eld 与同源词 old 相连：人的“老”是暮年，时代的“老”是远古。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect eld with its historical relative old: an old person suggests old age, and an old era suggests ancient times.

etymology_story.zh: empyema 经拉丁语借自希腊语 empyēma，后者源于表示“化脓”的动词 empyein，与 en-（在内，遇 p 同化为 em-）和 pyon（脓）有关。英语保留了“体腔内积脓”的医学意义，尤其用于胸膜腔积脓；参见[《韦氏词典》empyema 词条](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/empyema)。
etymology_story.en: Empyema entered English through Latin from Greek empyēma, derived from empyein, to suppurate, and associated with en-, assimilated to em- before p, and pyon, pus. English retains its medical meaning of pus accumulating in a body cavity, especially the pleural cavity; see [Merriam-Webster's empyema entry](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/empyema).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整体借入的医学名词；辅助分析可用 em-（在内）＋ py-（脓）＋ -ema（源于希腊语的结果或状态名词结尾），但这不是现代英语自由组合的构词公式。复数为 empyemas 或 empyemata；相关形容词有 empyemic（积脓的）和 empyematous（积脓性的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, this is a borrowed medical noun; a useful learned analysis is em- (within) + py- (pus) + -ema (a Greek-derived result or state ending), rather than a freely productive English formation. Its plurals are empyemas and empyemata; related adjectives include empyemic and empyematous.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pyothorax（脓胸）专指胸膜腔积脓，与胸部语境下的 empyema 对应；abscess（脓肿）通常指组织内局限形成的脓液聚集；suppuration（化脓）强调产生脓液的过程，而非某处积脓本身。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pyothorax specifically denotes pleural empyema; an abscess is usually a localized collection of pus within tissue; suppuration denotes the process of forming pus rather than the collection itself.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: em-＝在内，py-＝脓：脓积在体腔内；积在胸膜腔，就是脓胸。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Em- means within and py- points to pus: pus collects inside a body cavity; in the pleural cavity, it is pleural empyema.

morphology.text: 与 executor 对照记词形：将末尾 -tor 换成 -trix，即 execu- + -trix → executrix（女遗嘱执行人）。这是词尾替换的记法；历史上 executrix 是从晚期拉丁语整词借入的。

etymology.text: 中古英语借入晚期拉丁语 executrix，表示女性执行者。它与 executor 成对，词尾突出传统的女性身份。

etymology_story.zh: executrix 的历史形式来自晚期拉丁语，属于 executor 的女性对应称谓，其词根与“实行、完成”有关。英语自15世纪已有使用记录；传统女性词尾 -trix 标示性别，而 executor 也可作为不分性别的称谓，参见[《韦氏词典》](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/executrix)和[《柯林斯词典》](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/executrix)。
etymology_story.en: Executrix has its historical source in Late Latin as the feminine counterpart of executor, with a root associated with carrying something out. It is recorded in English from the fifteenth century; traditional -trix marks female gender, while executor also serves as a gender-neutral term, as documented by [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/executrix) and [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/executrix).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学习可对照 executor，将其末尾 -tor 替换为传统女性施事词尾 -trix，得到 executrix；这是词形对应分析，不是 execute 直接加 -trix。复数为 executrices 或 executrixes；相关词族包括 execute（执行）、execution（执行；实施；亦可指处决）、executor（遗嘱执行人）、executorship（遗嘱执行人职务）、executorial（遗嘱执行人的）、executory（尚待履行的），以及 executive（行政的；主管）和 executable（可执行的）。
morphology_enriched.en: For modern learning, compare executor and replace its final -tor with the traditional feminine agent ending -trix to obtain executrix; this is a correspondence between forms, not execute plus -trix. Plurals are executrices and executrixes; the related family includes execute, execution, executor, executorship, executorial, executory, executive, and executable, whose meanings extend beyond estate administration.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: executor（遗嘱执行人）可不分性别，是最直接的对应词；personal representative（遗产事务代表）范围更广，可包括遗嘱执行人和遗产管理人；administratrix（女遗产管理人）通常指由法院任命管理遗产的女性，不等同于遗嘱中指定的 executrix。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Executor is the direct gender-neutral counterpart; personal representative is broader and can include executors and administrators; administratrix traditionally denotes a female estate administrator appointed by a court, rather than an executor designated in a will.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: executor 负责执行遗嘱；把 -tor 换成传统女性词尾 -trix，就得到 executrix。
mnemonic_anchor.en: An executor carries out a will; replacing -tor with the traditional feminine ending -trix gives executrix.

usage_note: 常写 Franglais，也见小写 franglais；常带调侃或批评意味。本课指法语中夹杂英语，不泛指一切双语能力。

etymology_story.zh: Franglais 在20世纪从法语借入，由 français（法语）与 anglais（英语）拼合，英语使用记录至少可追溯至1952年。词形本身就体现了其所指的英法混合现象，参见[《韦氏词典》Franglais 词条](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/franglais)。
etymology_story.en: Franglais was borrowed from French in the twentieth century as a blend of français, French, and anglais, English, with English use recorded by 1952. Its blended form embodies the mixing that it names; see [Merriam-Webster's Franglais entry](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/franglais).

morphology_enriched.zh: français（法语，截取 fran-）＋ anglais（英语，截取 -glais）→ Franglais，属于截段拼合词，不是前缀加词根。通常为不可数名词，也写作 franglais；没有常用的规则派生词族，Frenglish（英法混合语）是相关的另一个拼合名称，并非其派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Français, shortened to fran-, + anglais, shortened to -glais, forms the blend Franglais; this is blending rather than prefixation. It is normally an uncountable noun and is also written franglais; it has no established productive derivative family, while Frenglish is a related alternative blend rather than a derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: anglicized French（英语化的法语）强调法语吸收英语词汇或表达；Frenglish（英法混合语）也是非正式名称，但使用范围不完全固定；code-mixing（语码混合）是适用于任意语言组合的语言学术语，范围更广，也更中性。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Anglicized French emphasizes English influence on French vocabulary or expression; Frenglish is another informal label whose scope varies; code-mixing is a broader, more neutral linguistic term applicable to any combination of languages.

mnemonic_anchor.en: The names français and anglais mix in the word, just as French and English mix in the speech.

etymology_story.zh: fusspot 由 fuss（过分计较；小题大做）和 pot 组合而成，后者在这里参与构成对人的诙谐称呼，并非实指容器。《韦氏词典》记载其英语首见年代为1921年，参见[该词条](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/fusspot)。
etymology_story.en: Fusspot combines fuss with pot, used here in a humorous label for a person rather than a literal container. Merriam-Webster dates its first known English use to 1921; see [its fusspot entry](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/fusspot).

morphology_enriched.zh: fuss（过分计较）＋ pot（构成人物诙谐称呼的成分）→ fusspot，是复合名词；复数为 fusspots。以 fuss 为核心的相关词族包括 fuss（名词／动词：大惊小怪；过分操心）、fussed／fussing（动词形式）、fussy（挑剔的）、fussier／fussiest（比较级／最高级）、fussily（挑剔地）、fussiness（挑剔）、unfussy（不挑剔的）和 fussbudget（爱计较的人）；这些并非都由 fusspot 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Fuss + pot, the latter contributing to a humorous person-label, forms the compound noun fusspot; its plural is fusspots. The related fuss family includes the noun and verb fuss, the verb forms fussed/fussing, fussy, fussier/fussiest, fussily, fussiness, unfussy, and fussbudget; these are not all derivatives of fusspot itself.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fussbudget（爱计较的人）意义最接近，尤常见于美式英语；nitpicker（吹毛求疵的人）侧重抓住细小错误不放；stickler（严格讲究某事的人）强调坚持规则或标准，有时带肯定意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fussbudget is the closest equivalent and is especially associated with American English; nitpicker emphasizes finding trivial faults; stickler emphasizes strict adherence to a rule or standard and can imply approval.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a pot full of fuss: a person overflowing with complaints and picky concerns; this is a memory image, not a historical account.

senses.meaning_zh: 动名词；英语中具有名词功能的动词-ing形式
senses.meaning_en: A verb form used as a noun, especially an English -ing form.
senses.english_definition: A gerund is a form of a verb that functions as a noun, such as swimming in the sentence 'Swimming is good exercise.'

etymology_story.zh: 英语于16世纪借入晚期拉丁语gerundium，其词根来自拉丁语gerere，意为“做、进行”。这个名称原用于拉丁语的一种动词性名词，后来也用于描述英语等语言中的类似形式。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Late Latin gerundium in the sixteenth century; its root comes from Latin gerere, meaning 'to do or carry on.' Originally the name of a Latin verbal noun, it was later applied to comparable forms in English and other languages.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中gerund是不可进一步作常规词缀分析的借入词；复数为gerunds。词族包括gerundial（动名词的）和gerundially（以动名词方式）；同源术语gerundive（动形词；动形词的）及gerundival（动形词的）与它相关，但动形词和动名词并非同一语法概念。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, gerund is a borrowed base without a productive internal affix breakdown; its plural is gerunds. Its family includes gerundial and gerundially; the related terms gerundive and gerundival share its historical root, but a gerundive and a gerund are distinct grammatical concepts.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: verbal noun（动词性名词）是较宽泛的相关术语，具体范围随语法体系而异；-ing noun（-ing形式名词）强调形式，可能包括普通派生名词；infinitive（不定式）也可作主语或宾语，但通常采用to do等形式，不能与gerund直接等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Verbal noun is a broader related term whose scope varies between grammatical frameworks; -ing noun emphasizes form and may include ordinary derived nouns; an infinitive can also function as a subject or object, but usually takes a form such as to do and is not equivalent to a gerund.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把“做某事”装进名词的位置：swim是“游泳”，Swimming is fun中的swimming就是动名词。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Put an action into a noun's position: swim names the action, while swimming in 'Swimming is fun' is a gerund.

etymology_story.en: Gharial entered English in the nineteenth century from Hindi ghaṛiyāl, the local name for the animal. The related English name gavial came through French gavial, a form arising from a mistaken rendering of the Indian name.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将gharial作为完整借入词使用，没有可用于常规构词分析的英语前后缀；复数为gharials。gharial-like（像恒河鳄的）是可临时构成的比较性形容词；gavial是相关异名，不是由gharial加词缀派生而来。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats gharial as a complete borrowed base, without an English prefix or suffix suitable for ordinary morphological analysis; its plural is gharials. Gharial-like is a freely formed comparative adjective; gavial is an alternative name, not an affixal derivative of gharial.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: gavial（恒河鳄）是同义异名；crocodilian（鳄类动物）是包含恒河鳄的上位词；false gharial（马来鳄）指另一种动物，虽然吻部也较细长，却不是恒河鳄的同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Gavial is an alternative name for the same animal; crocodilian is the broader category containing it; false gharial names a different species with a similarly slender snout and is not a synonym.

etymology_story.zh: gloxinia来自新拉丁语属名Gloxinia，该名称为纪念医生兼植物学家Benjamin Peter Gloxin而创。园艺中通常称为gloxinia的大岩桐后来被归入Sinningia属，但原有俗名保留了下来。
etymology_story.en: Gloxinia comes from the New Latin genus name Gloxinia, coined in honour of the physician and botanist Benjamin Peter Gloxin. The plant usually called gloxinia in horticulture was later placed in the genus Sinningia, but its familiar common name survived.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史命名结构为Gloxin（人姓）+ -ia（植物属名中常见的命名词尾）。现代普通名词gloxinia通常作为完整词基使用，复数为gloxinias；没有常用的固定派生词族，gloxinia-like（像大岩桐的）可按需构成。
morphology_enriched.en: Its historical naming structure is Gloxin, a surname, plus -ia, an ending commonly used in botanical genus names. The modern common noun gloxinia normally functions as a complete base, with the plural gloxinias; it has no established common derivative family, although gloxinia-like can be formed when needed.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: florist's gloxinia（园艺大岩桐）明确指常见的栽培观赏植物；Sinningia speciosa（大岩桐）是这一植物的学名，园艺品种由它选育而来；Gloxinia（大岩桐属）是仍然使用的另一个植物属名，不能与该学名互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Florist's gloxinia explicitly identifies the familiar cultivated ornamental; Sinningia speciosa is the scientific name of the species from which its cultivars were developed; Gloxinia is also the name of a separate botanical genus and is not interchangeable with that scientific name.

etymology_story.zh: greengage在18世纪由green（绿色）和姓氏Gage组成，传统上与将这种法国李树引入英国的Gage家族联系在一起。名称先指这种绿色果实，也用于指结这种果实的树。
etymology_story.en: Greengage was formed in the eighteenth century from green and the surname Gage, traditionally associated with the family that introduced this French plum to Britain. The name denotes the green fruit and also the tree that bears it.

morphology_enriched.zh: 复合结构为green（绿色）+ Gage（姓氏）；现代拼写连写并小写为greengage，复数为greengages。常见组合有greengage tree（绿李树）和greengage jam（绿李果酱）；没有常用的固定词缀派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: The compound consists of green plus Gage, a surname; its modern spelling is the closed, lowercase form greengage, with the plural greengages. Common combinations include greengage tree and greengage jam; there are no established common affixal derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: greengage plum（绿李）是更明确的同义表达；green plum（绿色李子）只描述颜色，也可能指尚未成熟的其他李子；plum（李子）是上位词，包含多种颜色和品种。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Greengage plum is an explicit equivalent; green plum merely describes colour and may refer to an unripe plum of another variety; plum is the broader term covering many colours and varieties.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: green记果皮，Gage记人姓：绿李成熟了也可以是绿色。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Green recalls the skin and Gage recalls the surname: a greengage can stay green when ripe.

usage_note: 指历史商人联盟时通常大写 Hanse；普通历史“行会”义也可小写。本课不指现代公司名称。

etymology_story.zh: Hanse属于日耳曼语词族，可与中古低地德语hanse及古高地德语hansa联系，早期表示“群体、团体”。在中世纪贸易语境中，它发展为商人联合组织的名称，并进一步成为汉萨同盟的称呼。
etymology_story.en: Hanse belongs to a Germanic word family represented by Middle Low German hanse and Old High German hansa, originally meaning a company or group. In medieval commerce it came to denote merchant associations and, more specifically, the Hanseatic League.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中Hanse是历史借入词，内部没有可自由拆分的英语词缀；泛指商人联盟时也写作hanse，复数为hanses。相关形式有Hansa（汉萨同盟的另一名称）和Hanseatic（汉萨同盟的）；Hanseatic是既有历史形容词，不宜把-atic当作可自由套用的现代英语后缀。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Hanse is a historical loanword without freely separable English affixes; the generic association sense can be written hanse, with the plural hanses. Related forms include Hansa, an alternative name, and Hanseatic, the established historical adjective; -atic should not be treated here as a freely productive modern English suffix.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Hansa（汉萨）是相关异名；Hanseatic League（汉萨同盟）明确指那个特定的北欧贸易联盟；merchant guild（商人行会）是一般组织名称，不一定属于汉萨同盟。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hansa is an alternative name; Hanseatic League explicitly identifies the particular northern European trading alliance; merchant guild is a general organizational term and does not necessarily imply membership of that alliance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“一群人”到“一群商人”，再到“商贸城市联盟”：沿着团体扩大的逻辑记忆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the expanding group: a company of people becomes a company of merchants, then an alliance of trading towns.

etymology_story.zh: Hedera 直接沿用拉丁语 hedera（常春藤），成为现代植物分类中的属名。它保留了原来的植物含义，并未经历明显的语义转变。
etymology_story.en: Hedera preserves Latin hedera, meaning 'ivy,' as a modern botanical genus name. Its meaning remains closely tied to the plant originally named by the Latin word.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，Hedera 是完整借入的属名，不宜拆成英语词根和词缀。相关专业词共享拉丁词干 heder-：hederaceous（常春藤的、似常春藤的）、hederin（常春藤皂苷类物质）、hederagenin（常春藤皂苷元）；这些是专业关联词，并非日常英语中可自由套用的派生模式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Hedera is a borrowed genus name rather than an English root-and-affix construction. Related technical vocabulary shares the Latin stem heder-: hederaceous ('relating to or resembling ivy'), hederin (an ivy saponin), and hederagenin (a sapogenin associated with ivy); these are specialized formations rather than a freely productive everyday word family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ivy 是常春藤类植物的普通名称；Hedera 是精确的科学属名；English ivy 通常特指 Hedera helix（洋常春藤），范围比整个属小。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ivy is the ordinary plant name, whereas Hedera identifies the botanical genus precisely. English ivy usually means the particular species Hedera helix, so it is narrower than the genus name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 Hedera 当作常春藤的拉丁文名牌：看见属名，就想到攀墙的常绿藤。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of Hedera as ivy's Latin nameplate: the scientific name points to the familiar evergreen climber.

senses.pos: v. 动词（古体、诗歌用语）
senses.meaning_zh: 名叫；被称为
senses.meaning_en: to be named or called
senses.english_definition: In old-fashioned poetry or storytelling, someone who is hight a particular name is called by that name.

senses.collocation_zh: 一位名叫……的骑士；名叫……

senses.sentence_zh: 在那个古老的故事里，这位骑士名叫埃德蒙。

etymology_story.zh: hight 经中古英语传承自古英语 hātan（称呼、命名、命令）及其历史屈折形式。它早期有更广的动词用法，后来主要以“名叫、被称为”的含义留在古体和诗歌语言中。
etymology_story.en: Hight comes through Middle English from Old English hātan, meaning 'to call, name, or command,' and its historical inflected forms. Its earlier verbal uses narrowed, and it survived chiefly in archaic and poetic language meaning 'named' or 'called.'

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中应把 hight 作为整体识记，不能分析为 high + -t，也没有常用的现代派生词族。历史相关词包括 behight（古体：许诺、命令等）；hight 的旧式屈折和相关词不应当作现代规则动词模式使用。
morphology_enriched.en: Treat hight as a whole historical form, not as high + -t; it has no common productive modern derivative family. Historical relatives include behight, an obsolete verb with meanings such as 'promise' and 'command'; these older forms do not provide a regular modern conjugation pattern.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: named 中性地说明姓名；called 可说明姓名、称呼或俗称；yclept 同样表示“名叫”，但也带明显的古体或戏谑色彩。hight 主要用于仿古叙事和诗歌。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Named states a name neutrally; called can introduce a name, familiar label, or nickname. Yclept also means 'called' but sounds archaic or deliberately playful, while hight belongs chiefly to archaizing narrative and poetry.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 古故事里的姓名标签：a knight hight Edmund，就是“名叫埃德蒙的骑士”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a name label in an old tale: a knight hight Edmund is a knight named Edmund.

etymology_story.zh: kyat 借自缅甸语，该名称在当地历史上既与重量单位有关，也用于货币。英语将它借入后，主要用来指缅甸的货币单位。
etymology_story.en: Kyat is borrowed from Burmese, where the name has historical connections with both a unit of weight and money. In English, it is used chiefly for Myanmar's monetary unit.

morphology_enriched.zh: kyat 是不可再按英语词缀拆分的借词；复数可用 kyats，计量金额时也常保留 kyat。它没有常用派生词；kyat-denominated（以缅元计价的）和 kyat-denominated assets（以缅元计价的资产）属于复合表达。
morphology_enriched.en: Kyat is a borrowed base with no English affixes to separate. Its plural may be kyats, while kyat also remains unchanged in monetary amounts; there are no common derivatives, but compounds include kyat-denominated and kyat-denominated assets.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Myanmar kyat 和 Burmese kyat 都可明确指缅元，区别主要在国家名称的选用；MMK 是其国际货币代码，而不是另一种货币名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Myanmar kyat and Burmese kyat identify the same currency, differing mainly in the country name used. MMK is its international currency code rather than a separate currency name.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Pair the country with its currency: Myanmar → kyat.

etymology_story.zh: 酒名 Marsala 来自意大利西西里岛的同名城市，是以产地命名产品的例子。颜色名随后由酒名引申而来，用于表示带棕调的酒红色。
etymology_story.en: The wine takes its name from Marsala, the Sicilian city associated with its production. The color term subsequently developed from the wine name to describe a brownish wine-red shade.

morphology_enriched.zh: Marsala 是完整借入的地名及其转用词，现代英语中没有可用的词根加词缀拆分，也没有常用派生词族。Marsala-flavoured/Marsala-flavored（用马沙拉酒调味的）和 Marsala-based（以马沙拉酒为基础的）是复合形容词；Marsala sauce 中的酒名作名词修饰语，不必另立形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Marsala is a borrowed place name extended to a wine and a color, with no useful modern English root-and-affix breakdown or common derivative family. Marsala-flavoured/Marsala-flavored and Marsala-based are compound adjectives; in Marsala sauce, the wine name functions as a noun modifier rather than requiring a separate adjective entry.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 酒义中，fortified wine（加强葡萄酒）是上位词；sherry（雪利酒）和 Madeira（马德拉酒）是其他加强葡萄酒，并非 Marsala 的同义名称。颜色义中，burgundy 通常更偏暗紫红，maroon 通常指深棕红，marsala 则强调带土棕调的酒红色；具体色域会因使用场景而异。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the wine, fortified wine is the broader category; sherry and Madeira are other fortified wines rather than interchangeable names for Marsala. For the color, burgundy usually suggests a darker purplish red, maroon a deep brownish red, and marsala an earthy wine red, although color boundaries vary by context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一条命名链：马尔萨拉城 → 当地的马沙拉酒 → 酒的棕红色。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the naming chain: Marsala the city → Marsala the wine → marsala the wine-inspired color.

etymology_story.zh: menhir 在19世纪经法语进入英语，由布列塔尼语表示“石头”的 men（也写作 maen）和表示“长的”的 hir 构成。字面上的“长石”成为考古学中竖立巨石的名称。
etymology_story.en: Menhir entered English through French in the nineteenth century, combining Breton men, also written maen, meaning 'stone,' with hir, meaning 'long.' This literal 'long stone' became an archaeological term for a large stone set upright.

morphology_enriched.zh: 从历史来源看，可分析为布列塔尼语 men/maen（石头）+ hir（长的）；从现代英语看，它是整体借词，不能把 men 当作 man 的复数来理解。常用复数为 menhirs，没有常用的现代英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Historically, the word combines Breton men/maen ('stone') + hir ('long'). In modern English it is a borrowed whole, and men is unrelated to the plural of man; the regular plural is menhirs, with no common modern derivative family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: standing stone 是最接近的通俗说法，强调石头被竖立起来；megalith 泛指史前大型石构中的巨石，不一定直立；monolith 强调单块大石或整体石构，也不限定史前年代。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Standing stone is the closest ordinary equivalent and emphasizes the upright position. Megalith covers large stones used in prehistoric structures without requiring them to stand upright, while monolith emphasizes a single large stone or stone structure and need not be prehistoric.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “石头 + 长的” → 一块被竖起来的史前长石。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Stone + long → picture a long prehistoric stone standing upright.

meaning: 使改用公制；实行公制化

pronunciation.note: 采用英式宽式音标，按词典音节和重音整理。

morphology.text: metric（公制的）+ -ate（使成为、使采用）→ metricate（使改用公制）。

etymology.text: 20世纪英语在 metric 后加动词后缀 -ate；metric 经法语 metrique 追溯到希腊语 metron（尺度）。想象把英里、磅的标示换成公里、千克。

usage_note: 常谈国家、行业、设备或计量标示改用公制；不等于只把数字四舍五入。

senses.meaning_zh: 使改用公制；实行公制化
senses.meaning_en: to convert to the metric system of measurement
senses.english_definition: If a country or industry metricates, or metricates its measurements, it changes to using the metric system.
senses.collocation_en: metricate an industry; metricate road signs
senses.collocation_zh: 使某行业改用公制；将道路标志上的计量单位改为公制
senses.sentence_en: The company metricated its production equipment to meet international requirements.

etymology_story.zh: 该词是20世纪英语在 metric（公制的）后加动词后缀 -ate 构成的，随公制化进程而使用。Metric 经法语 métrique 最终追溯到希腊语 metron，意为“尺度；计量”。
etymology_story.en: This twentieth-century English formation combines metric with the verb-forming suffix -ate and belongs to the vocabulary of conversion to metric measurement. Metric came through French métrique and ultimately derives from Greek metron, meaning 'measure'.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：metric（公制的）+ -ate（使采用某种体系）→ metricate。屈折形式：metricates、metricated、metricating；直接派生词：metrication（公制化）；相关词：metric（公制的）、metrify、metricize／metricise（改用公制）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: metric + -ate, a verb-forming suffix meaning to make or adopt. Inflected forms: metricates, metricated, metricating. Direct derivative: metrication, conversion to the metric system. Related forms include metric and the alternative verbs metrify and metricize/metricise.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: metrify、metricize／metricise 都表示“使改用公制”，与 metricate 的核心意义基本相同；convert to the metric system 是更透明、适用范围更广的表达。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Metrify and metricize/metricise have essentially the same meaning as metricate. Convert to the metric system is a more transparent expression that is readily understood outside specialist discussions.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: metric 是“公制的”，-ate 把它变成动作：把英里和磅换成公里和千克。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Metric names the system; -ate turns it into an action: replace miles and pounds with kilometres and kilograms.

meaning: 在潮汐河滩泥中搜寻物品的人

pronunciation.note: 采用英式宽式音标，按词典音节和重音整理。

forms: 可数名词；复数 mudlarks；相关活动名 mudlarking。
family: mudlarking 河滩寻物活动

morphology.text: mud（泥）+ lark（云雀）→ mudlark（在泥滩搜寻物品的人）；复合词带有鸟儿低头觅食般的形象。

etymology.text: 18世纪末英语把 mud（泥）与 lark（云雀）合成，用来称在河滩泥中捡拾东西的人。记忆时可以联想低头在泥中觅食的鸟儿。

usage_note: 本课指河滩寻物者，历史上有靠捡拾谋生的人，今天也可指业余寻物者；澳大利亚赛马等其他义项不在本课。

etymology_story.zh: Mudlark 由 mud（泥）与 lark（云雀）构成，18世纪末已用于称呼在河岸泥中拾取可用物品的人，后来也用于从事这种活动的爱好者。在澳大利亚英语中，它还成为鹊鹨的俗名，与这种鸟使用泥筑巢有关。
etymology_story.en: Mudlark combines mud and lark and was used by the late eighteenth century for people who scavenged useful objects from river mud; it later also came to describe recreational searchers. In Australian English, it additionally became a common name for the magpie-lark, a bird that builds with mud.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：mud（泥）+ lark（云雀）→ mudlark，为复合词；动词由名词零派生而来。词族：mudlarks（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、mudlarked（过去式／过去分词）、mudlarking（现在分词，也指泥滩寻物活动）、mudlarker（寻物者的另一种说法）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: mud + lark, a compound noun; the verb is formed by conversion without an added suffix. The family includes mudlarks, mudlarked, mudlarking, and mudlarker, an alternative name for a person who takes part. Mudlarking also functions as the name of the activity.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 拾物者义：scavenger 泛指寻找被丢弃或可利用物品的人；beachcomber 主要在海滩上搜寻漂流物；mudlark 特指在潮汐河岸泥滩上寻找。鸟名义：magpie-lark 是该鸟更明确的通名。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the person, scavenger is broader and suggests collecting discarded or useful material, while beachcomber usually refers to someone searching a seashore; mudlark specifically suggests tidal river mud. For the bird, magpie-lark is the more explicit common name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想象一只“云雀”低头在泥里找东西：人是在泥滩寻物，澳洲鸟则用泥筑巢。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a 'lark' busy in the mud: the human searches it for finds, while the Australian bird uses it to build a nest.

senses.meaning_en: food or substances that nourish the body, in formal usage
senses.english_definition: Nutriment is food or another substance that provides what a living thing needs to grow and stay alive.
senses.collocation_en: provide nutriment; absorb nutriment
senses.collocation_zh: 提供养分；吸收养分

senses.meaning_zh: 精神滋养；促进思想或情感发展的事物，属文学用语
senses.meaning_en: something that sustains or develops the mind or spirit, in literary usage
senses.english_definition: If something provides intellectual or spiritual nutriment, it helps your mind or spirit develop.
senses.collocation_en: intellectual nutriment; spiritual nutriment

etymology_story.zh: Nutriment 在中古英语时期进入英语，来源于法语 nutriment 和拉丁语 nutrimentum，后者由 nutrire（滋养；喂养）构成。其基本义是维持生命的养分，后来也比喻滋养思想或精神的事物。
etymology_story.en: Nutriment entered Middle English from French nutriment and Latin nutrimentum, a noun derived from nutrire, meaning 'to nourish or feed'. Its meaning extended from physical nourishment to things that sustain the mind or spirit.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可辨认结构：nutri-（滋养）+ -ment（名词成分），但该词是整体借入的拉丁语来源词。屈折形式：nutriments（指不同种类的营养物时）；直接派生词：nutrimental（滋养的，罕见）；同源词族：nutrient（营养物；营养的）、nutrition（营养）、nutritional（营养方面的）、nutritionally（在营养方面）、nutritious（富有营养的）、nutritiously（富有营养地）、nutritive（有营养作用的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Recognizable structure: nutri-, relating to nourishment, + the noun element -ment, although the word was borrowed as a whole. Nutriments is a plural used for distinct nourishing substances; nutrimental is a rare direct adjective. The related Latin-root family includes nutrient, nutrition, nutritional, nutritionally, nutritious, nutritiously, and nutritive.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: nourishment 最常指食物带来的滋养，也可表示精神滋养；nutrient 通常指蛋白质、维生素等某一种具体营养成分；sustenance 强调维持生命所需的食物或支持。Nutriment 较正式，常着眼于提供滋养的物质。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nourishment commonly refers to the food or support that nourishes someone; nutrient usually identifies a particular component such as a vitamin or protein; sustenance emphasizes what keeps someone alive or supported. Nutriment is more formal and often focuses on nourishing material.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 nutri- 与 nutrition 联系起来：nutriment 就是身体或心灵“吃进去的滋养”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect nutri- with nutrition: nutriment is the nourishing material that feeds the body—or, figuratively, the mind.

senses.sentence_en: Ethylene is an olefin used to make polyethylene.

senses.meaning_en: a synthetic textile fiber made from a polyolefin such as polypropylene
senses.english_definition: Olefin is a synthetic fiber made from a polyolefin and used in products such as carpets and upholstery.

senses.collocation_zh: 聚烯烃纤维；聚烯烃纤维地毯
senses.sentence_en: The outdoor cushions are covered in fabric made from olefin.

etymology_story.zh: Olefin 与法语 oléfiant（生油的）有关；这一旧称用于乙烯，因为它与氯反应会生成油状液体。词中的油义成分最终来自拉丁语 oleum，后来该名称扩展为一类烃的名称，并用于相关聚合物纤维。
etymology_story.en: Olefin is connected with French oléfiant, meaning 'oil-forming', an old description of ethylene because it forms an oily liquid when it reacts with chlorine. The oil element ultimately comes from Latin oleum; the name later broadened to a class of hydrocarbons and was also applied to related polymer fibers.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜把 olefin 作为完整词干，不把 -fin 当作有独立意义的常用后缀。词族：olefins（复数）、olefinic（烯烃的；含烯键的）、polyolefin（聚烯烃）、monoolefin（单烯烃）、diolefin（二烯烃）、olefination（烯化；形成碳碳双键的反应）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, olefin is best treated as a complete stem; -fin is not an independently productive suffix here. The family includes olefins, olefinic, polyolefin, monoolefin, diolefin, and olefination, a reaction that introduces a carbon–carbon double bond.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 化学义：alkene 是最接近的常用对应词，但严格分类时通常指非环状烯烃；unsaturated hydrocarbon（不饱和烃）范围更大，也包括炔烃。纤维义：polyolefin fiber（聚烯烃纤维）更明确；polypropylene fiber（聚丙烯纤维）只指其中一种材料。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: In chemistry, alkene is the closest common equivalent, although strict classifications generally use it for acyclic compounds; unsaturated hydrocarbon is broader and also includes alkynes. For textiles, polyolefin fiber is more explicit, while polypropylene fiber names one particular material within that category.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“生油的气体”记到乙烯，再抓住碳碳双键；双键聚合后，还能成为纤维。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with the old 'oil-forming gas', ethylene, and remember its carbon–carbon double bond; polymerizing such compounds can also produce textile fibers.

senses.meaning_zh: 少尿；尿液生成量或排出量异常减少

senses.english_definition: Oliguria is a medical condition in which a person produces or passes an unusually small amount of urine.
senses.collocation_en: develop oliguria; persistent oliguria
senses.collocation_zh: 出现少尿；持续性少尿
senses.sentence_en: The nurse reported persistent oliguria to the doctor.

etymology_story.zh: Oliguria 是19世纪形成的医学术语，由希腊语来源的 oligo-（少）和 -uria（尿液或排尿状况）组合而成。它将“少量”这一概念限定在尿液生成或排出的数量上。
etymology_story.en: Oliguria is a nineteenth-century medical formation combining Greek-derived oligo-, meaning 'little or few', with -uria, referring to urine or a urinary condition. It applies the idea of a small quantity specifically to urine production or output.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：olig(o)-（少）+ -uria（尿液或排尿状况）→ oliguria；组合时连接元音 o 在元音开头的 -uria 前省去。直接派生词：oliguric（少尿的）；同类构词：anuria（无尿）、polyuria（多尿），二者是使用相同后缀的相关术语，并非 oliguria 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: olig(o)-, meaning little or few, + -uria, a urinary condition; the combining vowel o is omitted before the vowel-initial element -uria. The direct adjective is oliguric. Anuria and polyuria are related formations sharing the suffix, rather than derivatives of oliguria.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: reduced urine output（尿量减少）是最接近的通俗解释，但不一定表示已达到临床上的少尿程度；anuria（无尿）表示几乎没有或完全没有尿液；urinary retention（尿潴留）强调膀胱不能正常排空，与尿液生成减少不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Reduced urine output is the closest plain-language explanation, though it does not necessarily imply clinically defined oliguria. Anuria means virtually no urine or none at all. Urinary retention concerns failure to empty the bladder and is distinct from reduced urine production.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: oligo- 是“少”，-uria 关联“尿”：少的是尿量，不是排尿次数。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Oligo- means little and -uria concerns urine: think low urine volume, rather than simply infrequent trips to the toilet.

etymology_story.zh: Palazzi 是意大利语 palazzo 的复数形式，英语借入时保留了这一复数。Palazzo 源自拉丁语 palatium；该词原指罗马的帕拉蒂尼山，因皇帝在此建造居所而逐渐具有“宫殿”之义。
etymology_story.en: Palazzi is the Italian plural of palazzo, retained as a plural in English. Palazzo comes from Latin palatium, originally the name of Rome's Palatine Hill, which became associated with palaces because emperors established their residences there.

morphology_enriched.zh: 意大利语屈折结构：palazz-（词干）+ -i（复数词尾），对应单数 palazzo 的词尾 -o。英语词形包括 palazzo（单数）、palazzi 和 palazzos（两种复数）；palace“宫殿”和 palatial“宫殿般的”是历史同源词，并非由 palazzi 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Italian inflection: palazz- (stem) + -i (plural ending), replacing the singular ending -o in palazzo. English forms are palazzo (singular) and palazzi or palazzos (plural); palace and palatial are historical relatives, not direct derivatives of palazzi.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Palaces“宫殿”通常更突出王室或统治者的居所；mansions“豪宅”泛指大型豪华住宅；palazzi 带有明确的意大利建筑与历史文化色彩，也可指城市中的贵族府邸。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Palaces more strongly suggests residences of royalty or rulers; mansions means large, luxurious homes generally. Palazzi specifically evokes Italian architecture and history, including aristocratic urban residences.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一座 palazzo，多座 palazzi：把意大利语复数词尾 -i 想成一排宏伟府邸。
mnemonic_anchor.en: One palazzo, several palazzi: let the Italian plural ending -i bring a row of grand residences to mind.

etymology_story.zh: Parian 最终源自希腊语中表示“帕罗斯岛的”的词形，经拉丁语 Parius 等形式进入英语。帕罗斯岛以白色雕刻用大理石闻名，十九世纪一种模仿这种大理石外观的无釉瓷也因此得名。
etymology_story.en: Parian ultimately comes from the Greek adjective meaning 'of Paros,' through forms including Latin Parius. Because Paros was famous for its white sculptural marble, the name was also given in the nineteenth century to an unglazed porcelain resembling that stone.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可按地名派生理解：Par(os)（帕罗斯岛，词干作 Par-）+ -ian（表示地域归属或居民）→ Parian。相关词形为 Paros、Parian 和居民名词复数 Parians；常见组合包括 Parian marble“帕罗斯大理石”和 Parian ware“帕里安瓷器”，没有常用的进一步派生动词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: A useful modern analysis is Par(os), with the stem Par-, + -ian, indicating geographical association or an inhabitant, giving Parian. Related forms are Paros, Parian, and the plural inhabitant noun Parians; established combinations include Parian marble and Parian ware, with no usual further verb or adverb derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Greek“希腊的”范围更广，不能特指帕罗斯岛；marble“ 大理石”是天然石材，Parian 的陶瓷义指仿其外观的材料；biscuit porcelain“素烧无釉瓷”是更宽泛的类别，Parian 特别强调仿白色大理石的质感。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Greek is geographically broader and does not specify Paros. Marble is natural stone, whereas the ceramic sense of Parian denotes an imitation material. Biscuit porcelain is the broader category of unglazed porcelain; Parian particularly suggests a white, marble-like appearance.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Paros → white marble → marble-like porcelain: one island-to-stone-to-ceramic chain connects the meanings.

etymology_story.zh: Poteen 借自爱尔兰语 poitín，字面意思是“小罐”，由 pota“罐”加指小后缀 -ín 构成。名称从小型蒸馏器具转指其中酿出的烈酒，并与爱尔兰的私酿传统联系起来。
etymology_story.en: Poteen comes from Irish poitín, literally 'little pot,' formed from pota 'pot' and the diminutive suffix -ín. The name shifted from the small distilling vessel to the strong spirit produced in it and became associated with Irish illicit distilling.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为整体借词使用，不宜拆成英语词根和后缀；源语言结构为 pota“罐”+ -ín“指小后缀”→ poitín。相关拼写包括 poteen、potheen 和 poitín；这些主要是同一词的拼写形式，没有常用的标准派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, poteen is a whole-word borrowing rather than an English root-and-affix formation; its source-language structure is pota 'pot' + the diminutive suffix -ín → poitín. Related spellings include poteen, potheen, and poitín; these are chiefly spelling forms of the same word, with no common standard derivative family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Moonshine“私酿烈酒”通常突出非法蒸馏，尤其让人联想到美国；hooch“烈酒、私酿酒”是宽泛的非正式说法；poteen 特指爱尔兰传统烈酒，名称本身并不意味着每一瓶都属于非法产品。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Moonshine usually emphasizes illicit distillation and particularly evokes the United States; hooch is a broad informal term for strong or illicit alcohol. Poteen identifies the Irish tradition specifically, and the name does not mean that every bottle is illegally produced.

etymology_story.zh: Prithee 是早期现代英语中 pray thee“请求你”的缩合形式，也常被还原为完整表达 I pray thee。随着 thee 退出日常标准英语，prithee 也主要保留在历史戏剧、文学及刻意仿古或诙谐的表达中。
etymology_story.en: Prithee arose in Early Modern English as a contraction of pray thee, also understood through the fuller expression I pray thee. As thee disappeared from everyday standard English, prithee survived mainly in historical drama, literature, and deliberately archaic or humorous speech.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史缩合结构为 pray“请求”+ thee“你，宾格”→ prithee；现代英语中是固定整体，没有常用屈折或直接派生形式。源词 pray 的常用词族包括 prays、prayed、praying、prayer“祈祷；祷词”、prayerful“虔诚祈祷的”、prayerfully“虔诚祈祷地”和 prayerfulness“虔诚祈祷的状态”；副词与感叹词标签反映其相近的请求功能。
morphology_enriched.en: The historical contraction is pray 'request' + thee 'you, object form' → prithee; in modern English it is a fixed expression with no usual inflections or direct derivatives. The source verb pray has the common family prays, prayed, praying, prayer, prayerful, prayerfully, and prayerfulness; the adverb and interjection labels describe closely related requesting functions.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Please“请”是现代日常请求用语；pray“请问、请”用于请求时带正式或古雅色彩；I beg you“我求你”通常语气更恳切。Prithee 的显著特点是古语或戏剧语体，并不一定表示强烈哀求。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Please is the ordinary modern request marker; pray sounds formal or archaic when used in requests; I beg you usually expresses stronger pleading. Prithee chiefly signals an archaic or theatrical register and does not necessarily indicate intense desperation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 prithee 展开成 pray thee：“请求你”自然就是“请”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Expand prithee into pray thee: 'I ask you' naturally becomes 'please.'
