etymology_story.zh: 这是现代医学构词，将源于希腊语 aēr（空气）的 aero- 与 digestive（消化的）结合。该词用一个形容词概括呼吸道与消化道及其相互关联的功能。
etymology_story.en: This modern medical formation combines aero-, from Greek aēr meaning air, with digestive. It provides a single adjective for the respiratory and digestive passages and their connected functions.

morphology_enriched.zh: aero-（空气；此处涉及呼吸）+ digestive（消化的）→ aerodigestive；digestive 可分析为 digest + -ive。相关词族包括 digest（消化；摘要）、digests、digested、digesting、digestion（消化）、digestive（消化的；助消化剂）、digestively（在消化方面）、digestible（可消化的）、digestibility（可消化性）、indigestible（难消化的）、indigestion（消化不良）、digester（消化器；消化罐）。Aerodigestive 本身没有常用的独立名词或动词形式。
morphology_enriched.en: aero-, meaning air and here referring to breathing, + digestive → aerodigestive; digestive can be analyzed as digest + -ive. Related family members include digest, digests, digested, digesting, digestion, digestive, digestively, digestible, digestibility, indigestible, indigestion, and digester. Aerodigestive itself has no commonly used independent noun or verb form.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Respiratory and digestive（呼吸与消化的）是直接释义；respiratory（呼吸的）只涉及呼吸系统；gastrointestinal（胃肠的）涉及胃肠道，不能单独表达本词同时涵盖呼吸道与消化道的含义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Respiratory and digestive is a direct paraphrase; respiratory covers breathing alone; gastrointestinal concerns the stomach and intestines and does not express the combined respiratory and digestive scope.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: aero- 管空气，digestive 管食物：空气与食物两条通路一起看。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Aero- points to air and digestive to food: consider both pathways together.

etymology_story.zh: Altazimuth 是十九世纪的科学合成词，由 altitude（高度角）的缩略部分与 azimuth（方位角）构成，英语用例可追溯至 1851 年。名称直接指出仪器转动或测量所依据的两个地平坐标。
etymology_story.en: Altazimuth is a nineteenth-century scientific formation combining a shortened form of altitude with azimuth, with English use recorded from 1851. Its name identifies the two horizon-based coordinates used to direct or measure with the instrument.

morphology_enriched.zh: alt-（altitude 的截短形式，高度角）+ azimuth（方位角）→ altazimuth。屈折形式：altazimuths；派生词：altazimuth + -al → altazimuthal（地平式的；与高度角和方位角有关的）。Alt-az 是常见缩略形式；altazimuth mount 中的 altazimuth 常按名词作定语处理。
morphology_enriched.en: alt-, a clipping of altitude, + azimuth → altazimuth. Inflection: altazimuths; derivative: altazimuth + -al → altazimuthal, meaning relating to altitude and azimuth or to this mounting arrangement. Alt-az is a common shortened form; altazimuth in altazimuth mount is commonly treated as an attributive noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Alt-az instrument（地平式仪器）是较简略的近义表达；theodolite（经纬仪）也测水平角和垂直角，但通常用于测量，不能全面替换；equatorial telescope（赤道式望远镜）采用不同的轴系，是对照术语而非同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Alt-az instrument is a shortened near-equivalent; a theodolite also measures horizontal and vertical angles but usually serves surveying and is not a general substitute; an equatorial telescope uses a different axis arrangement and is a contrasting term rather than a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: altitude 看高低，azimuth 看方向：上下加左右，就是地平式。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Altitude gives height and azimuth gives direction: up–down plus left–right makes altazimuth.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借入德语 Androstendion，并按英语化学命名形式拼写；该名称见于 Ružička 和 Wettstein 于 1935 年发表的化学论文。德语名称以 Androsteron（雄酮）的名称为基础，结合表示双键的 -en 和表示两个酮基的 -dion，形成结构性名称。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed German Androstendion and adapted its spelling to English chemical terminology; the name appeared in a 1935 chemistry paper by Ružička and Wettstein. The German formation drew on Androsteron, adding -en for a double bond and -dion for two ketone groups.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代名称可按 androstene（雄烯类结构名称）+ dione（二酮）理解，其中 dione = di-（二）+ -one（酮）；常用拼写保留 androstene 末尾的 e。相关化学词族包括 androstane（雄甾烷）、androstene（雄烯）、androstenediol（雄烯二醇）、androsterone（雄酮）；它们是相关但不同的化合物名称，不是同一物质的屈折形式。Androstenedione 通常作不可数名词，没有常用的普通英语动词或形容词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern name can be understood as androstene + dione, with dione = di-, meaning two, + -one, indicating a ketone; the conventional spelling retains the final e of androstene. Related chemical family names include androstane, androstene, androstenediol, and androsterone; these name related but different compounds rather than inflections of the same substance. Androstenedione is normally uncountable and has no common everyday verb or adjective derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Androst-4-ene-3,17-dione（雄甾-4-烯-3,17-二酮）是明确标示结构位置的系统名称；4-androstene-3,17-dione 是同一物质的另一种命名形式；testosterone（睾酮）是相关的下游激素，不是同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Androst-4-ene-3,17-dione is a systematic name specifying structural positions; 4-androstene-3,17-dione is another naming form for the same substance; testosterone is a related downstream hormone, not a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住雄甾骨架、烯键和二酮：雄烯二酮是合成睾酮与雌激素的前体。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember an androstane framework, a double bond, and two ketones: a precursor used to make testosterone and estrogens.

etymology_story.zh: 该词形成于十九世纪后期，由希腊语来源的 apo-（离开、免于）与 chromatic（颜色的）构成，用于命名比普通消色差透镜校正更充分的光学系统。[词源与释义](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/apochromatic)
etymology_story.en: Formed in the late nineteenth century from Greek-derived apo-, meaning away from or free from, and chromatic, meaning relating to color, the word named optical systems with more complete correction than ordinary achromatic lenses. [Origin and definition](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/apochromatic)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：apo-（免于）+ chromatic（颜色的）；chromatic 内含历史词干 chromat-（颜色）与 -ic（形容词后缀）。主要词族：apochromat（复消色差透镜或物镜）、apochromatism（复消色差性；复消色差校正）、apochromatically（以复消色差方式）。chromatic 是相关基础词，achromatic（消色差的）是相关术语。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: apo- (free from) + chromatic (relating to color); chromatic contains the historical stem chromat- (color) and adjectival -ic. Principal family members are apochromat (an apochromatic lens or objective), apochromatism (the property or correction), and apochromatically (in an apochromatic manner). Chromatic is the related base word, and achromatic is a related technical term.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: achromatic（消色差的）通常指较基本的色差校正，不能与 apochromatic 完全互换；color-corrected（经色差校正的）含义更宽，并不保证达到复消色差标准。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Achromatic usually denotes a more basic level of chromatic correction and is not interchangeable with apochromatic; color-corrected is broader and does not guarantee apochromatic performance.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: apo- 表示“去除”，chromat- 表示“颜色”：去掉成像边缘的杂色。

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自希腊语 apophatikos（否定的）的拉丁化形式，关联 apophasis（否认、否定），其更早构件表示“离开”和“说”。英语中既用于通过否定获得认识，也用于声称不提某事却将其带出的修辞。[词源说明](https://www.etymonline.com/word/apophatic)
etymology_story.en: The word comes from a Latinized form of Greek apophatikos, meaning negative, related to apophasis, meaning denial or negation, with earlier elements meaning away and speak. English uses it both for knowledge through negation and for rhetoric that introduces something while professing not to mention it. [Etymology](https://www.etymonline.com/word/apophatic)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜把 apophatic 看作借入的整体词干；历史结构可提示为 apo-（离开）+ phat-（说）+ -ic（形容词后缀），不能按现代英语直接理解为 apo- + phatic（寒暄交际的）。主要词族：apophatically（以否定方式）、apophaticism（否定式思想；否定神学立场）；apophasis（否定；假意略而不谈）是同源名词，并非简单去掉 -ic 所得。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, apophatic is best treated as a borrowed stem. Its historical structure can be represented as apo- (away) + phat- (speak) + -ic (adjectival), rather than a modern combination of apo- and phatic (serving social communication). Principal family members include apophatically and apophaticism; apophasis is a historically related noun, not a form produced simply by removing -ic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: negative（否定式的）含义更宽，在神学语境中可与 apophatic 接近；via negativa（否定之路）是相关名词术语，指通过排除不适当的描述来认识上帝的方法；paraliptic（假意省略的）主要对应修辞义，强调以声称省略来突出内容。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Negative is broader but can approximate apophatic in theology; via negativa is a related noun phrase naming the method of approaching God by rejecting inadequate descriptions; paraliptic corresponds chiefly to the rhetorical sense, highlighting a subject through professed omission.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用“不是什么”逼近所指；修辞中则用“不提”来提起。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Approach the subject through what it is not; in rhetoric, mention it by saying you will not.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：bar-（重量；组合形式 baro- 在元音前省去 o）+ -iatric（医疗的）。主要词族：bariatrics（肥胖症治疗学，形式以 -s 结尾但作学科名时通常用单数动词）、bariatrician（肥胖症诊疗医生）；bariatric surgeon（减重外科医生）是常用短语，不是单词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: bar- (weight, from the combining form baro- with o omitted before a vowel) + -iatric (relating to medical treatment). Principal family members are bariatrics, the medical specialty, normally taking a singular verb despite final -s, and bariatrician, a physician specializing in obesity treatment. synonyms_and_nuances.en: Weight-loss is broader and can describe nonmedical activities; anti-obesity emphasizes preventing or treating obesity and often modifies drugs or interventions; obesity-related indicates a connection with obesity without necessarily implying treatment or adapted equipment.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由希腊语来源的 bio-（生命、生物）与 region（区域）构成，《韦氏词典》将目前已知的最早用例列为 1945 年。它把区域的划分依据放在地形与生态联系上。[词史与释义](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bioregion)
etymology_story.en: The word combines Greek-derived bio-, meaning life, with region; Merriam-Webster dates its earliest known use to 1945. It identifies regions through their terrain and ecological connections. [Word history and definition](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bioregion)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：bio-（生命、生物）+ region（区域）。主要词族：bioregional（生物区域的）、bioregionalism（生物区域主义，强调依照地方生态条件组织生活与社会）、bioregionalist（生物区域主义者；生物区域主义的）、bioregionally（按生物区域；在生物区域层面）；复数为 bioregions。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: bio- (life) + region. Principal family members are bioregional, bioregionalism (an approach to social life grounded in local ecological conditions), bioregionalist (a supporter, or relating to that approach), and bioregionally. The plural is bioregions.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ecoregion（生态区）常用于具有相似生态系统的区域分类；biogeographic region（生物地理区）更强调生物分布及其地理和历史背景。两者与 bioregion 有重叠，但具体边界和尺度取决于所采用的分类体系。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ecoregion often belongs to a classification of areas with similar ecosystems; biogeographic region places more emphasis on species distributions and their geographic and historical context. Both overlap with bioregion, but their boundaries and scales depend on the classification used.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: bio- 加 region：让山水与生物来划区域。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bio- plus region: let landscapes and living things define the area.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 blood（血）与 root（根）合成，名称指向其根部及地下组织中血色的汁液。《韦氏词典》将该植物名目前已知的最早用例列为 1724 年。[词史与释义](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bloodroot)
etymology_story.en: A compound of blood and root, the name refers to the blood-colored sap associated with the plant's roots and underground tissues. Merriam-Webster dates the earliest known use of this plant name to 1724. [Word history and definition](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/bloodroot)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：blood（血）+ root（根），属于名词加名词的合成词，整体作植物名。可数用法的复数为 bloodroots；泛指这种植物或成片植株时也常用 bloodroot。没有常用的标准后缀派生词；bloodroot flower 和 bloodroot extract 中的 bloodroot 是名词作前置修饰语，不构成独立的常用形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: blood + root, a noun–noun compound functioning as a plant name. The countable plural is bloodroots, while bloodroot also commonly refers to the species or plants collectively. There are no common standard suffix-derived forms; in bloodroot flower and bloodroot extract, bloodroot is an attributive noun rather than a separate commonly used adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sanguinaria（血根草）是同一植物的另一名称，也见于药材语境；red puccoon（红普库恩草）是传统俗名；redroot（红根草）也可指该植物，但还用于其他植物，歧义较大。需要精确鉴定时使用学名 Sanguinaria canadensis。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sanguinaria is another name for the same plant and also occurs in medicinal-material contexts; red puccoon is a traditional common name; redroot can refer to this plant but also names other plants and is more ambiguous. Use Sanguinaria canadensis for precise identification.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由英语 blue（蓝色）和 stem（茎）合成，名称来自某些此类禾草的茎、茎基部或叶片呈现的蓝绿色。它逐渐成为多个相关或外形相似的禾草种类的俗名，并非单一物种的专名。

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：blue（蓝色的）＋stem（茎）→ bluestem，属于复合名词。复数为 bluestems；没有常用的直接派生词。big bluestem、little bluestem 是植物俗名短语，不是派生词。

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 近义或相关词：prairie grass（草原禾草）范围更广；big bluestem（大须芒草）和 little bluestem（小须芒草）指具体种类。三者都不能在所有语境中与 bluestem 完全互换。

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 bobble（轻轻地上下或来回晃动）和 head（头）合成，以头部摇晃的特点为这种玩偶命名。它后来也广泛用于体育明星、名人和虚构角色造型的收藏玩偶。
etymology_story.en: The word combines bobble, meaning to move with small repeated bobs, and head, naming the toy after its moving head. It also became widely used for collectible figures depicting athletes, celebrities, and fictional characters.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：bobble（晃动）＋head（头）→ bobblehead，属于复合名词；复数为 bobbleheads。基础动词的词形包括 bobbles、bobbled、bobbling；bobblehead doll 中的 bobblehead 是名词作前置修饰语，不构成独立的常用形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: bobble + head → bobblehead, a compound noun; its plural is bobbleheads. Forms of the base verb include bobbles, bobbled, and bobbling. In bobblehead doll, bobblehead is an attributive noun rather than a separate common adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 近义词：bobblehead doll（摇头娃娃）是较完整的称呼；nodder（点头玩偶）是较简短的收藏界用语；wobbler（摇摆玩偶）更强调摇摆动作，也可指其他会晃动的物件。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bobblehead doll is the fuller name; nodder is a shorter collectors' term; wobbler emphasizes the wobbling movement and can also refer to other objects that wobble.

etymology_story.zh: 英语解剖学借用了拉丁语 brachialis，原义为“臂部的”，源自 brachium（臂），后者借自希腊语。该形式原本是修饰“肌肉”的形容词，在英语中成为肱肌的名词名称。
etymology_story.en: Anatomical English borrowed Latin brachialis, meaning 'of the arm,' from brachium, 'arm,' ultimately borrowed from Greek. Originally an adjective describing a muscle, the form became the English noun naming the brachialis muscle.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史构词：brachi-（臂）＋拉丁语形容词后缀 -alis（……的）→ brachialis；现代英语通常把它作为完整的解剖学借词使用。复数为 brachiales；同根相关词包括 brachium（臂；复数 brachia）、brachial（臂的）和 brachioradialis（肱桡肌），这些并非都直接派生自 brachialis。
morphology_enriched.en: Historical structure: brachi- 'arm' + the Latin adjective suffix -alis 'relating to' → brachialis; modern English normally treats it as a complete anatomical loanword. Its plural is brachiales. Related forms include brachium, plural brachia, brachial, and brachioradialis; these are not all direct derivatives of brachialis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 同义名称：brachialis muscle（肱肌）是完整称呼；musculus brachialis 是拉丁语解剖名称；brachialis anticus 是较旧的名称。biceps（肱二头肌）是另一块肌肉，不能作为同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Brachialis muscle is the full English name; musculus brachialis is the Latin anatomical name; brachialis anticus is an older designation. The biceps is a different muscle and is not a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: brachi- 表示“臂”：记住藏在肱二头肌下面、负责屈肘的肱肌。

etymology_story.zh: 该词缩自较早的英语名称 cat-a-mountain，意思是“山中的猫”。这个旧称曾用于不同的野生猫科动物，在北美用法中尤其与美洲狮联系起来。
etymology_story.en: The word is a shortened form of the older English name cat-a-mountain, meaning a cat of the mountains. That older name was applied to different wild cats, while North American usage became especially associated with the cougar.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常把 catamount 作为整体词使用；历史上可追溯为 cat-a-mountain → catamount。中间的 a 不是现代英语中可自由构词的前缀，mount 也不宜据此分析为独立的现代派生成分。复数为 catamounts；没有常用的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats catamount as a whole word; historically, cat-a-mountain was shortened to catamount. The medial a is not a productive modern prefix, and mount should not be treated here as an independent modern derivational element. The plural is catamounts; there are no common direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 近义词：cougar（美洲狮）、puma（美洲狮）和 mountain lion（山狮）都指同一物种；catamount 更具地域或传统色彩，而且在某些地区所指范围更广。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cougar, puma, and mountain lion name the same species. Catamount has a more regional or traditional flavor and can refer more broadly to other wild cats in some areas.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把旧称 cat-a-mountain 缩起来：山中的大猫 → catamount。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Compress cat-a-mountain: a big wild cat of the mountains becomes a catamount.

etymology_story.zh: 英语从法语借入 chocolatier，该词由 chocolat（巧克力）加上表示从业者的后缀 -ier 构成。它原本指制作或销售巧克力的人，英语中也可指从事这类业务的企业。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed French chocolatier, formed from chocolat, 'chocolate,' and the occupational suffix -ier. It names someone who makes or sells chocolate and can also refer to a business engaged in that work.

morphology_enriched.zh: 借词内部结构：法语 chocolat（巧克力）＋-ier（从业者）→ chocolatier；现代英语通常整体借用，复数为 chocolatiers。同源相关词包括 chocolate（巧克力）、chocolaty／chocolatey（巧克力味的）和另一个法语借词 chocolaterie（巧克力店或制作坊）；它们并非都由英语 chocolatier 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Internal loanword structure: French chocolat 'chocolate' + -ier 'a person engaged in an occupation' → chocolatier. English normally borrows the whole form; its plural is chocolatiers. Related words include chocolate, chocolaty/chocolatey, and the separate French loan chocolaterie, a chocolate shop or workshop; these are not all direct derivatives of English chocolatier.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 近义词：chocolate maker（巧克力制作者）范围较广，在行业语境中常指从可可豆或可可原料制作巧克力的人；confectioner（糖果制作商）还制作其他糖果；chocolate retailer（巧克力零售商）强调销售，不一定负责制作。chocolatier 常强调把巧克力制成夹心巧克力等成品的技艺。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chocolate maker is broader and, in industry usage, often refers to someone who makes chocolate from cacao beans or cocoa ingredients; a confectioner also makes other sweets; a chocolate retailer emphasizes selling and need not make the products. Chocolatier often emphasizes the craft of turning chocolate into finished confections.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: chocolat 是巧克力，-ier 是从业者：以巧克力为手艺的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Chocolat means chocolate; -ier marks a worker: someone whose craft is chocolate.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自意大利语 consigliere，意为“顾问”，其基础词 consiglio（建议、商议）可追溯至拉丁语 consilium。英语中的用法尤其与黑手党顾问有关，后来也比喻政治或商业领袖身边的亲信智囊。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Italian consigliere, meaning 'adviser', based on consiglio ('advice' or 'consultation'), ultimately from Latin consilium. Its English use is especially associated with Mafia advisers and has extended figuratively to trusted advisers in politics and business.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 consigliere 作为整体借词，不按英语前后缀拆分；在意大利语内部，可分析为与 consiglio（建议）相关的词干加表示身份或职业的 -iere。常见复数为 consiglieri，也可见英语化复数 consiglieres；无常用英语派生动词、形容词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, consigliere is a whole-word borrowing rather than a formation from English affixes; within Italian, it contains a stem related to consiglio ('advice') and the occupational or personal suffix -iere. The usual plural is consiglieri, with the anglicized consigli eres also occurring as consiglieres; there are no common derived English verbs, adjectives, or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: adviser（顾问）最中性、范围最广；counselor（顾问、参谋）强调提供指导或审慎意见；right-hand man（得力助手）强调协助与执行。consigliere 则突出与权势人物的亲密关系和幕后影响力，并常带黑手党联想。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Adviser is the broadest, most neutral term; counselor emphasizes guidance or considered advice; right-hand man emphasizes practical assistance and execution. Consigliere suggests intimate access to a powerful person and influence behind the scenes, often with Mafia associations.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“建议”记到“顾问”：站在首领身旁、低声出主意的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect 'advice' with 'adviser': the trusted person beside the boss, quietly shaping decisions.

etymology_story.en: Crawdad arose in regional American English as an alteration of crawfish and is recorded from the nineteenth century. Crawfish belongs to the same historical word group as crayfish, whose earlier source referred to the crustacean rather than to a fish.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，crawdad 通常作为一个整体词处理，末尾的 dad 不表示“爸爸”。常见形式有复数 crawdads，以及同义变体 crawdaddy、复数 crawdaddies；crawdaddy 可按 crawdad + -y 理解，拼写时双写末尾 d。crawfish 和 crayfish 是相关名称，不是由 crawdad 派生的词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats crawdad as a single lexical unit; its ending does not mean 'father'. Common forms include the plural crawdads and the synonymous variant crawdaddy, plural crawdaddies; crawdaddy can be analyzed as crawdad + -y, with the final d doubled. Crawfish and crayfish are related names rather than derivatives of crawdad.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: crayfish（淡水螯虾）是广泛使用的标准名称；crawfish（小龙虾）尤其常见于美国南部及相关饮食语境；crawdaddy（小龙虾）更具口语和地区色彩。这些名称通常指同类动物，并不稳定地区分不同物种。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Crayfish is a widely used standard name; crawfish is especially associated with the American South and its food traditions; crawdaddy is more colloquial and regional. These names generally refer to the same kind of animal rather than consistently identifying different species.

etymology_story.zh: 英语从西班牙语借入 cumbia，用来称呼起源于哥伦比亚的音乐和舞蹈。这一传统在非洲与美洲原住民文化等影响下形成，后来传播到拉丁美洲各地，发展出多种地方风格。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed cumbia from Spanish as the name of a musical and dance tradition originating in Colombia. Shaped by African and Indigenous American influences among others, the tradition spread across Latin America and developed numerous regional styles.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中，cumbia 是不可再作实用拆分的整体借词，可作不可数名词表示音乐或舞蹈类型，也可用复数 cumbias 表示多首舞曲或多个作品。相关西班牙语词有 cumbiero、cumbiera，指昆比亚音乐的表演者或爱好者，也可作形容词；它们不是常规英语派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, cumbia is an unanalyzed whole-word borrowing: it can be uncountable for the musical or dance style, while cumbias can refer to individual pieces. Related Spanish forms include cumbiero and cumbiera for performers or enthusiasts, also used adjectivally; these are not regular English derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Latin dance music（拉丁舞曲）、Colombian dance music（哥伦比亚舞曲）和 tropical music（热带音乐）都是相关的上位表达，范围均比 cumbia 更广。cumbia 是特定音乐与舞蹈传统的名称，不能与 salsa（萨尔萨）或 merengue（梅伦格）直接互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Latin dance music, Colombian dance music, and tropical music are related umbrella expressions, each broader than cumbia. Cumbia names a particular musical and dance tradition and is not interchangeable with salsa or merengue.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一个词，两个相连画面：哥伦比亚的节奏响起，人们随之起舞。
mnemonic_anchor.en: One name, two connected images: a Colombian rhythm starts, and people dance to it.

etymology_story.en: Dermatologic belongs to modern medical vocabulary built from Greek elements and corresponds to dermatology, the study and treatment of skin disease. Dermat- comes from the stem of Greek derma ('skin'), while -logy denotes a field of study.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词关系为 dermatology（皮肤病学）去掉词尾 -y，再加 -ic，形成 dermatologic；词素结构可表示为 dermat-（皮肤）+ -o-（连接元音）+ -log-（研究、学科）+ -ic（……的）。常见词族包括 dermatology（皮肤病学）、dermatologist（皮肤科医生）、dermatologic、dermatological（皮肤科的）和 dermatologically（从皮肤科角度）；同根相关词有 dermatitis（皮炎）、dermatosis（皮肤病）和 dermal（皮肤的）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern relationship is dermatology minus final -y plus -ic, producing dermatologic; its elements are dermat- ('skin') + linking -o- + -log- ('study') + -ic ('relating to'). The common family includes dermatology, dermatologist, dermatologic, dermatological, and dermatologically; related formations from the skin root include dermatitis, dermatosis, and dermal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dermatological（皮肤科的）与 dermatologic 基本同义；cutaneous（皮肤的）偏重皮肤这一组织及其病变或反应；dermal（真皮的、皮肤的）在解剖学语境中可特指真皮层。dermatologic 更强调皮肤疾病及相关医学领域。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dermatological is essentially synonymous with dermatologic; cutaneous concerns the skin as a tissue and its conditions or reactions; dermal can refer specifically to the dermis in anatomical contexts. Dermatologic more strongly emphasizes skin disease and the medical specialty.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: dermat- 是“皮肤”，-log- 是“研究”：研究和诊治皮肤问题的，就是 dermatologic。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Dermat- means 'skin' and -log- means 'study': dermatologic concerns the study and medical care of skin.

etymology_story.en: Dumbass is an American English compound recorded in the twentieth century, combining dumb in the sense 'stupid' with ass as an insulting term for a fool. It can insult a person or appear before a noun to disparage an idea or action.

morphology_enriched.zh: dumb（愚蠢的）+ ass（傻瓜，侮辱性称呼）→ dumbass，可作名词，也可作形容词。常见相关形式包括名词复数 dumbasses、连字符拼写 dumb-ass，以及形容词变体 dumb-assed；没有常用的专属派生副词。
morphology_enriched.en: Dumb ('stupid') + ass ('fool', used insultingly) forms dumbass, which functions as both a noun and an adjective. Common related forms include the noun plural dumbasses, the hyphenated spelling dumb-ass, and the adjective variant dumb-assed; there is no common dedicated derived adverb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 名词 idiot（白痴、蠢货）直接贬低人的判断力，fool（傻瓜）更可侧重一时的愚蠢或轻信；形容词 stupid（愚蠢的）可修饰人、想法或行为。dumbass 比这些普通表达更粗俗，常带恼怒，也可用于自嘲。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: As nouns, idiot directly attacks someone's judgment, while fool can emphasize a foolish action or gullibility; the adjective stupid can describe people, ideas, or actions. Dumbass is more vulgar than these ordinary alternatives and often conveys irritation, though it can also be self-deprecating.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Combine dumb's 'stupid' meaning with the insulting use of ass: a stupid person, or a stupid idea or action.

The modern drink may contain no alcohol. [Word history](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/eggnog), [origin of nog](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/nog)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：egg（鸡蛋）+ nog（旧饮料名）→ eggnog，属于名词复合词。通常为不可数名词；eggnogs 可指多份或多种蛋奶饮，nog 可作简称；eggnog-flavored“蛋奶饮风味的”属于进一步构成的复合形容词。没有常用的直接派生动词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: egg + nog, an old beverage name, forms the compound noun eggnog. It is normally uncountable; eggnogs can mean servings or varieties, and nog is a shortened form. Eggnog-flavored is a further compound adjective. There are no common directly derived verbs or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: nog：eggnog 的非正式简称，在历史语境中也可指旧式麦芽酒；posset：相关的传统奶饮，旧式配方常用酒使热奶凝结，并非蛋奶饮的完全同义词；flip：常含鸡蛋、糖和酒的调酒，不一定含奶。三者之中，只有现代饮料义的 nog 通常可直接替换 eggnog。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nog is an informal shortening of eggnog, although historically it also names an ale. Posset is a related traditional milk drink, historically often curdled with alcohol. A flip is a mixed drink commonly containing egg, sugar, and alcohol, but not necessarily milk. Only nog in its modern beverage sense is normally interchangeable with eggnog.

etymology_story.zh: emerita 借自拉丁语 emeritus 的阴性形式；emeritus 原来形容已服满役期的人，来自表示“完成服役”的动词。英语将这一概念用于退休后仍保留荣誉头衔的人，emerita 则专用于女性。[拉丁语来源](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/emeritus)、[形容词与名词用法](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/emerita)
etymology_story.en: Emerita is borrowed from the feminine form of Latin emeritus, originally describing someone who had completed a term of service. English extended the idea to retirement with an honorary title, with emerita specifically referring to a woman. [Latin background](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/emeritus), [adjective and noun uses](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/emerita)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中应把 emerita 作为整体借词掌握，而不是按英语词缀自由拆造。历史结构可提示为 ē-（出、完成）+ merit-（服务、赢得）+ -a（拉丁语阴性单数词尾）。相关形式：emeritae（阴性复数）、emeritus（传统阳性单数，也可不分性别使用）、emeriti（传统阳性或混合群体复数）；merit“功绩”与其同源，并非由 emerita 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, emerita is a borrowed whole word rather than a freely assembled English formation. Its historical structure can be represented as ē- meaning out or completion, merit- relating to service or earning, and -a marking the Latin feminine singular. Related forms are emeritae, the feminine plural; emeritus, traditionally masculine singular and also used without specifying gender; and emeriti, traditionally masculine or mixed plural. Merit is a cognate, not a derivative of emerita.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: retired“退休的”只说明退出常规工作，不保证保留头衔；honorary“名誉的”表示荣誉身份，不一定经过退休；emeritus 与 emerita 表示相同的荣休地位，但 emerita 明确指女性，emeritus 的性别适用范围依机构惯例而定。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Retired describes withdrawal from regular employment without necessarily retaining a title. Honorary describes an honour-based position that need not follow retirement. Emeritus denotes the same retirement status, but emerita explicitly identifies a woman, while the gender scope of emeritus depends on institutional practice.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 服务已完成，荣誉仍保留；-a 提醒这是传统的女性形式。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Service completed, honour retained; final -a marks the traditional feminine form.

morphology.text: es-（estrane 的缩短形式，指雌甾烷骨架） + tri-（三） + -ol（醇） → estriol（雌三醇）。这是缩合命名，estrane 缩短时与 tri- 共用 tr 音段，不把 estr- 与 tri- 重复拼接；tri- 提示三个羟基。

etymology.text: 这是二十世纪英语化学命名形成的词，由 estrane 的缩短形式、tri- 与 -ol 组成；“三”与“醇”直接提示中文名雌三醇。

usage_note: 雌激素的一种。estriol 与 estradiol 名称相近，但不是同一种物质。

senses.meaning_zh: 雌三醇，一种含三个羟基的天然雌激素
senses.meaning_en: A naturally occurring estrogen with three hydroxyl groups.
senses.english_definition: Estriol is a natural estrogen hormone that has three hydroxyl groups and is produced in particularly large amounts during pregnancy.
senses.collocation_en: unconjugated estriol; estriol levels
senses.collocation_zh: 非结合型雌三醇；雌三醇水平

etymology_story.zh: estriol 是二十世纪形成的化学名称，由 estrane“雌甾烷”的缩略形式、tri-“三”和 -ol“醇”缩合而来。“三”指分子中的三个羟基，直接对应中文名“雌三醇”。[词源与读音参考](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/estriol)
etymology_story.en: Estriol is a twentieth-century chemical name formed by contracting estrane with tri-, meaning three, and -ol, the alcohol suffix. The reference to three hydroxyl groups is also reflected in the Chinese name 雌三醇. [Etymology and pronunciation](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/estriol)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词提示：estrane（雌甾烷）的缩略形式 + tri-（三）+ -ol（醇）→ estriol；这是缩合命名，不能机械拼成 estrtriol。英式异体为 oestriol，常用缩写为 E3。没有常用的直接派生动词或形容词；estriol sulfate“硫酸雌三醇”和 unconjugated estriol“非结合型雌三醇”为术语短语。estradiol“雌二醇”、estrone“雌酮”和 estrogen“雌激素”为相关化学词，并非 estriol 的派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation guide: a shortened form of estrane + tri-, three, + -ol, alcohol, contracts to estriol; mechanically producing estrtriol would be incorrect. Oestriol is a British spelling variant, and E3 is a common abbreviation. There are no common directly derived verbs or adjectives. Estriol sulfate and unconjugated estriol are technical phrases. Estradiol, estrone, and estrogen are related chemical terms, not derivatives of estriol.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: oestriol：同一物质的英式拼写，与 estriol 没有意义差别；E3：同一物质的专业缩写；estrogen“雌激素”：上位类别名称，雌三醇只是其中一种，不能在要求精确指称时互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Oestriol is a British spelling of the same substance, with no difference in meaning. E3 is its technical abbreviation. Estrogen is the broader hormone category of which estriol is one member, so it is not interchangeable when a specific substance is intended.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: tri 是“三”，-ol 是“醇”：三个羟基，记住雌三醇。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Tri means three and -ol signals alcohol: three hydroxyl groups anchor estriol.

morphology.text: extra-（向外）+ net（网络）→ extranet（向指定外部用户开放的网络）。

etymology.text: 英语把 extra- 和 net 组合成计算机术语。extra- 可追溯到拉丁语 extrā“在外”；net 经中古英语来自古英语 nett。想象公司网络向合作伙伴开了一扇需要通行许可的窗。

usage_note: 常用于企业合作、客户服务等场景。外部人员仍须授权；并非人人可访问的公共网站。

senses.meaning_zh: 外联网，允许获授权的客户、供应商等外部用户访问的专用网络
senses.meaning_en: A private network accessible to authorized external users.
senses.english_definition: An extranet is a private computer network that allows selected people outside an organization, such as customers or suppliers, to access information or services.
senses.collocation_en: secure extranet; extranet access
senses.collocation_zh: 安全外联网；外联网访问权限
senses.sentence_en: Suppliers can check their orders through the company's secure extranet.
senses.sentence_zh: 供应商可以通过该公司的安全外联网查询自己的订单。

etymology_story.zh: extranet 在二十世纪九十年代作为网络术语出现，按 intranet“内联网”等词的模式，由 extra-“在外”与 net“网络”构成。它指把组织的部分网络资源开放给指定外部用户，同时保留访问限制。[词义与词史参考](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/extranet)
etymology_story.en: Extranet emerged as a networking term in the 1990s, combining extra-, outside, with net on the model of terms such as intranet. It describes extending access to selected outsiders while retaining access controls. [Meaning and word history](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/extranet)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：extra-（外部）+ net（网络）→ extranet。复数为 extranets；extranet-based“基于外联网的”和 extranet-enabled“支持外联网的”是进一步形成的复合修饰语。没有常用的直接派生动词或副词；intranet“内联网”和 internet“互联网”为相关构词，不是 extranet 的派生词。extranet access 中的 extranet 是名词作定语。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: extra-, outside, + net, network, produces extranet. The plural is extranets; extranet-based and extranet-enabled are further compound modifiers. There are no common directly derived verbs or adverbs. Intranet and internet are related formations, not derivatives of extranet. In extranet access, extranet functions as an attributive noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: partner portal“合作伙伴门户”：强调外部伙伴使用的入口或界面，可能依托外联网；intranet“内联网”：通常面向组织内部人员；internet“互联网”：全球互联网络。后两者是辨析用的相关词，并非外联网的同义词；关键区别在于服务对象和访问权限。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Partner portal emphasizes the entry point or interface used by external partners and may run on an extranet. An intranet normally serves an organization's internal users. The internet is the global interconnected network. The latter two are comparison terms rather than synonyms; intended users and access permissions distinguish them.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: extra-“向外”+ net“网络”：内部资源向外开门，但只有获准的人能进入。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Extra means outside: the network opens a door to outsiders who have permission.

meaning: 带辱骂意味地称极端女权主义的

morphology.text: feminist（女权主义者）+ Nazi（纳粹）→ feminazi（带攻击性的混成词）；两词发生截短拼接。

etymology.text: 这是现代英语把 feminist 与 Nazi 拼接出的词，1990年代经美国广播话语传播开来。它把政治观点与纳粹作攻击性类比，记忆时要连同强烈贬义一起记。

senses.meaning_zh: “女权纳粹”，辱骂性地称说话者认为极端或专横的女权主义者
senses.meaning_en: An offensive label for a feminist whom the speaker portrays as extreme or authoritarian.
senses.english_definition: If someone calls a person a feminazi, they are offensively suggesting that the person's feminism is extreme, intolerant, or authoritarian.
senses.collocation_en: call someone a feminazi; label someone a feminazi
senses.collocation_zh: 辱称某人为“女权纳粹”；给某人贴上“女权纳粹”的标签

senses.sentence_zh: 她批评带有性别歧视的广告后，一些评论者便用“女权纳粹”辱骂她。

etymology_story.zh: feminazi 是 feminist“女权主义者”与 Nazi“纳粹”的混成词，二十世纪八十年代已有记录，后来在美国政治广播话语中广泛传播。它通过与纳粹作攻击性类比来贬损对象，是辱骂标签，而非中性的思想分类。[构词与早期记录](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/feminazi)、[贬义及冒犯性标注](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/feminazi)
etymology_story.en: Feminazi blends feminist with Nazi and is recorded from the 1980s, later spreading widely through American political broadcasting. Its hostile Nazi comparison makes it an insulting label rather than a neutral ideological category. [Formation and early record](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/feminazi), [offensive usage label](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/feminazi)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：femi-（从 feminist 截取）+ Nazi（纳粹）→ feminazi，属于截短混成词；复数为 feminazis。feminist“女权主义者；女权主义的”和 feminism“女权主义”属于来源词的词族，并非由 feminazi 派生。该词通常为名词；feminazi rhetoric 一类结构可分析为名词作定语，不据此另立常用形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: femi-, clipped from feminist, + Nazi produces the blend feminazi; its plural is feminazis. Feminist and feminism belong to the source word's family and are not derivatives of feminazi. The word is normally a noun; constructions such as feminazi rhetoric can be analyzed as attributive noun use rather than evidence of a separate common adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: radical feminist“激进女权主义者”：可指特定理论立场，不等于极端或专横；militant feminist“采取强硬行动的女权主义者”：强调斗争方式或态度，语气可能带批评；feminist“女权主义者”：基本为中性名称。这些词均不包含 feminazi 所带的纳粹类比，不能当作语气相同的替换词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Radical feminist can identify a particular theoretical position without implying authoritarianism. Militant feminist emphasizes confrontational methods or attitudes and may sound critical. Feminist is a basically neutral designation. None contains the Nazi comparison carried by feminazi, so they are not equivalent in tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: feminist + Nazi：把“女权”硬贴上“纳粹”标签，构词本身就提示强烈辱骂性。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Feminist + Nazi: the forced Nazi comparison makes the insulting force visible in the word itself.

morphology.text: fiddle（小提琴）+ head（头部）→ fiddlehead；卷曲的蕨芽像小提琴顶部的涡卷。

etymology.text: 英语将 fiddle 和 head 合成此词，既指琴头涡卷，也用来称形状相似的蕨类嫩芽。本课记蕨芽义：看见卷起的嫩叶，就想到小提琴头。

usage_note: 本课指卷曲的蕨芽，不指琴头装饰。植物识别与是否可食不能单凭这个名称判断。

etymology_story.zh: fiddlehead 由 fiddle“小提琴”和 head“头部”复合而成。蕨类嫩叶的卷曲形状类似小提琴琴头的涡卷，因此得名。
etymology_story.en: Fiddlehead combines fiddle, meaning a violin, with head. The young fern frond received this name because its coil resembles the scroll at the head of a violin.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：fiddle（小提琴）+ head（头部）→ fiddlehead，属于名词复合词。复数为 fiddleheads；常见扩展为 fiddlehead fern（卷芽蕨）和 fiddlehead greens（作为蔬菜的蕨芽），没有常用的独立派生动词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: fiddle + head → fiddlehead, a compound noun. The plural is fiddleheads; established extensions include fiddlehead fern and fiddlehead greens. There are no commonly used derived verbs or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: furled fern frond（尚未展开的蕨叶）是准确的描述性近义表达；crozier（拳卷状嫩叶）是较专业的植物学用语；fern shoot（蕨类嫩梢）的范围更宽，不一定强调卷曲的叶端。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Furled fern frond is a precise descriptive equivalent; crozier is a more technical botanical term for a coiled young frond; fern shoot is broader and does not necessarily emphasize the curled leaf tip.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 蕨芽卷成“小提琴头”：fiddle + head。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a fern tip curled like a fiddle’s head.

senses.meaning_zh: 跛行的；腿脚不便的（美式非正式用语，形容残障人士时常具有冒犯性）
senses.meaning_en: Walking with a limp or having difficulty walking; informal US usage, often offensive when applied to a disabled person.
senses.english_definition: If someone is described as gimpy, they walk with a limp or have difficulty walking, but this description can be offensive.
senses.collocation_en: a gimpy walk; a gimpy gait

senses.sentence_en: The word 'gimpy' can be offensive when used to describe someone who walks with a limp.
senses.sentence_zh: 用 gimpy 形容走路一瘸一拐的人，可能会冒犯对方。

senses.meaning_zh: 因受伤而活动不便的，尤指腿、膝或脚踝（美式非正式用语，也可能冒犯）
senses.meaning_en: Affected by an injury, especially to a leg, knee, or ankle; informal US usage, sometimes offensive.
senses.english_definition: A gimpy leg, knee, or ankle is injured and does not move or work normally.
senses.collocation_en: a gimpy knee; a gimpy ankle
senses.collocation_zh: 受伤而活动不便的膝盖；受伤而活动不便的脚踝
senses.sentence_en: The sports report said that the player was competing on a gimpy ankle.
senses.sentence_zh: 体育报道说，这名运动员脚踝有伤，仍在参加比赛。

etymology_story.zh: gimpy 由表示“跛行”或用作对跛行者贬称的 gimp 加上形容词后缀 -y 构成；这一义项的 gimp 更早的来源并不确定。该词也用于体育报道中，形容受伤后活动不便的运动员或肢体。
etymology_story.en: Gimpy was formed by adding the adjective suffix -y to gimp, meaning a limp or, offensively, a person who limps; the earlier origin of this sense of gimp is uncertain. It is also used in sports reporting for an injured athlete or limb.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：gimp（跛行；对跛行者的贬称）+ -y（具有某特征的）→ gimpy。比较级 gimpier，最高级 gimpiest；同族词有 gimp（名词或非正式动词“跛行”）、gimps、gimped、gimping。这一词族须保留其非正式及可能冒犯的语用标记。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: gimp + -y, meaning 'having a particular characteristic,' → gimpy. The comparative is gimpier and the superlative gimpiest. The family includes the noun and informal verb gimp, with gimps, gimped, and gimping. Informal and potentially offensive usage labels apply to this word family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: limping（跛行的）直接描述走路表现，通常更中性；injured（受伤的）说明受伤状态，不一定涉及行走；lame（跛的）与身体义接近，但用于形容人时也可能冒犯。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Limping directly describes the way someone walks and is generally more neutral; injured identifies physical injury without necessarily implying difficulty walking; lame overlaps in its physical meaning but can also be offensive when applied to a person.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: gimp“跛行”加 -y：带着跛行或伤病特征；同时记住语气可能冒犯。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Gimp + -y means 'having a limp or injury'; remember the potentially offensive tone too.

morphology.text: hag + berry → hagberry → hackberry（英语旧词形的变体）；不要按 hack“砍”来猜树名。

etymology.text: hackberry 是英语 hagberry 的词形变体，后来用于朴属树木及其果实。把它作为一个树名整体记，比从现代 hack“砍”联想更稳妥。

usage_note: 本课指朴属树木，常见于树木识别、园艺和城市绿化语境；不是任意长浆果的树。

senses.meaning_zh: 朴属树木或灌木；尤指北美朴树
senses.meaning_en: A tree or shrub of the genus Celtis, especially a North American hackberry tree.
senses.english_definition: A hackberry is a tree or shrub that belongs to the genus Celtis and produces small, round fruits.
senses.collocation_en: a hackberry tree; common hackberry
senses.collocation_zh: 一棵朴树；美洲朴
senses.sentence_en: A mature hackberry shades the back of the garden.

senses.meaning_zh: 朴树果实；朴果
senses.meaning_en: The small, round fruit of a hackberry tree.
senses.english_definition: A hackberry is also one of the small fruits produced by a hackberry tree.
senses.collocation_en: ripe hackberries; dried hackberries

senses.sentence_en: The cabinetmaker selected hackberry for the drawer sides.

etymology_story.zh: hackberry 是较早词形 hagberry 的变体，hagberry 原指一种与稠李相似的樱属植物或其果实。这个名称后来用于朴属树木，并可指其果实和木材，与现代动词 hack“砍”没有直接的构词关系。
etymology_story.en: Hackberry is an alteration of the older word hagberry, which named a cherry resembling chokecherry or its fruit. The name came to designate Celtis trees and, by extension, their fruit and wood; it is not a transparent formation from the modern verb hack.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代结构：hack-（在此树名中已不透明的历史成分）+ berry（浆果；俗称的小果实）→ hackberry，不宜解释为“砍 + 浆果”。复数 hackberries；常见组合有 hackberry tree（朴树）、hackberry fruit（朴果）和 hackberry wood（朴木），没有常用的独立派生动词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: hack-, a historically opaque element in this plant name, + berry → hackberry; do not interpret it as 'cut + berry.' The plural is hackberries. Common combinations include hackberry tree, hackberry fruit, and hackberry wood; there are no commonly used derived verbs or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: nettle tree（朴树）是朴属树木的另一俗名；sugarberry（糖朴）通常指特定种 Celtis laevigata，范围较窄；common hackberry（美洲朴）通常指 Celtis occidentalis，也不是整个朴属的完全同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nettle tree is an alternative common name for Celtis trees; sugarberry usually refers specifically to Celtis laevigata; common hackberry usually identifies Celtis occidentalis. The latter two names are narrower than hackberry used for the genus generally.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 hackberry 整体记作“结小果的朴树”：一名可连到树、果、木。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor hackberry to one fruit-bearing tree: the name can refer to its tree, fruit, or wood.

meaning: 听觉过敏；对声音异常敏感

pronunciation.note: 采用所列词典英语词条的这一读音；注意重音符号的位置。

forms: 通常为不可数名词。
family: hyperacusic 听觉过敏的；acoustic 与声音有关的。

morphology.text: hyper-（过度）+ -acusis（听觉状态）→ hyperacusis（听觉过敏）。

etymology.text: 这是用希腊语来源的医学构词成分形成的词：hyper- 表示超过通常程度，-acusis 涉及听觉。抓住“声音感受过强”的画面来记。

relations.meaning: 厌声症；对特定声音的强烈负面反应

usage_note: 医学名词，指声音耐受异常，不等于听力更优秀，也不等于听力丧失。本课用于理解术语。

senses.meaning_zh: 听觉过敏；对日常声音异常敏感或难以耐受
senses.meaning_en: Abnormally increased sensitivity or reduced tolerance to everyday sounds.
senses.english_definition: Hyperacusis is a condition in which everyday sounds seem unusually loud, uncomfortable, or painful.
senses.collocation_en: severe hyperacusis; patients with hyperacusis
senses.collocation_zh: 严重的听觉过敏；听觉过敏患者
senses.sentence_en: Her hyperacusis made ordinary office sounds difficult to tolerate.
senses.sentence_zh: 她患有听觉过敏，连办公室里寻常的声音也难以忍受。

etymology_story.zh: hyperacusis 是由希腊语来源的医学构词成分构成的术语：hyper- 表示“过度”，akousis 表示“听觉”，与 akouein“听”相关。该词表示声音敏感或耐受方面的异常，并不意味着听力比常人更好。
etymology_story.en: Hyperacusis is a medical formation using Greek-derived hyper-, meaning 'excessive,' and akousis, meaning 'hearing,' related to akouein, 'to hear.' It denotes abnormal sound sensitivity or tolerance rather than superior hearing ability.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代医学构词：hyper-（过度）+ -acusis（听觉状态）→ hyperacusis，通常作不可数名词。专业形容词为 hyperacusic（听觉过敏的）；相关构词有 hypoacusis（听力减退）和 presbycusis（老年性听力损失），后二者是共享听觉词素的相关词，并非由 hyperacusis 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern medical formation: hyper-, 'excessive,' + -acusis, 'hearing condition,' → hyperacusis, usually an uncountable noun. The specialist adjective is hyperacusic. Related formations include hypoacusis, reduced hearing, and presbycusis, age-related hearing loss; these share hearing-related morphology but are not derivatives of hyperacusis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sound hypersensitivity（声音过敏）是接近的描述性表达；auditory hypersensitivity（听觉敏感性增高）强调听觉系统的过度敏感；decreased sound tolerance（声音耐受性降低）范围更宽，可涵盖其他声音不耐受现象，不能在所有语境中与 hyperacusis 完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sound hypersensitivity is a close descriptive equivalent; auditory hypersensitivity emphasizes excessive sensitivity within hearing; decreased sound tolerance is broader and may cover other forms of sound intolerance, so it is not interchangeable with hyperacusis in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hyper- 过度 + -acusis 听觉：普通声音也显得过响。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hyper- means excessive; -acusis concerns hearing: ordinary sounds feel too loud.

meaning: 裤腿内侧缝；沿该缝测量的长度

morphology.text: in-（在内侧）+ seam（接缝）→ inseam（裤腿内侧缝）。

etymology.text: 英语以 in- 和 seam 组合成词。两部分都沿用古英语词汇：in 表示在内，sēam 表示接缝。想象从裤裆沿裤腿内侧向下量的那条线。

usage_note: 裁缝和服装尺码中常见。inseam length 从裤裆沿裤腿内侧量至裤脚，不是腰围。名词首音节重读。

senses.meaning_zh: 裤腿内侧缝
senses.meaning_en: The seam along the inside of a trouser leg.

senses.meaning_zh: 裤内长；从裤裆沿裤腿内侧缝量至裤脚的长度
senses.meaning_en: The length of a trouser leg measured along its inside seam from crotch to hem.
senses.english_definition: The inseam of a pair of trousers is also the distance from the crotch to the bottom of the leg, measured along the inside seam.
senses.collocation_en: a 32-inch inseam; measure the inseam
senses.collocation_zh: 32 英寸的裤内长；测量裤内长
senses.sentence_en: These jeans have a 32-inch inseam.

etymology_story.zh: inseam 由表示“内侧”的 in 与 seam“接缝”构成，两部分分别延续了古英语 in 和 sēam。词义由裤腿内侧的接缝，进一步扩展为沿这条接缝测得的长度。
etymology_story.en: Inseam combines in, meaning 'inside,' with seam, continuing Old English in and sēam respectively. Its meaning extends from the inner seam of a trouser leg to the length measured along that seam.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：in（内侧）+ seam（接缝）→ inseam，是透明的复合名词；这里的 in 不表示否定。复数为 inseams；相关词族有 seam（接缝；缝合）、seamed（有缝的）、seaming（缝合）和 seamless（无缝的），这些由 seam 构成，并非都由 inseam 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: in, 'inside,' + seam → inseam, a transparent compound noun; in does not express negation here. The plural is inseams. Related family members include seam, seamed, seaming, and seamless; these are formations from seam rather than direct derivatives of inseam.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: inside leg seam（裤腿内侧缝）明确对应接缝本身；inside leg measurement（裤内长尺寸）对应长度义；leg length（裤腿长度）更宽泛，未说明从内侧还是外侧测量。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Inside leg seam specifically names the stitching; inside leg measurement corresponds to the length sense; leg length is broader and does not specify whether the measurement follows the inside or outside of the leg.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: in 是内侧，seam 是接缝：先认裤内缝，再沿缝量裤内长。
mnemonic_anchor.en: In + seam: find the inside seam, then measure along it for the inseam length.
